author: Former Resident 370468
review_text: Moving into Avana Tempe was a terrible experience right from the beginning. Attempting to work with the office to move in was extremely frustrating - everything from getting answers to my questions about paperwork they sent me, actually obtaining needed documents, and even paying the move in fees was difficult as the staff either does not want to help or does not have the proper training to do so. The leasing manager at the time, Michael, was especially difficult to work with during my move in. Upon move in, the apartment was in terrible condition, practically uninhabitable. It was so bad, that I actually went right back to the office after seeing the apartment to ask if it was ready for move in. I was really surprised at the terrible condition, especially since my original move in date was pushed back by Avana Tempe and I had to pay for an extra month at my previous apartment. When I was finally able to move in, the apartment was extremely dirty. My new home had dirt, stains, black marks and grease splatters on the walls and floors all throughout, but the worst part was what appeared to be large stains from leaking on the living room ceiling. When I spoke to Carol at the office, she stated that the cleaning crew had been in and she did offer to send them back. I declined because if the cleaners had already been and they thought the condition of the apartment was acceptable, they would not do a better job if they came a second time so I had to clean the apartment myself. I was later told that maintenance came and looked at the leaking and stains on the ceiling, but I was not there when they entered, no notice of entry was left and nothing was done to improve the appearance or fix the issue at all so I am unsure if anyone even looked at this. I was also told that there was no mold, but I am also not sure if that is accurate. During my 7 months (March - October) at Avana Tempe, I submitted several maintenance requests, none of which were ever fully resolved in a timely manner and some of which were never resolved at all. - I submitted two requests for my kitchen light to be fixed as it would not turn on unless I flipped the switch up and down for several minutes or if I flipped the switch and left it on, it would come on hours later. Maintenance did come out on the first request, because I received a notice of entry, but whatever fix they implemented lasted about a week and then the same issue began again. I had to submit a second request before it was actually fixed. I was only made aware that maintenance had been in my home due to the light being fixed - no notice of entry was left. - I submitted one request for my garbage disposal as it just stopped working altogether. Maintenance came out and again, whatever they did lasted a couple of weeks and then it completely stopped working again. I did not submit a second request due to the fact that I was moving out. - My biggest concern was the Air Conditioning. I submitted at least four maintenance requests to have my AC looked at as it would turn on but was not blowing cold air and did not cool my home at all. I came home to an oven every day over the course of an Arizona summer, I had to buy my own fan and run it constantly but was unable to sleep in my own home due to it being so hot. I went into the office and spoke with the assistant manager, Danielle, who at the time, was extremely nice and I truly believed she would help get the issue fixed. At no time did maintenance enter my home to look at the AC while I was there, nor was any notice of entry ever left to indicate that the issue was being looked at or worked on. The issue was never resolved by Avana Tempe, and was only resolved due to the weather changing. - None of the above issues include the many notices from Avana Tempe about the AC, water and even the electricity being out for the entire complex. I had to move out early due to an out-of-state job relocation. I went into the office and spoke to the assistant manager, Danielle about this on 09.26.19 and was advised that I needed to pay a buy out fee and provide 60 days notice. At no time did I become rude or disrespectful during this conversation. I did ask if Greystar would work with me since moving was completely out of my control and if the lease was terminated prior to 60 days, it would benefit both myself and Greystar because they had been renovating all the apartments. If I vacated earlier, they would be able to renovate sooner and in turn, begin charging a new tenant a much higher rent. Danielle said she would ask Tiffany(who I think was Danielle 's boss; I 'm not sure as no introductions were completed). I do not think Danielle or Tiffany understood what I was asking them and Tiffany was disengaged and aloof during the brief conversation. Danielle then provided me a piece of paper and told me to sign it, which I did. I was advised that I would be emailed a copy of the document that I had just signed and I thought the issue was resolved. Over the course of the next 60 days, I paid my rent online and on time, as I always had. I expected the online balance to reflect the buy out fee that I was verbally advised of and to calculate the prorated rent for my last month, but it did not show the fee and it showed a balance for the entire last month, not just the 1st - 26th. I paid the entire balance for the last month so that I would not be late and then I contacted the office to obtain a breakdown of the charges so that I could determine how much I had overpaid, and confirm the remainder of the fee so that I could pay it. I emailed the assistant manager directly since she was the one I had spoken to and when I did not receive a reply, I emailed again and CCed the general mailbox for the office, hoping that someone would be able to assist me. Danielle then sent me an unprofessional response in which she accused me of "refusing "to sign a second document that I was unaware of, and threatening that I would be in breech of the lease if I turned in my keys. Danielle also failed to provide the breakdown of charges that I requested so I was unable to verify the remaining amount owed. I responded to Danielle requesting that she discontinue treating me so poorly when all I was attempting to do was resolve the issue and complete my move out. I explained to her that I was unaware of the second document and I also let her know that I would be posting this review due to the many issues I had experienced during my stay, especially the fact that Avana Tempe "refused "to fix my Air Conditioning over the course of an Arizona summer. (I believe this is an ACTUAL breech of their lease, Section 30.) I never received a reply to this email, however days later I was emailed a Notice of Entry from a law office. Due to my inability to obtain a confirmation of the charges owed, I finally had to figure out the remaining amount due on my own by taking the second document that had not been provided to me until 11.12.19 and subtracting everything I had already paid. I then paid the difference via the online portal on 11.18.19 (within 7 days as stated by this document) and I then sent my own breakdown on the signed document to the office. The only response back was a Statement of Charges due, which was exactly what I overpaid for my last month 's rent, which was EXTREMELY frustrating because it was clear that not only was the office stonewalling me, but they were not even looking at my many attempts to resolve the situation as I had clearly outlined the overpayment in my email to them. I 'm very surprised that a company makes it so difficult to work with and pay them; I had trouble paying fees upon move in and then I struggled immensely trying to pay fees when I moved out. Also, because Danielle and Tiffany either did not understand what I was asking them about the 60 day notice, I called Greystar directly on several occasions so I could hopefully speak with someone who could help me and understand what I was asking. No one ever picked up the phone or returned my many voicemails in regard to this issue. I contacted Greystar directly again when I was unable to obtain a breakdown of the charges from the office - I emailed them on their website begging for someone to assist me, and received an almost immediate response, but it simply asked what community I was inquiring about. I responded and told them I was trying to work with Avana Tempe and I requested that they help me instead of simply forwarding my email to the community since the office staff had been treating me poorly and refusing to provide the requested information I needed to complete move out. I never received a response to this email, however I received a call from Spring Stewart the exact same day that i provided my own breakdown to the office. She left a voicemail stating that I could call her back, but she did not leave a number or extension to reach her. I called the generic number back and emailed, leaving messages requesting that she call back and she never did. Lastly, during my entire 7 months living at Avana Tempe, they were re-paining all of the buildings, re-surfacing all of the all of the pavement in the parking area, completing apartment renovations and completing an entire office renovation so I dealt with constant noise and outside messes, the pool and hot tub was closed the entire time, and then there was the additional inconvenience of not being able to use the main entry into the complex and not being able to park in my space for days. Due to the overall attitude of the office staff, the condition of the apartments, and the abhorrent way that I was treated when circumstances out of my control arose, I would not recommend renting from Avana Tempe. I would even go so far to discourage anyone from renting from any of the Greystar properties due to their complete lack of response when I reached out when the office staff refused to help me.

review_text: The apartment itself is well put together with full-sized amenities, which is a big plus. Having an in-unit washer and dryer is a bonus that many apartments don ’t offer. I do wish the laundry area on the patio had shelving, since there ’s nowhere to store detergent or dryer sheets. I ended up having to buy a shelf to put over the dryer, which wasn ’t ideal, but overall, having the washer and dryer makes up for it. The biggest downside to living here is the very strict patio policies. Many of the rules are not explicitly stated in the lease, which makes it frustrating. For example, I had a shelf that was marketed for both indoor and outdoor use, but was fined $100 because shelves are not allowed on patios. It was categorized as “unsightly ”.The rules seem to allow only explicitly designated “patio furniture ”—no shelves, no string lights, no drying laundry, no exceptions. It feels overly restrictive and makes it difficult to actually enjoy the patio space without going out to purchase brand-new furniture. Aside from the patio restrictions, it ’s generally a chill place to live. The inside of the unit is comfortable, the amenities are solid, and the washer/dryer is a major convenience.

author: Current Resident 774981
review_text: Avana staff was courteous and responsive when dealing with the discovery of mold in our air vents. They technically completed the work in a timely matter and left the apartment in good condition. Frustration came with how Greystar/Avana did not consider our claims of mold a serious matter and did not listen to requests for professional inspection and removal. We were told that the growth was only mildew and did not require further investigation. However, my husband and I have been experiencing symptoms of mold poisoning with daily headaches, itchy eyes, and a bloody nose. We purchased our own mold testing kit (of which Avana will not reimburse) and received results that our apartment contained 4 different types of mold - 1 of which is listed as a top dangerous mold (penicillium). Because we were experiencing symptoms, we decided it was best to leave the apartment and live elsewhere while the situation was in progress. In all, it took 3 weeks (from 5/13 - 6/2) to complete the required maintenance. And after all of this, Avana will not prorate the time that we considered it dangerous to live in the apartment. Overall, we are disappointed in how we were led to felt like we were overreacting and were forced to call the office routinely to respond to the problem. My husband and I are excellent tenants - all bills are paid on time, we are quiet, clean, and respectful of the property. We will be writing thorough reviews of our experience and not referring new residents to Avana. In addition, if we continue to experience symptoms, we will be taking our lab results to the doctor and medically recording the harm we have encountered. This entire process with Avana has been recorded and documented since it began on 5/13.
response_text: Hi Verified Resident 774981, we regret to hear that you are displeased with your recent experience with us. Thank you for leaving feedback. author: taylorlovett
review_text: DO NOT LIVE HERE! I have lived at Avana Tempe since July of 2018 when it was Flagstone. I bought out of my lease early in March 2019 and would have left earlier if I could. If I could give this place zero stars, I would. I 'll begin with the quality of the apartment. I pay almost $1200 per month for the worst apartment I have ever lived in. And I have lived in student housing the last 4 years so that says something. It is a small, one-bedroom apartment, that 's low quality at best. The apartment is supposedly one of their 'remodeled 'units that you see on the website. First glance, I liked it. Over time, I saw more and more issues. The hot and cold water in my building is reversed. This has ruined my clothes by having piping hot water used when I thought it was cold. The water that does come out of the faucets and shower smell like sewer water. The drains are even more terrifying. Frankly, I have avoided these areas because of the strong odor that comes from it. My shower drain, bathroom drain, and garbage disposal smell like all of the toilets in Phoenix drain to this particular apartment complex. Management and maintenance said there was nothing they can do about either issues since it was a larger plumbing issue. My sliding screen door won 't lock and hasn 't since the day I moved in. As a single female, that is important for me. Maintenance responded by asking "why do you need it to lock "and followed up by saying they weren 't fixing it. I pay $1200 and get ridiculed when I ask to fix something as simple as a door lock. The carpet in my apartment comes up and has nails sticking out. I have been given a temporary solution by nailing it in myself so thanks, Avana, you guys did teach me some handyman skills! The management team is incompetent, from finding packages that were delivered to answering simple questions without being rude or giving wrong information. They over water the grass to the point of standing water every single day. I have even seen them watering it 20 minutes after it rained, global warming who In case you were wondering what kind of residents live here, as I am typing this, I saw a resident take their dog to the bathroom and not pick it up. Can 't wait to step in dog poop later. They give mediocre notice of building improvements and do not take responsibility for their actions. When we had pressure washers cleaning our roof, all of my windows and doors were closed and locked, and black, muddy water seeped through all of my doors and windows. That dirty water got on my bed, wall, and carpet. They told me that they did not have responsibility even though THEIR POOR QUALITY OF APARTMENT IS THE REASON WATER CAME THROUGH. I was offered a 'cleaning 'by one of their staff which never showed up and I was forced to clean it all myself. As I spend my last few days here, I found a woman sobbing in the leasing office explaining the roaches she had in her apartment. There is not a single positive thing I can say about this place. Except maybe the fact they let people buy out of their lease so people can leave after they realize their mistake of living here. The 'amenities 'are a straight up lie. The pool is disgusting and they have rusted, metal tanning chairs which will burn your skin in the summer. The first and only time I went into the gym, I gagged at the smell. Overall, if you want overpriced piece of trash apartment, a useless leasing staff, and roaches as roommates, this is your place!

author: Current Resident 997004
review_text: Dear Avana Management, I 've officially put my foot in my mouth. I had no idea that I could logically fit my size 10 shoe completely down my throat with such ease OK, I 'll elaborate- I 've lived at this apartment complex for several years. Honestly, it 's not the newest complex as I remember having friends that lived here in the 90s. When I moved here in 2019, I could assume that this location would likely have some “wear and tear ”because the Avana Tempe property is 40+ years old. While things wear out and break down, it might seem simple to file a maintenance request and hope for the best, however, in the past (prior to 2024) it felt as though said requests were part of a larger project of trying to keep up a 40+ year old complex, and unfortunately, communication regarding requests was minimal probably because there were several repair projects taking place at any given moment. Still, I cannot imagine how difficult it is to keep up with all the requests and complaints you might receive. A week or so ago, I sent a letter to management regarding some work orders that had not been addressed in the past. Most of these work orders were concerning small issues in my unit, however, a few of these work orders were larger issues related to the property as a whole. In my haste, I neglected to consider the difficulty it might require for many of these work orders to be completed. A few days after I sent my letter to management, To my great surprise, every single item I was concerned about in my original set of work orders has been either addressed, or completely resolved. My sincerest apologies if anybody was effected by original letter I sent to management, I stand in complete awe at this sort of positive response. Just, WOW - Simply amazing. Additionally, The maintenance team member that you sent to fix everything was extremely polite, knowledgeable, and truthful about everything that had to be repaired. Staff was trusting and careful around my apartment as though they were working on their own home while conscious of personal items and cleanliness throughout the repair. All in all, I 'm completely surprised by this response, and as a result, I apologize to everybody for my previous letter. Thank you for diligence and urgency. My apartment is AWESOME Everybody should literally get a raise in pay.

author: hrclev
review_text: I don't know where the other reviewer lived in the complex, but I haven't had any problems after over a year of living here. In fact, I renewed my lease. I live on the far south side of the complex. I have had a couple incidents of seeing lone cockroaches, but pest control is a free amenity and both times they promptly came over. Never any problems with infestation. I've never even seen a scorpion on the grounds. Maintenance always comes over right away when we send in a work order. Usually the next morning, but sometimes the same day. One of the only complexes in the area that allows large dogs. The dog-friendly environment hasn't caused much bother, though once for a period of about two months it seemed like the other residents in our part of the complex just decided to stop picking up after their pets. The grounds are always very well-kept. Fresh grass, trimmed trees, and the pools are always clean (not an easy feat with the dust storms lately). Unfortunately, if you have a window next to grass then you are going to be woken up a few mornings by lawnmowers. My neighbors have all been very nice, never a nuisance. My one-bedroom is very spacious for the price. The office women are okay, but I haven't had any issues I've needed to take to them. The office has computers with internet connections, which is nice. Sometimes you'll have to ask for paper to refill the printers, which can get annoying. All in all, I really like it here. Pretty positive experience.

author: Current Resident 94070
review_text: I loved it, until I moved in. First the room smelled like smoke and weed, and maintenance staff, when questioned, told us that it hadn't smelled like that before we moved in. Really? Because we moved in 5 minutes ago. Then one of our walls broke, because it had rained and the roof was unrepaired, so water dripped into the walls and leaning against it made it fold like paper. Then the AC broke, and started dripping and didn't work. Turns out there was no Freon left, as it hadn't been changed in months. Then plumbing failed in several apartments, and there was human crap on the lawn outside. Took em two days to clean that up. Today marks the end of our second week staying here! They still haven't fixed that roof. So in summary, we've had a real issue with preventative maintenance here. As far as I can tell, they just didn't care enough to fix up our room, and were hoping we wouldn't say anything. Once you walk into the office and talk to them and very clearly describe the problem, the staff is actually fairly quick at getting things fixed. Maintenance staff didn't put down towels when letting the AC drain, so it soaked our floor, but it's laminated, so whatever. That said, the office staff is, on the whole, friendly and helpful. If you move here, your neighbors will be a few ASU students (because it's so close to the university), but it's not necessarily dominating the community. Everyone so far has been friendly, and we've had no noise issues at all. The amenities are fairly nice. I'd love living here, if it weren't for the constant maintenance issues. The location is good: close to major roads while still being fairly separated from them. It seems safe at most hours. Parking is good and available, including shaded parking if you sign up for it with the office. Our neighbors and friends have had none of these issues, so it seems to be a relatively uncommon series of constant issues. You gotta ask yourself: Am I feeling lucky? With my experience, especially with the smoking issue, I'm not sure I can recommend it. (Also, if you plan on staying for a long period, but you only lease for single years at a time, they force you to move upon renewing the lease! It's small, but it's a factor.)

Later on when I mentioned it in the office a girl there said they sound have temporarily let me stay in another apartment. GEE, thanks for letting me know now! The a/c went out again a little over a year later and we had to have maintenence guys come more than once because the first time they just claimed it was the filter. The ancient thermostat must've been too difficult to deal with because we came home one day finding a nice new one they entered without permission. Also, my friend who lived in my apartment before me led me to believe that there was something seriously wrong in the apartment (I wont get specific to remain anonymous) and when I asked in the office about it the girl sounded very mean and said that I should have mentioned it in the walk-through (which they never had me do!) and basically anything that was wrong with it would be my problem unless I took actions against my friend. They couldn't contact her themselves for some reason, and they didn't correct the wrong in not doing a walk-through. This lady knew I had never rented an apartment before and she sounded SO much nicer when I signed the lease. Turns out I was able to fix the problem myself luckily. They didn't even try to make sure that the apartment was in decent shape before I moved in though just because I was taking over the lease. - Getting any packages delivered is a pain because they don't notify you when they come in most of the time and you just need to keep asking them in the office. I get all of my packages delivered to my parents' house now since they live close-by to avoid this pain. - The dishwasher in my apartment is ancient and I have to wash all of my dishes by hand. I asked the managers to replace it but they just tred to fix it when it really needs to be replaced. The maintenence guy came 15 min before the latest time he was supposed to come and by then I had just left. The paint of the bathtub walls is peeling. The walls/front door are so thin, my downstairs neighbors are always annoyingly pounding at me (not blasting music or anything, just trying to live) and I can hear EVERYTHING that goes on outside of my front door (and everyone outside can hear inside). It's true that the electric bill is really high, as the other reviews state. I never had an apartment before this one, so I thought it was normal until I read those. The laundry rooms suck because the washing machines and dryers are usually broken and the dryers are always broken. Other tenants get impatient and put your laundry on top of the machine so they can do theirs. - They obviously don't look very hard regarding cleanliness when re-renting an apartment out because I happened to move my refrigerator to locate the source of an ant problem and found the floor underneath and the wall behind entirely covered in black sludge. I really wish I had taken a picture before cleaning it. - They don't bother to put your parking spot near your apartment and tenants have a habit of parking in the uncovered areas because of that, leaving less parking available for visitors. Neutral: - For probably about half a year they did renovations on the office and temporarily moved their office to an apartment. This was slightly inconvenient, especially for getting mail, but I managed. I can't really say for sure whether it was their fault or the construction company's. - Taking groceries home sucks because the stairs don't lead to the parking lot and you have to go all the way around, but it at least this could make things a bit safer in terms of theft. I haven't had any huge security problems as of yet My liscence plate was stolen from my car. It seems like someone could have been trying to break into my car's trunk, especially since the electric lock mysteriously broke, but I'm not 100% sure.

author: Current Resident 310072
review_text: I lived at DPV for a few years until I found so many scorpions in my apartment, I was developing an anxiety issue over it. And, yes, my place was kept clean - they are not like cockroaches and are attracted to water not dirt. I got stung by 1 walking on the grounds to the laundry room in flip flops and a separate time in my apartment. Before you rent here because of the cheap price tag consider this: people are not kidding or exaggerating about having electric bills around $300/month in the summer. The lowest I could get mine in the summer was $240 and that was keeping it at around 90 degrees yes, 90 degrees in my home because of the bill that summer sucked. You should factor this in and it might be cheaper (and much more comfortable) to pay a higher rent elsewhere because of what you will save in electric. Now at my new and much nicer apartment, the highest my electric bill went in the summer was under $75 and I kept it at around a nice, cool 75 degrees inside. Also - laundry rooms. They suck. The machines are: never all working, expensive, small, and are always being used by other people that have left their clothes in there to mildew and rot for what seems like days. I used to do my laundry in the middle of the night (typically around midnight to 1 am) just so I could get empty machines. And, I was honestly scared to death I would be raped and murdered in those sketchy laundry rooms but a girl needs clean clothes Also, I have found that I save money now by having a place that has a washer/dryer in it. And, if you live here please make sure that you LOVE Pitbulls. I felt like every single person but me had a freaking pitbull and, no, they are not all mean and viscous but some actually are. Yes, they can be great pets if you train them, socialize them, and work with them but from my experience - for the average college gangster, dog training is not high on the priority list. So, before "saving" all that money by living at DPV, don't forget to calculate in the additional cost of anti-anxiety medication needed to live and co-habitate with poisonous insects, outrageous electric bills (seriously figure an average of about $175 per month year round - could never figure out why it was so expensive in the winter but it was then too), and laundry machines which really add up. Right now I pay $150 more per month in my current apartment than DPV but save money every month (or close to break even) because the other bills decreased so much. And, now I have granite counter tops, a roman bath tub, recessed lighting, a huge patio, walk-in closet, and NOT ONE scorpion Keep looking - you can find better than DPV.

author: Current Resident 298540
review_title: 10 Reasons to Avoid Desert Palm Village
review_text: Desert Palm Village is a dump. Here's why: 1. The electric bills are ridiculous. They're routinely $300 in the summer. The place isn't well insulated at all. 2. Cockroaches. It only takes on dumpy tenant to infest the whole building. We had some such tenants in our building and ended up with cockroaches and ants. It got better when they moved out, but they're still around. 3. Dog crap. Everywhere. Seriously, this place smells like a dogcrap all the time. They have free poop bags everywhere, but do you think the trashy dog owners here use them? Nope. There are a lot of big dogs, lots of barking, and lots of dogcrap. We tried to use the tennis courts, but guess what there was dog crap on them. The management threatens fines, but they never walk the property so no one pays attention. 4. They charge you the same amount of pet rent for a quiet little cat as they do for a pitbull. My cat doesn't crap all over the property. 5. There is one nice person in the office. I don't know her name, but if you go in there she'll stand out as the nice one because the other workers are nasty. 6. The laundry rooms are often broken. They put in new washers/dryers, but they put in fewer units. They're often full. I suspect that some people are running a laundering service in the laundry room near my apartment. 7. Do you like gangs? Do you appreciated having your area tagged? The maintenance hurries up and covers up graffiti, but both the dumpster (which stinks terrible) and the walls have been tagged. 8. Weirdos. There are a couple of people who just stare at you when you walk by. I came home one night to find my downstairs neighbor and some other weirdos outside smoking butts wearing only briefs. There are too many weirdos to go through them all. 9. Poor lighting. The walkways between the apartments and the parking lots are poorly lit. It doesn't feel safe at all. 10. Services. You can't get Cox, you can't get SRP. APS is a rip off. If your apartment doesn't face the right direction for a satellite dish, you have to pay some fraudulent company called Consolidated Smart Systems 10 bucks a month for Directv. Everything here is a rip off.

review_text: i lived here from 98 - 00. that time was ok but now i would not want to live there now. i like parties as much as any college kid but when its several times a week its starts to get a little annoying. my roommate ́s car was broken into and the stereo stolen. the apartments look nice from the outside but inside it looks dated. the trim around the doors kept coming loose. we also found scorpions on the patio several times. covered parking was a plus.

author: Current Resident 789655
review_text: what a bunch of babies! Obviously you spoiled college kids can ́t handle the real world-where everything is not perfect and handed to you on a silver spoon! I find it hard to believe anything I read on here because it all sounds like repetitive crying and complaining. I happen to very much enjoy living here. I think it is a good community and have had absolutely ZERO problems. I think maintenance is efficient and very nice guys-I think the office workers are polite and do the best that they can. What do you all expect? Them to bend over and kiss your everytime you walk in the door? Treat people how you want to be treated and again realize that everything is not going to be all honkey-dorey because this is your "first apartment" and mom and dad are totally going to pay for everything. Try to stop crying all the time and remember that what doesn ́t kill you in life can only make you stronger!!

author: funny_face17
review_text: My roomate and I were two college freshman girls starting out life on our own. We got a pretty good promotional deal here and decided to move in. Little did we know. First, they didnt allow us to view the actual apartment we would be living in until the day of our move-in. And when we finally did see it, it was so run-down. Things were broken, cracked, stained, punctured. The AC bill just about broke us. There were knife punctures in our front door(that is made tin or something like it), three of the four burners on our stove didnt work. We had an ant infestation. The front desk people were rude, pushy, and manipulative. There is no safe parking after 7pm. If you want creepy dirty guys hitting on you just call on the maintence staff. But the real "hazard" comes in when my roomates shower door had broken off(before we moved in), so we had maintenence come and "fix" it, and come "fix" it again, and again and again. Until one night after my roommate took a shower, she went to close the shower door and it fell and split her forehead open. When we informed management about this, there were no appoligies, no free rent, no sort of compensation. (And the door is still not fixed!) So we are moving to the Enclave apartments on Southern and Dorsey. They seem clean, up-kept, and we even get to view the apartment before we move in. You better bet we will be inspecting the shower door!

author: Current Resident 555211
review_text: I guess you get what you pay for. My roommate chose this place while I was out of town and when I showed up to sign the lease I definitely hesitated. It's just not that nice, but it doesn't cost much to live there so I guess it makes sense. The one thing that stands out most was when I called maintenance to have them fix my closet door (which wouldn't move unless I put all of my body weight into it) and the guy just straight up said he couldn't fix it. I could only use one side of my closet for the year that I lived there and even then, I couldn't actually open and close the door regularly. We had a pretty big scorpion problem toward the end, which was pretty much my worst nightmare come true. There was one guy who lived across from us who was clearly on steroids and used to scream like a gorilla at 3am. Come to think of it, there was a lot of noise most of the time. Everything in the apartment was just kind of run down and my bed was like slanted because one corner of my room appeared to be sinking into the ground. I never would have lived here in the first place, but it's obvious that you get what you pay for. Personally, I'd rather spend the money because I was pretty uncomfortable the whole time I lived there. Oh, yeah, and the staff was usually really rude to us, but I understand that they are under new management now. Hope it gets better!

author: Current Resident 404159
review_text: I dumped my cherry nuts into the disposal in the kitchen. The disposal stopped working and I called the apartment office to fix it. Rom, one of the service staff members, came in and he spent 20 minutes to pick the cherry nuts trapped in the dirty disposal one after another without complaining it. The good service quality in Desert Palm Village is a plus.

author: Current Resident 75798
review_text: The staff and maintenance crew are Awesome. They always seem to be making new improvements to the Facility. It is a very quiet complex. The Dog park that was put in is really nice, and everyone that lives here are always polite and you never really hear loud music or loud people.

author: Current Resident 712217
review_title: OMG! WE all feel the same way!
review_text: Yes to everything stated. This place sucked and is so run down. My girls and I didn ́t get hot water for the first week or two we were there, our roof literatlly caved in after a water leak and wasn ́t finished for 20 days after (while living with large energy consuming vaccuums and not being able to reach the kitchen for two days), yes, the AC broke a few times, the stove broke, and a list of other things, to top it all off, the week before we moved out the pipeline underneath the kitchen sink broke and flooded the apartment. They finally fixed it after a hour or so but didn ́t mop up all the nasty water, my roomate spent two hours cleaning it up herself. DO NOT MOVE IN HERE. PROBLEM FROM DAY ONE, LITERALLY!

author: Current Resident 75184
review_text: The staff is extremely cordial. Courtney was there to help me throughout my move-in process. Decent rent for a 1BHK. I don't have a pet but if you have one, they accommodate you. Easy access to ASU, restaurants, grocery stores, gas stations, etc. They definitely have my recommendation.

author: Current Resident 462561
review_text: I have been staying here from past 3 years and I can confidently say that their staff and services are very friendly and diligent. I have been friends with the staff on first name basis. My leasing manager, Thomas E, has been very helpful. Based on my discussion with my friends, we all agree that desert palms village is one of the best communities in Tempe. I had a problem few months back wherein my bathroom door was locked from inside and I put in a service request at 5am. Within 5 mins a very sleepy looking person showed up and solved it.
response_text: Dear Resident, Thank you for your residency with us for over three years! We are thrilled that Thomas and our team have provided you with the customer service you deserve. Thank you for calling Desert Palm Village your home.

author: Current Resident 882165
review_text: I lived there for almost one year. I like the spacious two bed two bath model. They repair things very quick, I can not complain about that. They have warm swimming pools and club house which brought me lots of fun long time ago. My neighbors were ASU students, only few of times they have parties but most of times they are quiet. I like it because the plenty of parking, it have gates, close to safeway and bus station. A good place!

author: Current Resident 413681
review_text: DPV is awful, I lived here for two years, the apts are horribly constructed, insects/scorpions seen frequently, Staff is rude! FREQUENT CRIME!

author: Current Resident 185508
review_text: I lived at Desert Palm for 2 years (2004-2005), and overall I really liked my apartment. I agree w/ the other reviewers that the management/office staff are not the friendliest, most competent people. But, quite honestly, I almost never had to deal with them. My apartment was very cute and had an amazing amount of closet space. I am a single female and I always felt very safe while living there. I was also a student at ASU, and loved the convenience of walking to class everday. Especially, since parking costs have increased astronomically over the years. Your experience at Desert Palm can depend greatly upon the decency of your neighbors. Toward the end of my second lease a guy moved into the apartment below me and blasted rap music at all hours of the night. I also had some new neighbors move into the apartment next to me that cooked every meal using an insane amount of curry, and the odor crept into my apartment and stayed there for the remaining period of my lease. The gym and the laundry room are awful. The pools are decent and are kept clean. If you are a student at ASU who is only planning on living here for a couple of years, I think you will find it to be a positive experience overall.

author: Current Resident 330446
review_text:
To the ignorant person who claimed I'm "crazy" for thinking they should have done more for me or at least called me on Christmas:

Maybe you have a rich lawyer daddy that can replace all of your belongings that could have been lost in a fire but I don't have that luxury. They most definitely should have called to notify me of the fire on Christmas and should not have left me surprised to come home that evening and find the building in shambles.

I don't care what your father says, I talked to a law professor at ASU after the incident and she said I was perfectly able to sue and had every right to. However, I opted not to because I'm satisfied with what they gave me enough to the point that I can live without anything else.

You will never understand the emotional trauma it caused me when I came home Christmas night to find the building ruined and my cat near death. If you think I shouldn't have been called, YOU are the crazy one.

If you think I don't know who you are either, you are wrong. Take your self righteousness somewhere else because any sane person would want to be called immediately after something as extreme as this.

And by the way, they did NOT help me move. My family and boyfriend's family moved every bit of our furniture. So with all due respect, you need to put your money where your mouth is.

author: Current Resident 611653
review_title: This apartment is garbage. Read this review
review_text:
First, I want to talk about the staff at Desert Palm Village. Their customer service skills are at a minimal level; a staff of uneducated women who repeatedly lie, steal, and manipulate any customer for money. It is entirely fair of me to say these people are the biggest pain in the to deal with. Again, I want to stress the fact that the staff at Desert Palms Apartments is the most rude, poorly mannered, impolite, disrespectful, offensive, and foul individuals you will ever do business with. No doubt, these employees strive for a high commission check by lying to their customers.

Second, I want to inform anyone who is considering living there, Desert Palms has a major scorpion problem. Within my year lease, my apartment had found nine scorpions. Again, the staff never informed us of any such problem prior to moving in. The staff believes by sending out an exterminator will resolve the problem. No doubt, this is a lie. The exterminator told us, “all that can be done is to keep the apartment clean”. The spray of chemicals does not keep these dangerous insects away. In addition, all the scorpions found were babies, which are known to be the deadliest due to the inability to control the amount of venom when injected into their prey. The scorpions were always present. My neighbor who lived below me, found eleven scorpions in one month. This is the truth. Again, this all leads back to the staff at Desert Palms. They lied about the solution to fixing this problem, they lied about calling an exterminator, and they were extremely rude every time we inquired this matter.

Third, anyone who considers living at Desert Palms will have to deal with crime. I know of several of friends, whose cars were stolen, vandalized, and damaged. Car stereos are ripped off, windows are broken, paint jobs are “keyed”, and car tires slashed. Again, the staff claims no responsibility for this matter. Last the living quality is absolutely horrible. Residential crime includes neighbors who beat their wives; residents are always partying as late as 4a.m., and homeless people bathe in the apartments public hot tub.

I have read many other comments that are similar to mine. To the comment by one of the residents who has lived at Desert Palms for five years-- I am an educated resident. I know what customer service is, and I understand good living conditions. Obviously, this person is a Desert Palms employee. The staff at Desert Palms Village are the only ones who do not have an education. A few questions to ask yourself after reading that particular review are; how would the person know there are 512 units available in the complex? Why would someone make excuses for a scorpion problem? What is this persons’ motive? Why would a resident put time and effort in defending an apartment complex? No doubt, the person spent more time attacking other reviewers, rather than making positive remarks about the complex. Don’t believe that last review. It’s not true.

My advice; if you live at Desert Palms, you are making a big mistake. Don’t believe me? Call Desert Palms Village and ask them yourself- (480) 968-1099. Speak to the manager, her name is Michelle. If Michelle isn’t there, ask for Rebecca. They will be happy to lie to about any questions that you may have.

author: DesertPalmVillage
review_text: I had a great experience while living at desert palm village. I especially appreciate the office and maintenance staff. The offic staff is very kind and helpful. The maintenance staff is always on time when it comes to work orders and they are friendly as well!

author: Current Resident 746215
review_text: I had a light switch issue in my living room. Greg Garcia from Desert Palm Village maintenance did a great job fixing it. Thank you so much for your patience, punctuality and effort, despite the especially hot day of 108 degrees!

author: Current Resident 220551
review_text:

I am well over 40 and have lived her for many years. I stay here because I like my apartment. The prices are good, location is good, things are fixed quickly, the staff is nice and it is my home. I would never base my decision on what some stranger wrote on a web site.

In my experience people who write such negitive things are out to get someone. I am not sure who made them so mad, but you can tell they are. The company is very strict about their policies and I myself have not been happy at times, but they are doing their job. I know that so I let it go.

I would suggest looking at this apartment complex. Oh yeah I just renewed for another year.

The site manager has always been solving any issues that we might have had in the past and in general I feel great living here!

They recently upgraded their washing machines and dryers to a card system. Unfortunately they never informed us that we would be without washing machines/dryers for about 3 weeks. As mentioned before the insulation isn't the greatest so your apartment heats up pretty fast and uses a lot of electricity. The location and price are top notch though and I have no complaints. The noise levels also don't seem to be too bad. I've had no problems in dealing with the maintenance staff or the people in the front office. Besides the brunette who works there is pretty cute.

author: KarenWalker21

I have never been happier living in this apartment. I hope that you enjoy it as much as I do. Feel free to e-mail if you want some respose to some questions you might have by an actual resident.

author: Current Resident 32505
review_text: I have been living here since 2/04, and I find the staff to always be willing to assist. The maintanence staff is always helpful..A few times took a day or two to get things done. Overall not bad for the low price.

author: Current Resident 150252
review_text: This is a fairly nice community near my college. The rent is at a reasonable amount but it keeps going up. Staff in the office is always nice and helpful. author: Current Resident 920131
review_text: We have had a good experience renting here and we are moving out only because we've bought a place. The pool and hot tub are also very nice. There a lot of dog owners so if you are weary of dogs, that might be an issue for you. The apt was very comfortable in the winter months, but I cannot attest to the summer living experience(the walls do not seem very insulate) It is very convenient with the Orbtiz stopping right at the door step that takes you to campus and Mill Ave. and the 72 going to downtown scottsdale is a block a way. author: legendaryfrog
review_text: Desert Palm Village has been a dream; far and away our best rental experience. The buildings were built in the 1970's, but are kept up well. This is a surprisingly quiet neighborhood considering it is only half a mile from ASU, and we have never had any issues with our neighbors. Having easy access to the on-site gym and pool facilities is a great bonus, but far and away what elevates the experience of living here is the most shockingly personable and friendly staff we have encountered living in multiple states and many different apartments. The management staff is eager to answer any questions we might have, and despite presiding over a large complex, quickly learned our names. Interacting with them is always a joy. Whenever something needs to be repaired, no matter how large or small, the office will send someone the same day to fix it. The maintenance staff is very helpful - Greg is always timely and cheerful when he comes to fix something, and will go above and beyond to ensure we are satisfied. IMT residential is lucky to have such an amazing staff working to represent their company, and we are lucky to benefit from their efforts as residents.

author: sweens112
review_text: On the bright side, Desert Palm Village is very close to ASU, which helps me as a college student. The fitness centers are really nice with the usual workout equipment and a sauna and hot tub. The apartments are fairly spacious - they were the biggest we found for the same price when looking last year. I wish that wouldn't have played into my decision so much though. The neighbors are great, generally a mixed group of college students and young adults with kids. The maintenance guys are really nice as well, despite all the plumbing problems they've had to deal with. Our apartment flooded 5 or 6 times throughout the last year. The immediate neighborhood, specifically the two apartment complexes to the west before Rural, isn't the safest, and there have been a couple of major burglaries and a stabbing over there in the last 6 months. Because of the terrible housing market the last couple of years, every available housing option has seen an increase in monthly rent and utilities. For a 9 month lease, rent is $816/month for a 2-bed/2-bath apartment. That does not include any of the utilities. Electric will run you $180/mo. in the summer but only around $30/mo. in the winter. DirecTV, the only option for cable, offers crappy packages, starting at $55/mo. which includes about 100 home-shopping channels along with the 9 or so my roommate and I watch. We just decided to disconnect our cable because the deal sucks so much. Consolidated Smart Systems, based out of California, provides the internet, which also rips us off for about $40/mo. The service always cuts out whenever there's a storm between here and CA. The girls who work in the main office are generally unhelpful and not hard workers. I went in to say that there was no way to change the televisions in the fitness center, and one of them said they didn't have a remote and that it had been a problem for awhile. Well what are you doing to fix the problem?! The same thing happened when the water dispensing machine broke - I went in to tell them, and the girl said, "Yeah I think there's a number on it. You can call that." Why don't you call it?! Overall, compared to friends' places, Desert Palm Village is really average to poor in the service and quality of the apartments, but it's one of the best bargains around. If it weren't for the rest of the market being expensive, I wouldn't recommend it. I'm freaking astounded that upwards of $950 a month is cheap for a 2-bed/2-bath though

review_text: I've lived here for almost a year. For the most part these apartments are fine. But if you like sleeping in it may not be possible. They start doing random grounds maintenance at 8 in the morning. Which is understandable because it's too hot to do it later I'm sure. But holy crap the walls are so thin I can hear all of it like they are working right outside my window even if they arent. Yesterday I couldn't sleep past 8 because they were weed wacking the grass for 3 hours. It was so loud even with all the windows closed I couldn't sleep. Today I couldn't sleep past 8 cuz they decided to replace just the screws on people's porches so all I could hear was this drill for 3 hours which shouldn't be loud enough to keep you up. But it is. I'm not a light sleeper either. And never mind replacing the old boards on the porches that are so cracked and us baked they look like theyre about to just fall apart. Nope they just painted them instead so they look less cracked. And then decided to replace just screws. Like that'll do a whole lot of good. It's almost like they have them doing busy work that doesn't even do any good except to wake you up at 8 and not let you go back to sleep. Yes this is pretty much my only complaint but seriously. I just wanna sleep in guys! This loud early outdoor maintenance is driving me nuts. Oh and the porches aren't covered. So if you want to go out on the porch in the summer forget about it. It's hot enough as it is but there's not even shade which would definitely be nice when it's already so hot in phoenix. We used to have a tree that shaded it. But then they took it down. Great. author: Current Resident 62270
review_text: Overall, I really like this apartment complex. I feel like I am getting a fairly large apartment compared to how much I pay in rent. The ladies in the office are very helpful and friendly. Maintenance requests are always responded to in a timely manner. I did have some issues with the power going out in summer a few times, but it was always fixed later that day. Communication about maintenance to the complex is not that great, though. I would get a sign on my door saying they are painting the building on X date, but that date is in the past, so I have no idea when they are actually painting. Or I would get a notice on my door that they are doing some maintenance that requires some action from me (such as clearing my balcony, or moving my car), that needs to be done that same day or the next day, which is not enough notice. And when they repaved the parking lot it was a disaster, because they did not keep to the schedule that they had posted, so I was never sure when my car needed to be moved, and there was a big problem with people parking in covered spots. Speaking of which, they never enforce the assigned parking, so there are always people parked in my spot, even when the parking lot isn't being repaved. This review has been kind of complainy, but these issues are not that frequent, and overall this is a great place to live. My only ongoing annoyance is dogs barking at all hours, but that's hardly the complex's fault.

author: Raindrop3084
review_title: The ULTIMATE reason not to live here:
review_text:
If there ́s anyone that can convince you not to live here,it ́s me. There was a fire in my building on Christmas morning at 3 A.M. because my idiot neighbor left a burning cigarette on his couch. This is the only fire in the apartment ́s history. My boyfriend and I were with our family for the holidays so the only one home was our little 6 month old kitten. The fire was raging apparently and the firefighters thought it was going to take the whole building, but luckily, only 2 of the 8 apartments in the building were unsalvagable. Out of all 8, ours was the only one spared of any damage. NO ONE CALLED TO TELL US THE FIRE HAPPENED. After a wonderful Christmas, my boyfriend and I arrived home to find 6 of the 8 doors in our building boarded up, soot everywhere, and all of the power shut off. Our kitty was left alone in there and we were never ever called by any staff. He was wheezing and I was afraid he was very sick, but after some fresh air, things were fine. We gathered our things and went back with our families until something could be worked out. First thing the next morning, the front office received a very angry call from me asking for an explanation. I was told someone would get back to me within 30 minutes. When no one called after 45, I called even more upset. The manager asked me to come in and discuss what we could do. So, when I came in, she offered me the very least. She said she didn ́t see why I couldn ́t stay in the apartment because in her opinion, it was livable. Let me tell you I couldn ́t even breathe because of the smoke, the power was still off, and the rest of the building was in shambles. I told her I wanted to move and then proceded to ask her why I was not called. She said she heard the news about 9 am on Christmas morning and since she is pregnant and has bad morning sickness, she wasn ́t feeling well enough to call anyone. I ́m sorry, but morning sickness is NO EXCUSE for not informing someone of almost losing all of their belongings and their pet in a fire. To make a long story short, they transferred us to a new apartment and paid all my activation fees for electricity and such. They also replaced all the groceries that went bad in the refrigerator and freezer when the power was shut off after the fire. It was honestly the least they could do and I had to fight just to get them to give me that. There is no excuse for not calling anyone after something like this, especially when they have a pet.

Aside from this, the area I live in isn ́t too noisy, though I live underneath a girl who sounds like she is moving around her apartment in the wee hours of the morning every night. I have complained and nothing happens.

Also, the first week I lived here one of my car ́s tires got stolen and I walked out to my car to find the front right side resting on a green crate. The night time security is non-existent here.

And, in the winter, the longest shower you can take before the water is ice cold is about 5 minutes.

In my opinion, parties aren ́t an issue. I am an ASU student, but an honors one, and I have no tolerance for that kind of crap. Luckily for me, I must live in an area where that doesn ́t happen since so many people claim to hear parties all the time. Glad those parties aren ́t by me, because I ́d be calling the police every night on them!

Overall, don ́t live here, because if anything bad happens to you they take little or no responsibility for what has happened to you. I can ́t wait to move when my lease is up.

review_text: Nice community. Many amenities around the complex, including a dog park that is well maintained. Many people own dogs and cats, but there tends to be a lot of dog poop around the complex grassy areas. The windows are not sealed and let in the heat/ cold and sound very easily. A good amount of ASU students live here, but it does not get overly noisy on the weekends. Front desk staff are happy to help and friendly. Bus routes are easily accessed from this complex.

author: Current Resident 640831
review_text: I haven't been here long, but I already know it will be great. The grounds are clean, parking is close, and the apartment itself is very nice and spacious. The office staff is very helpful and down to earth. But I am most impressed with the maintenance. The previous tenant had kicked a hole in one closet door and knocked both of them off the hinges so they didn't open/close at all. I placed a request yesterday evening and Roman was here first thing in the morning. He was so nice and helpful and did a spectacular job. I'm thoroughly impressed and can't wait to see how the rest of my lease plays out.

author: Current Resident 137459
review_text:
I have been living in a 1b/1b apartment in Desert Palm for 1.5 years. I like my apartment very much, because it is spacious, has a good view (a big tree infront of the window and balcony) and my neighbors are quiet (most of them are senior ASU students).

The new managers are fine, better than the ones before. I like the tennis court, basketball court, but NOT like the swimming pool and hot tub (sometimes they looks dirty, but this impression was from last summer, i don't know whether they have been changed since the new managers come). We seldom use our covered parking lot, because it is far away from our apartment. I don't know why the manager arrange it so unwisely.

It usually have 2 month free in the summer, and give out current residents good recommendation fee. If you want to live near ASU, and have a spacious room in a fair price level (around $550), it is definitly a good choice. I have visited a lot of apartments near ASU, Desert Palm is the best in that price level.

author: sachingrover
review_text: It is a good place to stay and the maintenance is what has really impressed me. I would surely recommend this to other people.

They don't leave a mess and are even respectful about walking on the carpet. When I moved in my apartment was not cleaned how I would have liked and there was dog poop stains all over the carpet, but since then they have been removed (that's more of a previous tenant thing).

author: Current Resident 980258
review_text:
After 2.5 years, I finally I graduated from ASU and moved out of Desert Palm. Having moved around Tempe for years, I'm so happy I found this place. The community is nice and clean and they're doing a lot of renovations these days. Since IMT management took over, the service became much better - maintenance supervisor is excellent.

I loved the tennis courts and the swimming pools. I never used the gym, I don't think is that good. I love the free copy machine. They have highspeed internet (though the computers are bad and full of spyware, if you're just surfing its good!) There's also free color laser printing in the office which I often use. Unfortunately, some residents abuse it, printing tons of crap so the printers are taking a beating and down a lot.

I felt safe in that apartment. Twice I left my apartment key hanging on my door overnight and nothing happened. I just realize my mistake the morning after.

I encounter problems due to high turnover of leasing agents and some of them are inexperienced. I also complained that my assigned parking space is so far from my place but I only use it during summer and the rest of the year, there's enough parking for me and my guests. I also heard about some bug problems but I never had it. Maybe it's better on the second floor.

I was sad to leave it last week but I have to move on. I recommend this place. Good price and good community.

author: frugal1
review_text: I'm simply sharing my feedback so new potential renters don't make the same mistake. Before moving into Elliot's Crossing After being a resident at this apartment for over 7 months, and any positive review couldn't be more fabricated. I invite to you to take a walk on premise and see for yourself The only positive thing I can think of is maintenance has always been responsive. Saftey is a concern. Check the Tempe Police website. Garden Grove Apartments ,which is just across the street , is the number 1 police callout in Tempe and some of the toxicity has spilled over into Elliot crossing ungated community. I've had other residents mentioned their cars have been broken into and police visit the premises a lot. The pictures online are deceiving. I'm afraid to invite guest over. The grounds are dirty. Dog mess is everywhere. When summer ends and the jet engine a/c units stop blasting, every conversation from the neighboring apartments can be heard. Drama and arguments have played out in my bed room at night. Outside noise goes on from outside at all hours of the day and night as well. Ear plugs have not helped. There have been various reviews of cockroaches (which they call waterbugs) and termites infesting the dwellings. I'm sad to confirm those reports are true. I have taken several pictures I can show. Management is delusional if they think this apartment complex is great. Ownership has changed several hands and rent has perpetually increased without improving the quality of living for the residents. Management is also very lenient of the noise and does not enforce policies for the number of roommates living in one apartment unit. The management has done a very poor job displaying speed limits in the parking lot; a catastrophe waiting to happen.. As working residents we don't ask for me much; just a quiet, safe, and clean apartment dwelling. I've spoken up the chain in several cases and no action has been done. If you're a member of Elliot Crossing Apartment management and reading this, I do have some advice . Instead replying with more broken promises, please actually do something tangible. Start by sending a letter out to all your residents with a plan to improve the quality of living and remind all residents of the rules they signed in their lease. Loud noise, parties, and dog mess are unacceptable. Invest in a noise reducing barriers and a security gate; I'm sure an apartment community with 2 pools and over hedged apartment rent can afford it.
response_text: Thank you for your honest review. At Elliots Crossing, we strive to provide great service and are upset to read that you feel you've experienced the contrary. We would appreciate the opportunity to properly address your concerns. Please contact us at bpmcares@bridgepm.com at your earliest convenience so that we may go over the concerns outlined in your review. We hope that you have a positive experience with us moving forward.

author: Current Resident 204703
review_text: A transitional home for me. The property is older (built in the early 80's), and while they are renovating many of the apartments (mine included) remain dated. The infrastructure of the property remains dated. AC unites are old and you can tell the seasons by the number service men repairing AC units. Not well insulated, so expect to see that in your electric bill. Lots of green space, however. Parking is nightmare for the east side of the property, particularly after they built a "soccer pitch," a nice amenity for families but one that will be under used in context of the inconvenience created for many residents. The staff is hit or miss. While I've had a generally positive experience working with the leasing and maintenance staff, I know others have not.

author: Current Resident 543536
review_title: Just about everything that could go wrong did!
review_text: Lets start with the apartment itself. The noise in the apartments travels through walls as if they were paper. If you are unlucky, you get stuck on the 1st floor where you can hear your upstairs neighbors daily rituals and relish the time they are away. If you are extremely unlucky and live in apt 103 you will be able to hear everything (sounds of the bathroom). The lady that lives up above has been there for approx 13 years, weighs over 300 lbs, and rarely leaves home. One would think a 300+ lb lady would not be 300+ lbs with the amount of movement she makes on a daily basis, but I can only assume it is from excess trips to the fridge. The office staff has completely changed with the exception of the property manger, Joanne. If anything goes wrong (and it will), it will be pulling teeth to get it straightened out. I had a sewage flood in my apartment and we had to fight to get a hotel stay, and it took 3 days to clean the place. The A/C went out (in the summer) and we had to fight to get a hotel stay. Apparently there is an unwritten rule that the temperature inside your apartment has to exceed 90 to get a free hotel stay, but luckily enough it got up to 91. My car was towed to repave the lot without notice. They give out these little stickers to identify your car but when I asked the Joanne about them she said they don ́t even keep the records. I guess it is to give you an initial sense of security when you move in. I had to complain about the "large woman" that lurked above me for the duration of the lease, and notices were issued but no action was ever taken. Once the "large woman" above realized we were complaining about her, she started to complain about us and Joanne just let it go on and on. The maintenance staff is the shining jewel. About 80% of all issues were resolved quickly and were done right the first time. Parking is horrible if you live on the north side of the property unless you want to pay $15 a month for a covered spot. If you live there a year, almost all your neighbors will change (except for 300+ lb neighbors above you), the office staff will all change, some major appliance will break, and you will always hear a party, a dog, or screaming kids. My advice, stay away FAR AWAY!

author: Former Resident 824811
review_text: The staff lies to you. The staff covers up the truth. Corporate sides with their staff without having a conversation with you about the situation and hearing your side. They fill out a move out charges worksheet and then days later destroy the original one, recreate a similar one, and add nearly $100 to the total from the original sheet. and claim the total on the fraudulent sheet are "standard fees." If they are standard fees then why the heck were they not put on my 1st move out charge sheet that was destroyed and recreated. Luckily for me I made a copy of the original one. Then when confronted about this they tell that you should've signed a paper stating the standard fees and acknowledge that you were never given this sheet, never signed it, never saw it, and still proceed to charge you the "standard fees" that you knew nothing about and acknowledge they failed to disclose them to you. Additionally, I was promised a rent rate that I agreed with and applied for. I dove 3 days cross country just to arrive to sign my lease and they increased my rent nearly $200 a month and claimed it was because of "market value." Again corporate refused to honor the original agreed upon rent price so I got screwed by them the day I got here. SOUNDS LIKE A CROOKED BUSINESS AND SHADY BUSINESS PRACTICES TO ME AND YOU NEED TO FIND SOMEWHERE ELSE TO LIVE. Unless of course you like being lied to, taken advantage of, being ignored by corporate staff, and having fraudulent documents created to support their outrages lies. I have attached the charge worksheets (original and fraudulent one) for your convenience to prove that I am not just making this up. Pay particular attention to the handwriting as they are different, the date is different, the original charges are scratched out and the 35 dollar fee is changed to a 75 dollar fee. If they claim the 85 and 75 are "standard fees" then why are they not listed on the sheet as such, why were they not listed on my original sheet, and why did they feel the need to destroy the original cost sheet and recreate a similar one?

author: Current Resident 785485
review_text: Uncovered parking is an absolute nightmare in the summer! Management was very friendly, but often quite slow to fix things. Pool is very nice! Three times during my three years of living there, I got knocks on the door at 2 in the morning looking for someone who wasn't there. They were obviously looking for drugs, and it freaked me out. The thing that made me move out, however, was the HORRIBLE cable system! They have "TV Max" cabe, which only has 60 or so channels, and they are low-tier channels (honestly, who wants The International Channel?). Never had a problem with roaches, as previous posts screamed about. Also, got a little concerned with the high voltage wires running through the parking lot. It messed with my radio reception, and I have to wonder if it messed with my health. There is not a grocery store nearby! The nearest ones are at Guadalupe and Rural, Elliot and McClintock, or Eliot and 48th Street. Doesn't make for a quick trip to the store!

author: Former Resident 777660
review_text: This place deserves zero stars Do not rent here! The apartments are not nice enough to compensate for the heinous apartment managers. They are absolutely the worst! Every time you walked down there, it was being staffed by a whole new set of people. They probably went through a million employees in the whole two years we were there. They were really good at promising anything and everything to you, and then when you came back to ask about it, all we got was "Well who told you that? That's not right." If you are going to live here, get EVERYTHING THEY SAY IN WRITING! The grounds crew are there cleaning the grounds every single morning, so say good bye to hearing anything from 7-9am, the pool during the summer is disgusting! Hopefully you're one of the first few swims of the week, but then someone is guaranteed to POOP in it (happened both summers we were there), and it won't be cleaned for about two weeks. There were cockroaches in our bathrooms, and the toilets overflowed regularly. (be prepared to use only 1-2 squares when using the facilities). Lastly, the move out. I was told by one of the front people (who knows which one, they're probably gone by now), that we could get a free cup of touch up paint. When I went to collect I waited 5 HOURS for them to contact the head maintenance man, because only one person in the whole damn place had access to the magical unattainable paint. I finally lost my patience and went to figure it out myself, and it turns out they didn't carry the color of paint that I needed. cool. We also cleaned and scrubbed that apartment for two days. Two whole days. We bought special cleaners, and scrubbers, and that place looked amazing! At least better than when we moved in (there was a visible dirty foot print on the wall). We were charged almost $300 in cleaning fees. $300?!?!? Absolutely ridiculous. I have lived in a total of 7 apartments, and these people were by far the worst. Do not rent here. Do not work here. Stay as far away as you can and pray for the poor souls who still live there.

author: Current Resident 873895
review_text: By far the worst apartment complex I have ever lived in. Been here for about a year, moving out on January first thank god. First of all, there are notices on everyone's door about once a month for "annual" maintenance inspections. They give you a days notice that someone will be coming into your apartment at any given time throughout the day. It feels like a violation of privacy, I understand maybe once a year but this has happened almost every month since I've lived here. Then there's the fact that on two separate occasions I've been walking down the stairs only to find that the concrete stairs are completely broken in half, like there's a whole stair missing. It's extremely dangerous. The one that's busted now has been this way for two weeks, they finally just put caution tape up around it. God forbid anyone is walking underneath one if them when another one breaks. You would literally die or have a serious concussion. Then there's the fact that there are constant police stand offs and situations in this area, two people got shot across the street a few weeks ago, another person got shot just a short time before that. Also, there are people smoking pot pretty much on a daily basis on their patios, which wouldn't be so bad if I didn't have to go out onto MY patio to do my laundry and smell their bad decisions. Especially since I'm pregnant. Lastly, they've been painting the whole complex for the last few months and they start outside slamming ladders on the side of the buildings at 7 am. I honestly feel like they try to be as absolutely loud as possible. I hate this place to the core, heed my advice look elsewhere!

author: Current Resident 535120
review_text: There is nothing better than walking into a clean community. It shows just how much the staff takes care of the place. The community is very green and well kept. The staff is nothing short of kind and generous. I'm moving out this month and I'm sorry to go. This community is very great, it's a hidden gem in the uglyness that Tempe, AZ can sometimes be. You'll feel it too the moment you walk through the doors. The manager is always making conversation with his residents and always seems to be in a good mood. His assistant is the exact same way, she actually cares about the residents and isn't just out for the money, the leasing girl has always been very nice to me as well! I wandered on this site the other day and felt that I needed to post something positive amongst all this cruelty. Rent at Pinnacle Grove, you won't be dissappointed.

author: Current Resident 740889
review_title: My Home Away From Home II (STAY AWAY )
review_text: I am the person that wrote the posting "My Home Away From Home" in October of 2006. It is now November and do I ever have a change of heart about this place After I posted the 1st comment, I noticed that there was a leaky water sprinkler in my walk-in closet. I have told management about this SEVERAL times and the issue has yet to be resolved. On 11/17 I was in my closet and was getting my luggage for a vacation in Sedona. My luggage was sopping wet & FULL OF MOLD I have told management about this several times and they claim they have told maintenance but now my walk-in closet looks like something from a movie! There is MOLD everywhere on the walls, on the ceiling, on clothes and my luggage. In addition to the mold, there are gnats because of the stagnant water. The apartment STINKS to high heaven because of the mold that grows larger on a daily basis. I have had to move out and stay with a friend because of the black mold infestation! When I would stay at my apartment I would feel nauseous, feel fatigued, have headaches, ache all over and have asthma attacks. On top of the leaking pipe issue, the grounds are over watered, causing pools of water to develop which are prime breeding grounds for pests & bugs. Other than the issues listed here, the place is quiet! But please take my advice: DO NOT RENT HERE If you do, take a black light to shine on the walls & carpet. If the carpet/walls glow a 'yellow' color then there is MOLD

author: ArizonaNewby
review_text: I lived at Pinnacle Grove during 2001 through 2002. As a new resident to Arizona, I found the apartment to be great. The staff were very hospitable and professional. However, during the middle of 2002, a new staff and management took over and the apartment complex turned horrible. Several less than desirable tenants moved in and the complex became very trashy. My new neighbors were always fighting with each other and one ended up in a horrible bloody fist fight right outside my door. I moved out about a month later because I was scared to live there. The staff was unresponsive and after numerous complaints from other tenants, the situation ceased to resolve. Luckily none of my belongings were destroyed and I received my full deposit back.

I pay twice as much for an appartment here than back home but it is 200 sq ft larger, AND I have a patio so I'm not complaining! :o) I would recomend Pinnacle Grove if you are looking for a place where you can get on your feet financially.

review_text: I would not recommend this apartment complex at all. I have been to my share of apartments and I have lived at this apartment complex.
