But here are the logistics of Pinnacle Grove: The apartments are nice inside but noise is very loud and you can hear your neighbors all too well and you have to pay for covered parking $15/month. The grounds are poorly upkept and there is no grass and mostly muddy and there is always tree debris over the complex and they use a lot of the leaf blowers early in the morning so not a place to sleep in. The maintenance is not as good as well. They will do simple stuff but if its a big project they will just do a quick fix and not do a proper job. For the bigger projects like fixing the back of a crumbling toliet tank it will take about a month to fix or they wont bother with it unless it starts flooding and then it becomes an emergency. A lot of lower-class people live here and are very noisy. The staff can be friendly sometimes but they do get a lot of temps who don't really care about their job and aren't very helpful. For apartments I would recommend 909 West. The apartment complex next door to Pinnacle Grove or The Palms on Scottsdale. The Pinnacle Grove is by Bridge Management and they don't do the best job to keep their residents happy. Well I hope helped. I know apartment hunting can be difficult and sometimes not truthful.

The garbage disposal broke a few times and water went everywhere, but we managed to fix it on our own with the exception of one time they had to call the rooter guy out so he could snake the line. He said its pretty common to find a lot of crap in the lines around apartments because people will run stuff down their garbage disposal thinking its will obliterate anything you stick in it when in fact he stated, "Most common apartment garbage disposals are not able to handle the amount or type of stuff common renters are convinced they can handle." I rarely see the police here and when they are it ́s usually only for a little while and then they are gone. There are tennants that leave garbage in front of their doors, on their porches and balconies and there is an occasional trailer parked in the back. The lighting is poor in the back/south parking lots. It's only a matter of time before someone gets struck by a car speeding through there. The appliances are outdated and need to be replaced. The walls are paper thin. The stairs vibrate into your apartment. There are "special people" that live here and roam around aimlessly. It's some sort of haphazard state-run assisted living program. If you're lucky you get to hear them rant and rave. You'd be even luckier to live near one of them. Overall, I'd have to say your money would be better spent living somewhere else and I cannot wait until my lease is up.

author: Current Resident 251112
review_text: Would not recommend. Grounds not kept up, some maintenance issues, such as locks on pool area gates, seem to never get fixed. Pool area often dirty and hot tub not clean, dog waste everywhere, rules not enforced with residents, parking often a problem.
response_text: We're disappointed to hear that your time at our community has left you displeased. We completely understand your frustration, as we strive to provide a beautiful community for all of our residents to enjoy. We would love a chance to sit down with you and go over any other concerns you may have. Doing a better job at maintaining our pool area and enforcing dog waste pick-up is something we can work on. We hope to speak with you soon and help turn things around.

author: Current Resident 509024
review_text: Initial meet, tour, pricing, communication, and move in were wonderful; I was pleasantly surprised. I received a very warm welcome by Ryan and was put at ease immediately. The grounds were very well maintained, apartment very well accommodated, and every staff member I encountered was super pleasant, professional, and helpful.
response_text: Dear Resident, we appreciate your kind review! We're so happy that we were able to get you situated into your new home, and that you found Elliot's Crossing to be the perfect fit for you. Our team is excited to have you a part of the community and looks forward to providing you with a wonderful living experience!

author: Current Resident 163298
review_text: Do not move here Staff is nice at first, then you need maintenance and it changes. They don't care about their residents and it shows in their work. It's all about the money and definitely not worth half the rent paid. Wish I had Bern warned

author: Current Resident 163179
review_text: The office staff is kind and tried to be helpful, yet they are often short staffed and given few resources (i.e. Enough Maintenance staff). Issues are handled quickly and professionally in all other regards. Complex is overall well kept and looks nice. Safety has increased, but this is not the area to live if this is a major concern.
response_text: Thank you so much for your feedback. We're glad you appreciate our helpful staff and well-kept grounds. Nonetheless, our on-site team would greatly appreciate the opportunity to follow up with you regarding your concerns. Are you free to call or visit our office? Hopefully with your input we can determine what we're doing well and where we can improve. Moving forward, we hope to better your stay.

author: djpitz
review_text: Elliot's Crossing is a nice complex to live in as far as standard apartments go. The landscaping is pleasant and well maintained, featuring many citrus fruit trees and healthy grass lawns. The pool area is looks great. The pool itself is heated and the hot tube usually works perfectly. The complex has many grills that are quite clean. A pet friendly complex there are often dogs being walked around, and disposal are well supplied with bags making cleaning up after your pet simple. The office staff is friendly and seems to genuinely care about residents. Maintenance is prompt, and generally efficient. I would say Elliot's Crossing is a great value for the cost and would recommend it to anyone.

author: jrey25
review_text: I am half way through my second lease and I plan on a third! Very helpful staff, grounds are always clean, apartment maintenance is always quick to respond and fixes the issue the first time, they are very pet friendly, they have pool side BBQ's every few months with prizes such as free rent, free carpet cleaning, and gift certificates. James the apartment manager and his staff are always going out of there way to make the residents happy. I have never seen one roach since I have lived here! The residents are very friendly and the complex is quiet after hours. After kids get out of school there is some noise but the kids are very well behaved on the grounds. I have nothing but good things to say about Pinnacle Grove apartments and there very courteous staff. Thanks for making my apartment a home!

author: Current Resident 394825
review_text:
I lived in this apartment for a year and only left because some friends talked me into moving in with them across town. And everyone is sick of listening to me complain about how much I miss my wonderful old apartment at Elliot's Crossing!

I LOVED my apartment, very nice, clean, I lived in the front of the complex and never had a problem with parking. Despite overlooking the pool noise was never an issue. Management was always helpful and friendly and maintenance responded promptly to problems. I feel I paid very low rent fo the quality that I got.

I can't say enough good things about this place and I would probably move back if I hadn't taken a job in another part of the valley.

author: Current Resident 506227
review_text: They have always been so helpful and so kind and always on top of everything for me. They're extremely professional and get the job done right the first time. Best complex I have ever moved into. Love Elliots crossing
response_text: Dear Resident, we're very happy to have you a part of our community! The team here at Elliot's Crossing is prepared to make your experience with us the best it possibly can be, so don't hesitate to reach out with any comments or feedback. Welcome home!

author: Current Resident 248924
review_text: The office staff was always nice and willing to help. It was a pain sometimes trying to get direct answers or return calls without having to walk into the office and complain again but all in all my time here was pretty ok. The maintenance department was always GREAT!
response_text: We understand if you are not completely satisfied looking back at your time with us. Our office staff is extremely busy and does their best to answer phone calls in a timely manner. We appreciate your feedback and will work on being more responsive in the future. We take pride in our friendly attitude and our willingness to help out our residents. It seems you have moved out, however, we wish you the best in your future endeavors.

author: LeeshaLuv
review_text: If there are maintenance problems give the repair guys time. I had some air conditioning issues at first but after some trial and error that I had to be patient through, I was able to get a new AC unit installed and the air is running great now. Very happy with how things are going!

author: eandj2006
review_text: I have lived at Pinnacle for the last 4 years and my experience has been a good one so far. Even thought I live in one of the older apts, I have never had major problems. When my ac broke down I was offered another apt to sleep in and a brand new unit was put in. I have never seen a roach in my apt or anywhere on the property. The place is quiet and so are the neighbors. The staff enforces pet rules and have prepared a doggy park. True a new staff moved in and what has happened, is that they are a little over whelmed. They have taken on so much in such a short time span. They do need to work on their smiles: Not everyone that enters the office has a complaint. This doesn t mean that they are rude or unfriendly, they just seem apprehensive all the time. Not everyone will be happy; we can t always choose the color of the apt because, we do not own the property. All I can say is that this is a great place to live. JM & EM :):):):):)

author: amaroconversion
review_text: I went into Pinnacle Grove last week and was toured by a really nice girl. I told her about the problems I had with an apartment I had moved into. She was very sympathetic and showed me various floor plans and practically showed me the whole complex. It didn't even feel like I was being toured by a boring/rude leasing agent, she truely cared for my needs and did her best to accommodate me. She got me moved in that same day and the apartment itself is really nice. I had a chance to speak with the manager who is also very nice and professional. I went back in because my garbage disposal wasn't working and the maintenance guy went that same day to fix it. The grounds are always kept so nice as well. I had such a positive experienced that I felt I needed to let people know. Also, don't take these negative reviews to seriously, if someone has a bad experience they're going to find an outlet but the people who have good experiences hardly go out of their way to let people know.

author: Current Resident 654677
review_text: Just recently moved in and so far I love it. The one bedrooms have plenty of space and storage. The community is quiet and everyone seems nice. Wish they had more covered parking and we're closer to the building I stay in.
response_text: We are so happy to hear that you are loving your new home! It is a true honor to have you in our community. Thank you for your review and please feel free to reach out if you should need anything at all. Welcome home!

author: Current Resident 161045
review_text: The community has gone downhill since the recent merger with pinnacle grove. Some of the new staff members have no idea what they're doing. If I have to visit the office I pray that Ryan is working, he's always friendly and knowledgeable. My upstairs neighbors are incredibly loud. They constantly blast their stereo and television, sometimes until midnight. They must smoke a pack of cigarettes a day because you can hear the opening and slamming of their patio door every hour in addition to smelling the smoke drifting down to my apartment if I have the backdoor open. The apartment itself is pretty nice and a good size. The grounds are maintained well however, I could do without someone waking me up with a leaf blower at the crack of dawn. The pool and grilling area looks great. I wish the pool hours were still enforced. It's very noisy and people will swim until the early hours of the morning. I always have to watch for broken glass around the pool gate when I take my dog out because people can't seem to hold onto their beer bottles. I would still recommend the apartments to a friend.

author: Current Resident 653586
review_text: Overall the apartment appearance and the overall atmosphere is family-friendly and pretty nice. It has a pool and a few playground areas. My overall apartment experience has been somewhat negative though. Within the first few days of moving in I encountered two rather large roaches. After those were elminated and the apartment put some bate in my apartment, the cockroaches left basically permanently. A few months later though I had termites in one wall that the apartment did treat I think but I am not exactly sure how. I also had to deal with a rather large rat in my apartment which I killed myself with a trap I bought myself that same night. I went and showed the office a picture of it. I have also had some plumbing issues. The sink has issues with water falling back "into" the dishwasher causing it to pool and fester if you don't run the dishwasher. Also sometimes when turning on the bathtub the water turns black upon initial turn on and clears up shortly after. Overall I feel like I have spent too much money for how small and for what issues I have had. Interactions with the staff at the office have been good though, and they have always been friendly and accomodating as they possibly can be. And maintenance staff has come and done some repairs whenever requested so I can't complain there at all.
response_text: Hi there, it's wonderful to hear from you! Thank you for your compliments of our wonderful community. It is important that we provide you with the utmost comfort in your home and we would like to connect with you regarding the pest control option that we have for our residents. When you have a moment, please stop by our office so we can schedule the best time for us to assist you. Thank you for your review and we are honored to have you here at Elliot's Crossing!

author: Current Resident 160394
review_text: It has been great. A quiet community- my time here has been undisturbed and peaceful- not much more I can ask for. As soon as the new staff came in, the community seemed to run much more efficiently. What little problems I did have were always resolved quickly.

author: Current Resident 70002
review_text: I moved into Elliot's Crossing Apartment Homes in 2001, after moving to Arizona from the midwest. I was impressed by the lush landscape, because it reminded me of home. I lived at Elliot's Crossing for four years and loved the community so much. I moved from there to be closer to my job and try to save some gas money. Since then, I lived at two other communities and have never had the level of customer service that I experienced at Elliot's Crossing. Last month, I made the decision to move back and to my surprise, many of the original office staff greeted and remembered me when I walked through the door, as well as many familiar residents that still live there. I just thought that was amazing and wanted to share my story. I highly recommend the family atmosphere and the incredible staff at Elliot's Crossing!

author: Current Resident 160317
review_text: Maintenance and office are the best! Tenants are trash that are loud and harass others, background checks are minimal and this is the result. I only had one attempted break in this year and not only will I not renew, I will be breaking my lease next week. There are better places, avoid.

author: Current Resident 50131
review_text: Management doesnt have a clue whats going on. If you go in the office to ask a question you wait around forever before someone will help you like its an incovenience for them to help. And they are always trying to nickle and dime you. The maintenance there are clueless and cant even fix a light bulb. Not to mention the hoodlams they let run around there. Dont live there!

author: Cam2006
review_text: I lived here for a year and the apartment was nice and clean, I didn't have a roach problem, but the rest of the complex sucks. There was two deaths in the apartments while I lived here, one a sexual predator killed himself during a standoff with the police and the second one was a guy who broke in to someone's apartment and the tenant shot and killed him. There is special people walking around, in fact one night around 2:00am one tried to enter my apartment with a key, I didn't know who the hell the person was so I called the police come to find out she lived there but in another apartment and forgot to take her meds. You have to pay for a covered parking space, not a garage but a F$cking parking space. Management is nice until they screw you when your lease is up and you don't want to renew your lease with them. Don't move here, pass up Elliot's Crossing. Move somewhere else PLEASE Now that I'm gone I'm at peace of mind.

author: Current Resident 160130
review_text: Great. I have been here for 5 years. It is a great location. Located near public transportation and many stores and shops. Quiet area, low crime. Generally good neighbors. Pretty property. Will sign another lease.

author: Current Resident 160036
review_text: Maintenance is ill-trained and ill-supervised. They lack knowledge. Work is shoddy. Materials used are crap. No craftsmanship whatsoever. Water sits in my bathtub and on top of my sink because they were installed improperly. Random dips in the floor. Older buildings need more maintenance not more cover-ups.

author: Current Resident 340398
review_text: My husband & I lived here for a little over a year and at the beginning we didnt have any problems but a month after we moved in new management bouth it out; unknown to us. Six months later we got a notice saying that we owed over $900 because we never paid our security deposit and they have been charging us late fees on top of that every month and had not advised us until six months after we were already living there. I tried delaing with the rental office but every time I did i was told to deal with corporate. Corporate then toldus that it was oir resposibility toprove that we paid the security deposit not theirs; if we didnt pay how did we get the keys? went round and round for 2 more months. We ended up have to pay the security deposit again becuase we were trying to transfer. SO then everything got cleared up and our account was at a $0. When we got ready to transfer we were then told that we had to pay over $700 if we wanted to transfer to the other apt on top of the difference in the apartment prices; hence that day we put went out and found a new and much better place. Also the staff in the office doesnt know what they are doing becuase everyone in there will tell you a different story. I wouldnt reccommend this place to anyone unless you like dealing with stress.

author: bobbygarzaaz
review_text: I have lived here for 2 yrs. ever since Richdale took over service in the front office has gone south. I'm getting additional charges for overage on water, I'm usually at the apartment 3 days out of the week at best. Also A/C went out on June 1, 2011, its now June 14th and still not fixed. Manager WILL NOT do anything about it and went I call corporate they refer me to the worthless manager. They are also remodeling the apartments and letting contractors in and out of the apartment as they please and I've been ripped off with over $15, worth of my personal belonging!

author: Current Resident 177220
review_text: It's in a great location-close to just about everything you need! We do get T1 internet connection-just because that's what we ordered from our company. I wish we could get the local channels without having to buy an antennae. The people are friendly..we got a great price on the lease! The only thing wrong is that we turned in a few things before we moved in to get fixed and they said they'd get right on it, but they haven't yet.

author: Current Resident 499740
review_text: This has to be the worse apartment complex I have ever lived at. Apartment wasn't ready on move in day. Staff is very unprofessional. There is no priority on getting maintenance orders done at an adequately time.

author: atltophx
review_text: Moved in not to long ago. The place is OK. There were several problems with the apartment when we moved in and we are still waiting to have them fixed. The place is actually a bit noisy with people yelling and actually barking or there is loud music playing. I was in a hurry and new to the area so I guess it could have been much worse. Office staff is nice but not very informative maybe not that knowledgeable. Was also told that the internet connection was a T1 and turned out to be DSL not very good. I think overpriced for what you get.

author: Current Resident 544834
review_text: Not worth the living the staff and maintenance is not helpful at all. It is very noisy and can hear everything above you and around you. The maintenance is very slow. If I put in a request it will take 2-3 weeks to get your request done and the staff is rude. The assistant manager doesn't know what their doing and just follows what authority tells them and not try to be cooperative. They will charge you extra fees that you didn't even know about and they will never contact you about it. They never contact you when they say they will and they are always short staffed. Every time I go in the office to pick up a package or drop something off I have to wait for 15 minutes and there is a huge line. It is difficult to live here and it is not easy or comfortable living. The staff is not very helpful and just does what the regional manager says. Bridge property is very rude and just wants the money. They don't care if you have problems with your apartment. You signed the lease so you have to deal with it. It is just not peaceful place to live.

author: Current Resident 650459
review_text: The apartment looks really nice with upgraded appliances and cabinets, but that's about it. When I had sewage back up into my kitchen sink and dishwasher, no one came out to take a look because it eventually drained back but not after spilling out over the counter top and on the floor. 3 months of complaints about the upstairs neighbors being loud, walking heavily and sounds of dropping large objects well into the night have not resulted in anything. Tenants still continue with the noise.
response_text: Hi there, It is disappointing to hear that you have experienced issues in your home. It is important that we resolve all maintenance request in a timely manner and we apologize that we have not been able to do this for you and we hope it is not too late to show you how much we truly care. We would like to speak with you about your review and develop a plan to improve your comfort. When you have a moment, contact our community manager at rfrausto@bridgepm.com. Thank you for your time and we hope to speak with you soon.

author: Current Resident 158590
review_text: This is my 2nd year here and the office staff has always been very nice and helpful. The grounds are well kept with lots of plant and citrus trees. Ryan Paulson is one of the best agents in the office, always goes out of his way to assist. It would take a big change for me to move.
response_text: Thank you for your five-star review and continued loyalty to Elliot's Crossing! We're happy you have been satisfied with our customer service and your home. We're glad you are proud to call this community home and we hope to keep you content for some time to come. Again, we appreciate your review and don't hesitate to stop by the office if you ever have questions or concerns.

author: Current Resident 158472
review_text: Over all is been placent and secure. In the past have son misunderstanding with management. I'M very ha y with the new staff also the person i first sign my contract with he's still very nice and 100% good customer service. Thank you. Nice new play area.
response_text: Thank you for your recommendation of Elliot's Crossing. We appreciate your feedback, especially since we can use it to improve the community. As for our staff, we're happy that your experience with communication has improved and resulted in a more positive impression. Again, thanks for your review and if you have any further questions, stop by the front office.

author: Current Resident 158204
review_text: I love living in this community. The staff are very friendly and helpful, the grounds are always clean and the residents all have a sense of pride for where we live. I don't have any complaints at all. I have lived here over a year and was happy to renew my lease.

author: Current Resident 122003
review_text: Wanted to review elliots crossing after my second year here. I have not had any major issues to report, just minor things here and there - nothing I haven t come to expect after 10 years living in apartments. Unlike a couple reviews before me, I do think Tyler is doing a decent job, although he could probably use some extra help. He seems too busy for his own good sometimes. MY apartment is nice and has been since I moved in. The price is good for the amount of space and I get to look out at the pool from my balcony. I think management knows some things that would make this property better; hopefully they make some changes and stop focusing on attracting the new renters, but keeping us current, paying residents here and happy.

author: nicole1979
review_text: I moved into these apartments in June of '06. I liked them until new management took over. Since Greystar Management began running things there have been nothing but problems. Maintenance doesn't fix anything. While they were redoing the apartment above mine, they left a hose running overnight. I was out of town and came back to find my bathroom flooded. It took two weeks for them to fix it and they didn't do it correctly. They actually plastered over the vent in the celing where the leak came from. This is causing a serious mildew issue because there is no ventalation. That was back in March and they have yet to fix their error. The AC unit broke down and it took them 2 days to fix it. Mind you it was 106 outside. The hot tub is almost always broken as well. Due to the leak, I have had to deal with the staff on a fairly regular basis. They really couldn't care less. One of the staff, a girl by the name of , told me that they would fix it when they got to it. She is very rude and unprofessional on a daily basis. They often lock up early and are just generally unaccomadating. They could be really nice apartments if they were under different management. My suggestion is to skip over this place until a new crew is running the show.

author: Current Resident 101605
review_text: I must say the woman who works in the office is RUDE, Jenelle! How are you ever suppose to keep tenants here with her horrible attitude and approach towards others? She has no respect for others and treats people like crap around here. She acts as if she owns this place. The last I checked Tyler was the manager! I'm sorry, but as long as she is an employee here at Elliot's Crossing, the residents will continue to treat her as the way she treats them! That is like sh#* We'd much rather have her replacement stay than have Jenelle back! So much nicer not having Jenelle around!

author: Current Resident 495958
review_text: Not gated community, not handicap parking friendly. Pool can use cleaning water is not clear. Had plumming issue first couple days and eventually had a pool of wayer in my kitchen a week later. Overall satisfied.
response_text: Dear Resident, although we're happy to hear that you're having an overall satisfied experience at our community, we'd love for you to visit our office to talk about your concerns in more detail.

author: Current Resident 664521
review_text: When I first moved in here,the place was beautiful. The office staff was very friendly, and always went out of their way to help me. Maintenance was EXCELLENT!! They always came right away, and they always asked if there was anything else that I needed. They even left lollipops! The grounds were immaculate, and they kept the pool heated really nice all winter long. It has recently changed hands, and the new owners are CHEAP, and the first thing that they want to do is raise the rent. They got rid of the wonderful office staff, and they fired most of the old maintenance guys. The next thing that they did was to shut off the pool heater. Now, the new maintenance staff that they have is either unwilling or unable to fix problems, and it takes them DAYS to get here. The grounds are full of litter, and the office staff either doesn't know or doesn't care. I will be looking for a diffent place. That is too bad. It use to be nice.

author: Current Resident 493516
review_text: My apartment was not ready when I wanted to move in. I came from out of town so that was frustrating I could tell they quickly finished what they could do I could move in. I was told only some have microwaves and mine didn't , which feels unfair. Neighborhood is quiet. Close to the freeway.
response_text: Dear Resident, we appreciate you taking the time to share your thoughts. We're excited to have you as a resident and hope we have the opportunity to address some of the mentioned concerns. Please visit our office when you have a chance, we look forward to improving your experience at our community.

author: Current Resident 855282
review_text: We have lived at Pinnacle Grove for six months. Bridge Property Management took over the property shortly after we moved in. There have been many recent upgrades to the property such as a pool renovation, new dog park (which appears to be popular with the residents), new exterior paint, recently planted flowerbeds/desert landscaping, and repaired/replaced complex lighting to name a few. As to be expected with any change, not all aspects of the transition have been smooth but there have been many nice changes at the property. I suspect that the reviews of this property will continue to improve as other improvements are completed. Positives of the community are that some really nice people live here (we have some great neighbors), the units themselves are large and have a lot of storage compared to some of the neighboring properties; we especially like the in-unit washer/dryer and ceiling fans. We toured some of the neighboring properties and found Pinnacle Grove to be a good value in terms of rental cost in relation to included amenities/apt. square footage. Plus, the location is centrally located to many valley fun spots.

author: Current Resident 241232
review_text: Elliot's Crossing Apartment is located at very useful ad efficient spot. It's close to mall, grocery, Costco, Wal-Mart, School, Business District, and Sport centers. The people from leasing office are so friendly and helpful. Quiet place as well.
response_text: Thank you for writing us this positive review of Elliot's Crossing! It is a joy to read that you are enjoying our convenient and peaceful location, and our kind office staff. Not only do we strive to be kind but professional as well. We hope these aspects of our community continue to benefit you during your stay. Don't be afraid to stop by the office if you ever need assistance with something.

author: Current Resident 155705
review_text: Love my home. Concerns always addressed in a timely fashion. Office staff delightful and go out of their way to please. The only thing that has gone unanswered is the lack of landscaping outside my home. I have not mentioned this before but the trash area is almost always overflowing.
response_text: Thank you for your four-star rating of Elliot's Crossing Apartments. We appreciate the kind words about our attentive office staff that goes above and beyond to please our residents. We hope that this will continue to happen and would love to hear any suggestions you may have about landscaping. We will look into getting the trash area cleaned up so our community looks nice and beautiful for you. Please feel free to discuss any concerns in more detail by seeing us in the office.

author: Current Resident 155677
review_text: I moved here right after they bought Pinnacle Grove property, so the transition was a little rough, but I do recommend it here. The office staff are friendly & professional but the communication b/w maintenance & office needs improvement.

author: Current Resident 21470
review_text: This is the worst possible place you could live in the entire Phoenix area. My apartment has been broken into not once not twice but FOUR times in the past few months. My roommate and dear friend was also robbed at gunpoint in one of the back buildings. Management is all but concerned. Maintenance is always too busy fingering their own s to ever get anything done, and when they do show up, its always during some inconvenient time in the morning, like when you're trying to sleep off your hangover. Our garbage disposal had been broken since we moved in and it smells godawful unholy. I have talked to maintenance countless times, and my kitchen smelled like a filthy . It took them THREE MONTHS to replace that, and it took nearly a month of nagging to get them to install a ceiling fan. They tell me that they would like to make the Elliot's Crossing my home. In the email they sent me, they said "Our aim is to provide you with outstanding service and we would like to hear about your experience with us." Well I would like to say " YOU" because that's a crock full of . They can bite me. Richdale Group has so many residents that they just don't and can't care about the condition of the apartments, the goings on about the complex, and the satisfaction of the resident. They make up for this by sending out inane satisfaction surveys that they will never read. All they care about is that the rent checks keep coming in. On that note, their late fee is absolutely absurd. Elliot's Crossing has a $25/day late fee at their apartment, and those mother outright will charge you. They can shove it up their . Their employees hide these facts behind a cheerful facade of a pleasant living community, they will offer you one thing but when you go to sign your lease it will be something completly else. The b s that work here have the worst attitude, especially Janelle. And the layout of the apartments is very awkward, both in the respects of arranging furniture and fitting people comfortably. And don't expect to get cell reception anywhere. And I mean ANYWHERE. I thought it was just inside no, its outside, too. I'm pretty sure my upstairs neighbor is a 400-pound tap dancer, but that's just my luck. If you ever have a problem with another apartment concerning noise, etc, management says the same thing every time: "call the cops." Not only is this a waste of time for the police who could be out doing their jobs (writing speeding tickets for five over), but it is also a waste of time for you, because it never settles anything. It goes without saying there's like an entire squad here 24/7, yet I still don't feel safe. Also people will park in your PAID parking spot and it is not enforced like they claim. I've called and the towing company says they might drive by in a few hours. The apartments themselves are horrible. They're dark and gloomy. Every time I walk inside, I feel like I'm walking into a catacomb. My apartment was trashed when I first got here. The carpet looks like someone wiped their all over it, and there's an obvious hookah accident right in the middle of the living room. The repairs on the drywall look like they hired a limbless to do it, and I wouldn't be surprised. In a satisfaction survey, they asked me how they could improve the Elliot's Crossing. I responded with: I suggest that you BURN IT TO THE GROUND. Or, relinquish the title of the complex to Michael Jackson so he can have Neverland Ranch Phase II in Arizona. The raping of innocent children under the guise of a theme park would be better than letting Elliot's Crossing operate as it does now. I would rather see those buildings used as a covert communist outpost, a concentration camp for minorities, or a slaughterhouse for cute and fuzzy animals. In short, the living experience at the Crossings is less pleasant than sodomy and mass genocide combined. THEY couldn't pay ME to live here for another day. I hope the entirety of The Richdale Group goes under and all of its owners and employees are left jobless, homeless, and utterly miserable, so they can know how their tenants feel. The price we pay gets us here. They don't even spend our money on worthwhile things. Instead of upgrading the hardware or replacing the carpets, they paint the exterior, build a model apartment in the front of the the complex to make it look better than it really is. Do Not Rent Here

author: Current Resident 137834
review_text: I moved from Garden Grove Apartments (basically across the street) to Elliot's Crossing after Garden Grove raised my rent to New York levels. For basically the same apartment, I paid 2/3 of what Garden Grove charged, but got a much nicer staff, better neighbors, and a less broken-down apartment. Although I can hear almost everything that my upstairs neighbors do, they're not particularly noisy people and have never caused trouble at night. This apartment is far enough from ASU so that you aren't living with a bunch of young college students, but close enough to stores, the highway, and several local gyms. I did not move out because of the apartment or the community, but because work relocated me. I have seen the security company roaming the parking lots at night, and have never encountered any safety issues. I definitely recommend this apartment complex.

author: jtrent
review_text: As i sit by the pool on this fine 100 degree (spring?) day, I just can't fight back the urge to log onto apartmentratings.com and write a review! It got a tad worse before they figured it all out. I was glad to see they decided to keep Tyler as he is the only reason this place stayed in one piece. The pool is nice. author: Current Resident 227704
review_text: My dryer was not working, I tried all settings and it could not fully dry a half load of clothing. I opened a ticket online. I received no response until I called in a full week later. I'm told somebody will come by on either Friday or Sunday. So A guy comes by on Sunday to tell me they need a part and nothing gets fixed and the supervisor would be there first thing on Monday. Monday comes and goes I get home from work and nobody has come by, I call the office and I'm told a halfhearted sorry and they say they'll have somebody come by first thing the next day. A guy comes by sometime midday and cleans out the lint trap and tells me its working. It does not work still. At this point I email Bridge corporate and I get called by Tyler who promises me everything will be fixed and they'll have a guy there first thing in the morning to fix it. I take a day off so I can be there to make sure it gets taken care of. Nobody shows up I get a call at around three telling me that they can't come over and they'll be there tomorrow. They find a problem with the vent and that doesn't resolve it so they replace the dryer. More than 14 days have now passed I'm legally allowed to call a third party and have them fix it but I continue to work with the site maintenance. I run the new dryer on the 'Timed Automatic' setting with a towel and three shirts. It takes four cycles to dry the towel completely. At this point I'm told that I should use the onsite laundry and I will be reimbursed for any money I put on a laundry card. I put 10 dollars on the card and I'm told that they will reimburse me for the that and 'some extra reimbursement for all the trouble I've had' I am considering breaking my lease at this point because I have had this apartment for less than a month, but the promise of making it right with credits to my account actually makes me feel a lot better. They have another guy come in and it turns out the "timed Automatic" setting does not seem to work as advertised, however the regular timed mode works so I can dry my clothing. I had tried this setting on the first dryer BEFORE I submitted a maintenance request and it did not work so I assumed this one had the same issue. Now weeks later I get my monthly charges and No credits have been applied to my account. This is just a stream of broken promises that really set a negative precedent for the rest of my time here.
response_text: We'd like to begin by apologizing for your negative experience. It is always our goal to offer a painless and easy living experience and we're sorry that wasn't your impression. Due to the extensive nature of your concerns, we feel as though it'd be better if we discuss issues in person. During this time, we sincerely believe we can immediately begin improving the community for you and all residents. Thank you for your feedback.

review_text: The management is quite unhelpful. Although they look professional, whenever you need them to do anything, they turn into rude unprofessionals- especially the guy. And they are sneaky about nickel-n-diming. Please please read the lease completely before signing it. and don't expect any help from management.

author: Current Resident 805408
review_text: I only moved from this apartment complex because I moved out of state. I am now getting ready to move back into Arizona so am looking at apartment ratings and was shocked to see all the bad things about this complex. I would definitely move back in here except my new job is on the west side of the valley and am trying to get close to that. We lived here for 2 years and really enjoyed it. We did have an issue with the a/c breaking in the summer but they were very quick to fix it (less than 24 hours). I did see a couple vehicles get broken into but that is not the apartment complex's fault. Of course you can hear your neighbors sometimes but that is part of living in an apartment. If you do not want to hear noise either rent or buy a house. I was sad that I had to move out of here.

author: Current Resident 756380
review_text: The entire move in process was a horrible experience! First, they made false claims on my background report, stating I did not qualify due to a felony appearing on my report. After going back and fourth for a week with them, and TransUnion, it was finally corrected to reflect it was incorrect . Not once did the property management apologize for any inconvenience, and time wasted. Secondly, the apartment was not ready for the original move in date that was set in place by Elliot's Crossing. My partner and I had already given our notice to vacate to our current landlord, but had to push that out 2 weeks since the new apartment wasn't going to be ready for the initial move in date. Once again, no empathy or understanding of our frustration. Once the 2nd move date came, the apartment was still not ready until later on that same day. The "cleaning" & last minute "repairs" did not take place until the day of move in. Once we did the walk through, we found the apartment dirty, with leaks, restroom floorboards coming off, stove burners not working, & the kitchen countertops were completely mismatched. When questioned about the countertops, they advised us the contractors had broken them accidentally so they needed to place something there temporarily. Not once, did they give us a heads up of this when we went to pick up the keys for the walk through. Makes me truly believe they never intended to tell us, or swap them out to match, but only did because we complained and brought it to their attention. It was never offered by them to have the apartment cleaned out again, only to fix the repairs since we advised them we needed them fixed since it was unacceptable that they had 2 weeks to get the apartment ready since it wasn't done on the original move in date. There are still little things here and there that need to be fixed, and it's only been 1 week since we've lived here. It's been a nightmare! When we should've been happy and ecstatic to be getting a new place, It's been the opposite. If it wasn't for us not having the time to look for another place, and due to Covid19 with apartments no longer doing walk throughs, we wouldn't have moved in here. It's why we only did a 6 month lease, and are trying to make the best of the entire situation.

author: Current Resident 934362
review_text: Okay, so full disclosure, I just signed my second year with Elliot's Crossing and think you should hear what it is like here, both the pros and the cons. First off, the grounds are very well kept. Currently, they are remodeling a lot of apts to add a washer and dyer so some areas are under construction. At least they are trying to add value to the property. The reviews of the office staff are mainly true. I never really have an issue with them as I pay my rent on time, and typically just don't go in the office. However, the one time i had an issue, i went to the office to speak with them about it. They could do nothing. I needed to contact corporate to have a basic problem solved. This seemed like a bit of a pain, given i was looking at someone i thought could help me. I mean, they can take my money, but can't help me? Come on The apartments: They are in good shape. Nothing fancy, by any stretch, but they are nice. I really like my one bedroom. They are currently raising the rents on all apartments and we are seeing a mass exit of some really great people. I just don't understand (outside of greed) why you would raise a single income families rent on a small 2 bedroom $180/mo in this economy. The community: LIke all complexes, you have the trash, but you also have some great people. I have made new friends that i will have for life in this complex and we all enjoy the pool in the warmer months. I feel safe at night, and am close to what i need. My advice: Understand that this place is a business, not a charity. Their job in the front is to sell you an apartment, nothing more. TO the person that was upset about them asking his monthly payment requirements well yea jackass, i wouldn't want to spend my time with you if you can't afford the apartment either. It is called qualifying, it is sales 101, read a book. I hope the folks that own this complex now don't continue to up rent on everyone. The apartment i am in is perfect for what i pay, but to add $100/mo to it would just be silly. The market value in the area may be more, but those complexes are newer and much nicer know your limitations and keep your current tenants happy. Anyway, check out the complex, it really is a good place to live in Tempe Hope to see ya around the pool.

author: Former Resident 33759
review_text: I've lived in several apartments since college and this is by far the worst experience I've had in my life. Maintenance has been great here, but management needs considerable work. I complained for over 3 months about my loud downstairs neighbor to management, but unfortunately the issue was never resolved. I had a meeting with the property manager of the apartment complex, Rosanne, but she told me that they need evidence of the loud neighbor in order for them to take legal action against them. Management waited over 3 months to tell me they couldn't do anything about the issue without evidence. There's definitely a lack of communication with their residents. I can't even count the number of times I've emailed the apartment office, but they completely ignored/disregarded my messages. Not only does this demonstrate indifference, but it's unprofessional as well. This is not management's only shortcoming. They deceived me on multiple occasions in the office. I never received a fitness center key when I moved in, so I went down to the office to request a key. The lady down at the office told me the assistant manager, Trystan, would be making more keys and they would be sending out a mass email to residents. Well, that never happened. Also, I went down to the office to complain about my loud neighbor in person and they told me they would be taking legal action against them. Again, this is another lie the office artificially created for me to leave them alone. I believe this apartment complex is extremely unfit for the job of caring for their residents. They're basically managing two apartment complexes in one, but they won't hire more staff. I finally gave up with this apartment complex and broke my lease contract. They tried convincing me to transfer to another unit, but they wanted to raise my rent to close to $1 . I was happy with paying $858, but I couldn't put up with that irritating neighbor any longer. It was already an inconvenience for me to have to move all of my stuff into another apartment, but they wanted to charge me extra rent as well. This apartment complex simply isn't worth your time and money. You would have a better experience paying just a little bit more for a higher end complex. I moved out of this apartment complex on February 15th 2020. I received my final move out statement from Elliot's Crossing in the mail 3 weeks later. They're now trying to nickel and dime me for anything they thought wasn't absolutely perfect in my apartment. I'm being charged for them to retouch up the paint in my apartment even though I thought it was fine. I don't have any children or pets. Here's my advice. Take many pictures of the apartment on move-in day. Take time filling out the move-in damage paperwork. Insist upon a walkthrough of the apartment with management on move-out day. Also, take a lot of pictures of the apartment's condition on move-out day. This may help when they have exaggerated claims of damages to the apartment. Believe me, they will try to chisel you out of all the money you have. I gave a 60 day notice that I was moving. I paid 2 months base rent (approximately $1750) to break the lease. I had to forfeit a $99 non-refundable deposit. They charged me an additional $273 on move-out for shampooing the bedroom carpet (the only room that was carpeted), touch up paint and clean up. I've never had to pay this much on move-out before. I left the apartment absolutely spotless. I strongly believe that had I given them the standard $500 deposit, they would have invented $500 worth of move out costs. Keep in mind, I lived in this complex for 5 and a half months. In total, I spent in excess of $2 getting out of this dump.
response_text: Dear Resident, we were sorry to read your review of our community. Even though you are no longer a resident with us, we appreciate any and all feedback you may have. We wish you all the best in your future endeavors.

author: ubermonkey
review_text: I've lived here since 2007 so I've seen a lot of change over the years! First let me hit a few of the good things: 1. Super convenient - nearby are Walmart, Safeway, CVS, QT, Circle K, Arby's, BK, McDonald's, Wendy's, Panda Exp, Subway, Starbucks, Fuddruckers, Taco Bell, Red Robin, Sonic, Popeye's, Oregano's and even more food joints. There's also a Costco and one of those car wash/oil change megaplex things. AND access to the I-10 AND the 60 less than 3 miles away. 2. Nice grills, gym, decent pool (not Olympic but it's clean and usable), onsite laundry and 'business office' with computers - and a clubhouse which has a pool table -honestly the clubhouse is not really the kind you'd rent out for a party or anything but I'm not sure how important that is for most people 3. Enough parking so you don't have to park on the street, ever. 4. In the 11 years I've been here I've seen a handful of police related calls. Put hundreds of people from everywhere together and incidents will happen but I've seen less of that here than anywhere else. My car has never been broken in to, and the grounds are well lit. Now, let me give you the low down that might speak to a few of the issues I've seen other reviewers mention: Friendliness of office staff - seriously I have never had them be rude to me. That's probably because I've worked customer service and I realize that every apt staff has more to do than they can handle so I'm patient and nice. That's my big secret. I stand in line a little longer or sometimes even have to come back the next day..but when I have a really big issue and raise my voice a bit they know it's out of character and they help me out (and in the course of 11 years everyone will have something happen!) Stuff breaking down - well yeah talk to a home owner, stuff breaks. Take care of your apt as much as you can; don't treat it like a rental car (in fact don't treat your rental cars like a rental either will ya?!? It's wasteful.) Want it fixed? Go to the office and be nice; being a tenant doesn't give you the right to treat the employees like minions. Bugs - I've lived all over the US, most recently in New Orleans, the roach capital of the US, so I feel qualified to talk about this. First I live on the top floor, honestly that helps a lot. But I've seen two cockroaches and one silverfish since 2007 (that's 11 years!) Here's the deal; don't leave dirty dishes or half full beverages around, and if you have a pet clean it's litter box or pick up it's poo and take it to the dumpster. It's really that simple. Speaking of dog owner who let their dogs go everywhere and don't clean it up that irritates me a lot! The apt complex has put pet trash cans with plastic bag dispensers all over and there's also a couple dog parks and somehow people are still so lazy they let their dogs go and don't clean it up - even though they're 20' from the can I don't know how that's the apartment's fault..they've got the lawn service out there several times a week! It's probably a little unfair of me to say this but I seriously think some folks must be used to living with their parents and being catered to It's like they think since they're paying everything should be taken care of without any effort on their part and it should be done instantly. People like this are the same ones who don't pick up after their dogs or clean up after themselves after using the grills can't say I'm sad when they move out ;) If that sounds harsh, please feel free to skip living here - if you're one of the good ones who don't think all that's unreasonable - welcome, it's a great place!

author: Current Resident 335850
review_text: Do yourself a favor and just don't move here. My problems started immediately upon moving in. My apartment was NOT move in ready- there was a cabinet completely hanging off its hinge, one of the window screens had fallen off and was just sitting on the patio, and the apartment was dirty. The doors barely opened and closed because of the built up paint, and the deadbolt did not work. There was also no washer and dryer, which was the only reason I had picked this complex over several others I had been to. The management apologized, and said everything would be fixed asap and I would have my washer and dryer within the week. Thankfully most of it was fixed promptly (new locks were put on the door, new window screen, fixed the cabinet). However I did not get my washer and dryer for THREE MONTHS! Not only that, but I was blatantly lied to by the employees in the office, who told me each time I'd call (at least once a week), that they were getting the new washers and dryers in within the next week. That was until I got someone new on the phone, who finally told me that there was a waiting list, and it would be at LEAST another month and a half before I received my washer and dryer. I was not told this before or during my move in. About a week after I moved in, the paint, or whatever substance that they had used to paint the bathtub (yes they PAINTED the bathtub) started to flake off, clogging my tub drain, and revealing two huge disgusting dark brown circles about 6 in in diameter each on the bottom of the tub. Despite using bleach to try and clean these spots, they were obviously stained into the tub. I cannot even describe how disgusting the bottom of the tub looked- it was obvious why they had attempted to paint it. When I reported this to management, they said that I would not be charged for the dirty spots upon moving out because I had reported them right away (?!?!), and there was nothing they were going to do because it was normal wear and tear. Needless to say I never took a bath in that tub. The BEST part about my experience at Elliot's Crossing was the certified eviction notification I received from their corporate office a month after moving in, stating that if I did not pay over $800 in late fees, that I would be evicted 5 days after the letter was dated (which happened to be the very next day). I had paid my rent and all fees on time, so had no idea what this letter was regarding. But since they were supposedly going to evict me the next day, I panicked. I called the contact # at the corporate office multiple times with no answer, and when no one had called me back 2 hours later, I left work and went to the management office. After looking into the issue, they had apparently not applied my move-in discount. The girl in the front office barely batted an eyelash at the situation like it was no big deal! After ALL of this, I called their corporate office to voice my frustration. I asked to be compensated for the three months I was without the washer and dryer I was paying for (and for having to pay to wash my clothes at a laundry facility), and the few hours that I had to miss work to deal with their "oops" eviction notice. Their "resident relations specialist" was possibly one of the rudest people I have ever spoken to. She decided to point out to me that there is no separate charge for the washers and dryers (good to know that Elliot's Crossing gives people free w/ds! Good thing the residents don't have to pay for them!), that it was my decision to take my laundry off-site (because doing laundry is a choice?!), and, my personal favorite, "Our letter didn't tell you to leave work and drive down to our office." I was speechless. But good news! After mentioning my frustration with my experience to one of the new front office girls while picking up a package, she offered me a free parking spot (have I mentioned the parking lot off of Grove Parkway sucks? Good luck getting one of the 10 open spots ). One month after receiving this free parking spot, a notice for a failure to pay for this spot was posted to my door, along with the late fees I was going to be charged if they did not receive payment Needless to say, I submitted my notice to move out over two months early. With glee.

review_text: When I moved into this apartment I was so excited and couldn't wait to move into my luxury apartment in a gated community or so I thought . author: Former Resident 634745
review_text: DO NOT RENT. JUST DONT. As if this apartment complex needs another terrible review to prove a point. But I just have to. In hopes that this will help prevent someone else from going through what me and my family did. The last management company was great! However, preffered apartment communities is certainly not "preffered". There was issue after issue the minute they took over. Additional fees were added to rent every month with no explanation of what they were. I reached out to the office several times with no response, leaving me to pay them anyways so I wasn't charged $100/day for a late fee in hopes they'd reach out to me eventually. Once I confronted them with the issue they were entirely unhelpful. Weren't knowledgeable at all about the fees I was talking about. Later, (I'm assuming) after many complaints, they sent out an email stating it was state taxes. Interesting that I never saw those fees from the last management company. The app for payment has constant issues and was extremely vague about the fees and payment details. The app was always crashing and just an absolute pain to use. Trash valet is charged every month even though trash is rarely picked up. I'd prefer to not have my trash sitting on my porch for 3 days. Thanks though. Maintenance is ridiculously slow. Didn't have a working dishwasher for 3 weeks. In the midst of trying to get it fixed. I set up an appointment with them anytime after 12pm, so i could be present (i have a dog). Waited at my apartment all day only for them to not show up. I went to the office the next day for them to tell me that they had shown up earlier yesterday morning and it was signed off around 10:30am. Which would've been impossible because my dog was left out, not to mention he shouldn't have shown up at my apartment before 12pm. I go back to the apartment and nothing had been fixed. (Which i already knew) i confronted them about that and they tried to set up another appointment. Communication is so infrequent form the front desk staff that its hard to accommodate anything. Good luck moving out! It's a show. No one knows what's expected. Every person tells you something different. And they charge you for whatever they feel like and have "no control over changing it" so don't bother trying to argue any of the charges apparently. I asked for proof of "paint damages" several times and they never provided me pictures. It's expected that you fill the holes and paint them to avoid charges. It was listed on the move out paper that i received a month prior to move out. As well as "contact the front desk for paint codes" But then I'm told after being charged $150 for painting that there's just a "blanket painting" fee. Would've been nice to know. And almost in the same breathe he says " we don't require our residents to paint and we don't have paint codes". Every single person contradicts the other in this place. It's extremely frustrating. Wish I would've gotten the name of the lady I dealt with frequently but she was snarky and always had an attitude. They have absolutely no concern for you as a resident or a person. Thankfully I am all moved out now! Still dealing with the move out hassle. But I can't wait to never have to deal with them again. I absolutely hate conflict and having to be argumentative. But If you're not they will try to screw you out of every penny you have with no concern for you at all. But honestly, if you're reading this. Just save yourself the time, hassle, money, etc. Go find another apartment complex. One thats not managed by PAC!! Greystar was amazing!!

author: Current Resident 299818
review_text: I've never written my own review but I feel compelled to do so when it comes to these apartments.. I normally always read reviews before ever making a decision but in this case I was referred by a friend who's opinion is normally right on point. Don't make the same mistake as me!! Read the reviews anyway!! When we first got here and were given the tour the place looked pretty and I loved the floor model. When we moved in we were overall very happy with the appearance of our unit. We had just got brand new carpets and the bathrooms and kitchen had wood flooring (fake wood but we still liked it better than the lenolium tile). Ill start with the smaller things that really didnt bother me too much but may bother other people. Within a few weeks of living here we notices the problems they had with the water. There's no pressure and both of our toilets clogged up at the same time as well as our kitchen sink. The toilets were an easy fix with a plunger but the sink we had to wait for maintenance who took two days to come.. Again not that big of a deal they came and fixed it but it was frustrating to have to use our bathroom sinks to wash things. For anyone who lives near the pool I am so sorry. It's a 24 hr pool which you would think is a nice ammenity but when your bedroom patio door is facing the pool and there's constantly people partying down there all night.. Not so fun. But again this is minuscule to what I'm about to get into.. However it's a shame that the pool has been closed several times due to people taking a crap in the water or getting glass from their glass beer bottles in the pool. When we first moved in there was a free online rent payment when the management was still udr.. they changed management and now its a $33 fee to pay with a credit card, $10 fee when u pay with a checking account (and this id everytime u pay) or free for automatic payments which is frustrating because not everyone can or wants to do this. Now for the entire reason I'm actually taking the time to write this review.. After being here about 4 months I started noticing that my 1 yr old daughter was getting bit. A lot. I figured its summer and we live by the pool it's probably Mosquitos. But it was strange that I never saw them in my apartment. One day when my fianc was taking out the trash (a mile away from our unit it seems like) there was a couch with the words bed bugs spray painted on it. I had never had a bed bug experience or really ever knew much about them so it's not something I ever would've thought about. But it triggered me to go look at the reviews. Upon typing in "finisterra" the first thing in google I saw said "bed bugs".. Funny though that these are now the only reviews I can find. So this is when I decided to start checking my daughters room and monitoring her bites more. I always check on my kids before I go to bed and one night I went in there and went to adjust her and noticed blood on her sheets and called in her dad to get a second set of eyes. He started moving her sheets to look for more and there it was.. A live bed bug. DISGUSTING!! We immediately pulled her out of her bed and started searching her bed. Along the inside of the lining of her sheet was a group of about 7 bed bugs. We wrapped her sheets up and trashed them killed the one we found and left it for the apartments to see. The next day we noticed out neighbors getting pest treatment. Our apartment is attached to our neighbors at my daughters room. Called the office got the treatment for free which was a nuisance because it consists of bagging and washing a the linens for two full weeks. We got the all clear at the follow up inspection and all seemed calm in the world again. Until now 3 months later and they are back. Only this time the office has informed us that our treatment would be at our own cost. They basically told us we have to prove we are not the source.. Let me tell you.. We didn't have a problem again until our same neighbors were getting their carpets ripped out. But we heard two different stories from the office as to why they were getting ripped out. One said it was for roaches (yep there are roaches here too) and one said because the carpets were thrashed. Here's the thing. With as many reviews online about the bed bugs at this place and the fact they do routine pest inspections here.. They know they're the source. I've had to throw away my bed, and my baby's brand new bassinet to try and help the matter on my own. Now I've decided that I won't live here with my two children and am paying almost $3 to get out of my lease plus what's it's going to cost me to buy all new furniture Do yourself a favor Go somewhere else!

author: Current Resident 836838
review_text: Everything was great for the first four to six months living here. After that things started to decline. CONS:Our next door neighbors got robbed, to confirm this you can see the newscast online by searching "robbery caught on camera by video game" and watch the one with the Asian girl. Then tempe PD woke us up a week later at midnight when I was sick with the flu and made us leave for three hours. A month or so later the office had our buildings painted and the painters broke two of my patio chairs. I left multiple voicemails to the office regarding my broken chairs but heard nothing back ever! I guess they figured my renters insurance would take care of it and they couldn't be bothered. Maintainence took three days to change a light bulb in our kitchen then shortly after the other one went out and we have just dealt with it rather than wait for them again. They also barged into our apartment while I was sleeping, jimmied my LOCKED bedroom door open and demanded that I wake up so they could check my faucet for thirty seconds. No regard for the tenants' property or privacy whatsoever. Waking a tenant up to check a faucet is unacceptable. Wait another hour, make a phone call, come back later but don't break into a locked bedroom with the half naked tenant asleep within and demand to see the faucet. And last but not least the spa has had about a pound of dirt in the bottom of it for the past 10 months and no one has bothered to clean it out. The gates keep breaking and the gate on our end of the complex was broken for six months, causing us to drive to the front end of the complex and exit near the office. When your complex only had two gates, it shouldn't even be an option to let one sit broken for six months. Some PROS: The unique floor plan makes the living room feel huge. The apartment was clean and ready upon move in. The clubhouse and fitness center are always clean and great. The community is USUALLY very quiet though the occasional Indian guy can be heard on his phone at 3am-5am talking to his relatives in Bangladesh or wherever but that's anywhere you go. The grounds are kept quite clean except for the aforementioned dirt in the spa. OVERALL SUMMARY: The unique floor plan and clean grounds make you feel like you've gotten a steal for your money until you have any sort of issue, especially major ones. Management seems only to care about well nothing really. They'll say or do anything for you the first couple of months then they treat you like crap and let their maintenence staff destroy your property and sleep schedule. Community isn't very safe despite the gates as you can tell from the robbery. Overall, the nice-ish apartment is not worth all the hassle and complete lack of respect you will experience living here.

author: Remnika
review_title: Within my 14 month lease with this dread of a complex.
review_text: What originally brought me to moving into this complex was because they have glass-top stove ranges instead of the coiled (easier to clean) and because they have a washer/dryer in every unit. It looked like it was the best in the area that was close to my work. I was completely WRONG. Upon move-in, many of our appliances were broken (bathtub had little to no water pressure and gave freezing cold water, the micro-hood was totaled, and the fridge would leak excessively) and it took maintenance forever to replace or fix them, despite all of my requests. The walkways throughout the complex are VERY easy to slip and trip on (especially if the walkways are wet by the sprinklers). Parking is very crammed, people rarely use the special covered parking because the spaces are too crammed to make at least one side of the car impossible to open the doors to. The streets are too narrow; it's barley enough room for 2 cars going opposite directions to fit onto. Security is okay, but the general neighborhood has several emergency phone calls and during my 14 months here, the area of the complex in which I live has been flooded with cops several times. The walls are whatnot are also very thin. That, or the neighbors are just too big of party people. I personally don't mind loud neighbors, but if you don't like them, I would be cautious. Other than constantly having to have maintenance come out to our apartment, we also had to have our cable company (Cox) come to re-wire out internet/television connection because it was poorly done, causing our cable to constantly become intermittent. About 6 or so months after we moved in, the staff started giving everyone of the tenants notices about a pest infestation (bedbugs/roaches) and how they were going to inspect each of the apartments to see if any of them were infected. Our apartment was conveniently skipped, but our building had a cockroach issue. My family and I are very cleanly, but no matter how clean there would still be roaches coming out of the kitchen sink and whatnot. I called the staff about them missing my apartment, and how we have a cockroach issue that needed to be tended to, and while the staff appeared friendly it took them several months to bring a pest maintenance guy out to even "inspect" the apartment, and now about 2 weeks before we move out, they want to do a fog of the apartment which should have been done months ago. Go figure, they'll wait till the apartment nearly becomes available to make it look as nice as possible for the next poor people to bother signing a lease with this place. The rent is too expensive for poor service, constantly breaking appliances, and for anything else I mentioned in my review. I'm glad I will be leaving this place soon.
