author: Current Resident 896400
review_title: Please RUN don't walk away from these apartments
review_text: I know people read reviews on apartments before moving in or going to see and then think well maybe they are just disgruntled people. Actually what I have read on here for the awful reviews are true, so please believe them when you read them. I lived in these apartments for basically three years. At first the place was great, office people were great and maintenance was AWESOME! Then the changes came. The office people were changed, this happens like clockwork, think we went through about six or more changes while we were there and the property manager was changed. The new manager had not a clue what he was doing, and the new office people didn't seem to get it or have a clue or maybe it was they just didn't care. The maintenance people are shuffled between I think three other complexes trying to keep up with repairs. This is impossible for them to do and you never get the same one after you waited your three weeks to have them come. YEP, three weeks was the last count I heard from one of them (who was smart and left)that they are behind. The office manager that came on board and was the start of the place being destroyed is now working as the maintenance manager, wonder why the maintenance is so bad. Let's move on, the front security gates are usually open pretty much of the time because they are broken most of the time and they don't want to pay for the repairs to them anymore so this allows for anyone to walk in. If they aren't open there's a small wooden gate that anyone can walk through further in the back and that's always open so anyone can get into the complex, so when they say secured it's not. There use to be security officers that were on after 10pm until like 4 or 5am but they got rid of them too. They have ground people that come to mow the lawn like two times a week and they arrive at about 6:15 to 6:30am and start with their loud noise, you can't sleep or even hear yourself think when they start. The pool itself is pretty nasty most of the time,but there are two, that are the same way. They also have a lock to get in and out of the pool, doesn't seem to safe to be locked inside the pool and can't get out. Just my opinion on safety. The fitness room is small and doesn't have a lot of equipment,even less when it's broken which is most of the time. Now let's talk about the apartments themselves, I see others have mentioned the roaches, unfortunately this is true, creeping a long the floor, and they are huge! One of the apartments we had the sliding glass door had no security latch, we asked them to put one on, their response we don't have them in stock anymore so we aren't replacing them, okay, leave us unsafe, sound reasonable doesn't it? When we moved into our first apartment everything was dirty, filthy and stains and holes all over the carpeting, when we moved out we were charged for carpet cleaning. Since then they thought they'd cut costs and some upstairs apartments don't have carpeting, they have tile instead, talk about hearing every move your upstairs neighbors make. We had three kids above us that did nothing but jump, our entire apartment shook, kept letting the office know, they didn't care. We had to have a lot of maintenance done to our apartment which I previously mentioned were three weeks behind, you would put in your request and then instead of them coming they would send you an email stating that the work had been completed when they didn't even come, this was always happening. Then one morning I got out of bed and stepped into a huge puddle on the floor, ended up being a main pipe broke and flooded our two bedrooms and bathroom. It took them awhile to acknowledge the problem and then sent plumbers out to fix it. They never pulled up the carpeting that was all flooded out, talk about smelling moldy. We had people in and out of the apartment for days, and you would think with this that all the work could of been done, they had to tear up some of the bathroom floor and put a huge hole in the bathroom wall, the work still wasn't completed by the time we moved out which was about three weeks or longer later. They did nothing to help the mold smell or anything. This happened in the second apartment, in the first apartment, the neighbors below us complained of squeaky floor board so instead of them giving us our notice maintenance came busting into our apartment immediately giving us no notice, it wasn't like the squeak had just begun and the floor was going to fall down, it had been that way for the 8 months we were in there before that. Anyways, they left and sent someone else to the apartment, I wasn't fully dressed and this guy comes barging into our apartment that wasn't even with the apartment complex, didn't knock or anything, I grabbed a blanket and covered myself, I'm like what are you doing, he said the office called him to come over and fix something, the guy had no idea why he was there or what he was suppose to fix but had the key to open the door and come in without us knowing he was coming or having our approval to enter the apartment. I went directly to the office to find out why they allowed this to happen and of course there was no answer by any of them. Thought I'd let you know these things are happening. There are a lot of pit bulls that live in these apartments and dogs that run around without leashes or without people watching them. I have been jumped on a few times by these dogs. There are also a huge amount of kids. One of my neighbors who has also lived there for a long time made a comment about it becoming a slum place and he said that others have been talking the same way. I actually did mention that to the office and they just brushed it off like don't be silly, but if you take a good look at it and look at the grounds really good before you move in then you might make the same decision. It use to be VERY VERY nice. Also if you use a cell phone be careful where you are moving in these apartments because you may not get signal. We had to live for a year without good signal and was very hard to make or receive calls so just be aware that this complex doesn't pick up signal very well and it's not a cheap cell phone company that we use, it's one of the major ones. Be aware that the office personnel don't know you by name but you are just a number to all of them and same with maintenance. The last thing be careful about payments to them, I sent them a check for the last portion of the move out and some how they are saying they didn't get it and sent me to collections. They didn't even try calling me to let me know they didn't receive it, off to collections I went. I had NEVER missed a rent payment or been late in the three years but off to collections I went. If you can overlook everything else, the apartments themselves aren't to bad as far as square footage but they are VERY expensive and not worth the headache or aggravation that is caused by them and the bad management. Please whatever you decide to do just remember we did try to warn you about this place.

author: ryanmcmullen
review_text: STAY FAR AWAY Dont let the model and flat screens fool you When I rented my unit there was two weeks in between them moving out and me moving in, I asked the staff to please let me know when everything is done so that I can view the apartment and get any concerns addressed before i actually moved it. I mean really and that is just getting me started the patio had 1 's of luges reside dripping from everywhere even on the front porch! EWW! Then I noticed that bathrooms, mold and mildew growing in the grout and around the soap holder in both bathrooms, toilet seat broken in one bath no water pressure at all in either bathroom (which we were told was normal!) it took 45 min to fill up the small tub for a bath. ceiling fans not working, dishwasher was broken, kitchen floor was coming up and splitting in areas, bathroom ceiling not painted after an apparent repair. fridge had water puddling in the veggie bins and the bottom. needless to say it was a huge mess, I reported this all to the office, a week later nothing was done, so i went in an spoke with them and they said that they would send someone out to fix them today, well all I got that day was a tub stopper, the next day they installed a ceiling fan, the next day the maytag repair man came out to say that the dishwasher was broken and not under warrantee. Yet nothing yet has ben addressed about the mold in mildew in the bathroom, I went in to the managers office and issued a complaint her responses were very vague and not taking responsibility for so she came out to the unit and i showed her all of my concerns, with in a couple days they had people working in my unit, first off they re grouted the tubs but didnt remove the mold or mildew, the installed a brand new dishwasher cheapest one and loudest one on the market. Defrosted my fridge, painted the ceiling in the bathroom and had the carpet cleaners come out again to clean the carpet. This all took close to a month for them to coordinate and do. Two weeks after the re-grout the grout started coming off right where the mold and mildew was that they didnt remove. At this point I spoke with the district manager who was just as rude and unsympathetic as the manager. I asked to be moved into another unit at their expense but according to their records would not be until Feb. Okay so here is the timeline. I moved in Oct 1st by Halloween everything was done the 1st week in November the regional manager finally gets a hold of me after I had to call corporate. She views the unit and sees my concerns they come up with a remedy to replace all the parts in the shower facets because they no longer make them anymore and they have to get them from somewhere else and they will not replace the selectors knobs cause they would have to call a plumber in to do that. well I got a little more pressure. THey fully remove (or so they say) the tiles in the bathroom and put up backer board and then put a pvc shower panel in there on DEC 3th~ Then the property manager calls and asks if she could schedule for a courtesy house keeping to clean up the mess left behind. U I have been cleaning up after them for two months now but yes I will take that. Their vendors are so shady and do such a cheap job I wouldnt be surprised if they picked them up from the side of the street to do the work. They have no reputable companies doing their work it is very shotty and you only deal with more problems later. The caulking on the pvc shower panels are now cracking and peeling away and i am scared to call maintenance to see what they will do next. then one morning I wake up at 3am to hear rip drip drip in my bathroom and my ceiling fan in the bathroom is driping water. I called emergency maintenance and the maintenance manager called me back at 9am to say that it was probably an overflow from upstairs. Then at 330 pm he says that he is in my unit and the entire ceiling is flooded with a pipe leak and they have to take it all down and the dry wall people would be in the next day to fix the ceiling now a few months go by no problems till one night getting ready to go to the other side of the valley to visit family I am taking a shower and when i went to turn it off the entire knob crumbled in my hand with the water still on so at 1230 am i called emergency maintenance and was told that someone would call me 5 am still no one called!! I had an appointment at 8am on the other side of town and i have no sleep great! so I went to bed! 1:30pm they finally came and fixed the shower. How many gallons of water was wasted Who had the phone that night Now this month I tried to go pay my rent online and was on the other side of the valley for the weekend and UDR doesnt even have Finistera on their website anymore, tried to call the office and they were closed. Came home sunday night to a letter on my door dated 6/29 that the property was under new management and that we have to personally hand a check into the office this month. Um banks are closed, I dont have a checkbook so now tomorrow I get to go to the back get a cashiers check pay extra and pay my rent. I swear if they try to charge me fees I hope that this new management didnt hire any of the workers that were here with UDR they all are worthy of half of what they get paid. It is all lies and work arounds so they dont have to do anything about it. Now the common area, landscapers do a horrible job at anything the grass is either dead patchy or dirt, the bushes are all over grown that you cant even get to the Jacuzzi switch. I had dead leaves in front of my unit for over 2 months and still have some right now, every time that i open my door and it is breezy outside they come flying into my apartment. At first the gas BBQ were broken till enough residents complained that they put in new ones, the fireplace in the pool doesnt work the Jacuzzi the light was floating around not attached for months. the pool was suppose to be heated to 80 degrees they say but you touch the water it is more like 60. The little pool looks like it never gets a cleaning there is always debris on the bottom and floating on the top. No one parks in their covered parking spot because they are assigned like 200 feet from your unit instead f the ones that are right in front of your unit. The security gates are always breaking the walk thru gate by my unit has never locked and after reporting it they never knew there was one there. Half of the security light on the property are out or completely fallen off. The trees are so over grown that they block the lights any how. Car go like 40 mph around the complex and honk and yell at you if you are trying to back out and are in their way. I have been almost hit I dont know how many times take out the trash. They have two dogie poop stations all not remotely close to where I live so i have to trek to the other side of the complex to get poop bags for my dogs and it is not in the budget to put a closer one in. Man I swear If I were you and you are still reading all the problems Go somewhere else No joking I have 5 months left and I cant wait to get out of here!

author: Former Resident 532620
review_text: Past resident. Honestly disappointed with office staff and Greystar management. Flooring of top story apartments are paper thin. This is a disadvantage to both top and bottom story dwellers. This place is rundown with endless things breaking. Kitchen sink leaked everywhere within few months, warping the floor and cabinets. Took WEEKS for maintenance staff to get it fixed. Water heater broke & water spilled over patio. Took hours to fix. Sink water disgusting with sink parts being ancient. Setup of apartment is weird with no open floor plan & windows everywhere (makes the house very hot). Ceilings very low. The 'renovated' apartments look cheesy and there is little difference between the 'renovated' apartments & the old models. Greystar nickels and dimes EVERY SINGLE THING. Not great if you want to call a place your home! Constant legal reminders are wedged into your door (at least 5 a year) asking for various inconveniences such as walking into your house for an inspection checking your porch, fire detectors, etc. Very obnoxious if you have pets. They let you know they'll show up anytime from 9 and 5 with only 3 days notice. I have been in several different apartments which have never sent notices nor did walk ins of my apartment. The purposes of these walk through are to charge residents for minor infractions. Obnoxious & petty! The effort put to overcharge residents is ASTOUNDING. Staff are constantly driving around to ticket cars and to check your outside decor, charging you for not following community guidelines (since when is a simple plant on my porch an infraction?). Parking situation is obnoxious. Only 12 parking spaces next to any given apartment complex chunk. Cars parked there never leave and you are struggling to find parking. Your covered parking spot is likely far away from your apartment & you have to jump over hills of rock & gravel to get there. The gate situation is weird too. They discourage the usage of gate codes and try instead to give you this chunky key card to get you into the complex. Area around Finisterra is and unsafe. Down the street (Elliot & Priest) you'll see pollution, a Circle-K with drug addicts & homeless people, a Plasma Donation Center, and the world's grungiest Walmart & Starbucks. The icing on the cake of living here was being charged way more than expected without getting a deposit back (which equated to a total of an entire month's rent!) despite leaving with a relatively clean apartment.

author: Current Resident 988846
review_text: If you’re considering living here, don’t. Unless, of course, you’re okay with sharing your home with rats, losing your furniture, and enduring sweltering heat with no real sense of urgency from management. We transferred units back in November 2024, and from the very beginning, we had a rat infestation. Rats — not one, not two, but a recurring, destructive infestation. Rats were underneath the fridge, within the back ends of the cabinets, and under appliances. The rodents would leave piles of feces in the cabinets, under our furniture, and on top of counter tops. Our house smells constantly of there feces or dead rats, no in between. No matter how much we cleaned or even got rid of the dead rats ourselves. Pest control showed up for about seven weeks, then stopped coming entirely. Even though they found rats each visit. The company told us that the management did not want to continue service until other units were reported. Predictably, the rats came back and of course It took yet another month for the complex to simply provide a response again in which was only a confirmation of the rat infestation once again and that only happened after my husband left a public review. They offered to help ONLY after panic calling my husband within minutes after the review to take it down. Apparently, ignoring tenant health and safety is standard practice until you threaten their reputation or legality. The rats caused actual resident property damage, they made a nest in our couch, ate through groceries within cabinets, pissed over our dishes and other stored items within cabinets and more. This has been a reoccurring issue with no actual solution, This has been thousands of dollars in personal loss, and not a single offer of compensation or meaningful help. They even wanted us to pay x2 our rent to even get out of the lease due to the rat infestation. Once again we are in the 7 week cycle and once again they will stop after the 7 week cycle and it will restart where we are going to need more residents besides us to put in a report about the rat infestation for them to come back and do another cycle. It will be an endless cycle until we can get out of the lease. Now, let’s talk about the AC — or lack thereof. Our air conditioning has had problems since we moved In. During the winter it went out quite a few times and we submitted maintenance requests. It was eventually temporarily fixed for the winter. We were told the unit would stop working as it is fairly old. The unit was not replaced or treated again until now during the summer. It stopped working on a Saturday night and since then we have spent every night in up to 90 degree interior temperature. Someone finally came Monday only to confirm the entire unit was dead and had to be replaced. Once again telling us the unit is going to stop working and needing to be replaced. In the meantime their temporary solution was A single portable AC unit. The interior temperature did not change it was still 90+ degrees in every room. WE told the maintenance the solution was not working and we needed either another solution or something alternative. Not a great solution that is until the power went out immediately after the technician left. I tried calling the office for over an hour and was sent straight to voicemail every single time. My husband had to physically go down to the office to get any sort of response. Their solution? Offer another portable unit. But — surprise — the maintenance team was already gone. We sat for over two hours in a hot, powerless apartment before anyone came to help. This place is a masterclass in negligence. There is no urgency, no accountability, and certainly no regard for the health, comfort, or sanity of the people who live here. Every “solution” they offer feels half-hearted and delayed to the point of being useless. If this is how they handle basic habitability issues — rodents, air conditioning, electricity — imagine how they treat anything else. It’s not just frustrating. It’s unacceptable.

author: JSM2015
review_text: Here's what you need to know about Finisterra & its management company, Milestone Management. - The staff in the leasing office do not even pretend to care about your problems. At best, they are pleasant & dismissive . At worst, they are argumentative, condescending & utterly useless. Do not ever go into that office thinking that they will help to advocate for your needs as a paying resident. - After a few short months of residency, I quickly lost my sense of safety in the complex. Several violent break-ins occurred in the complex in the year we lived there. We were woken up to the SWAT team kicking us out of our apartment on one occasion while in pursuit of an armed suspect who was lurking in the complex. The office does not update the community when break-ins occur to help with awareness, as there were several incidents & only one letter issued after it was obvious that Finisterra had already been all over the news. - Intel rents close to half of these apartments out to workers moving here from out of the country. What this leads to is a large population of foreign people that congregate in the common areas & basically take it over & neighbors that make loud overseas phone calls on their patios or while pacing the walkways at all hours of the night. It's clear that it's just a temporary landing pad for them to get settled- most of them have patio sets in their living rooms or nothing at all. I completely understand their situation, it's nothing against them. But for people wanting to live in a relaxing neighborhood setting, Finisterra is not the place. it feels more like a hostile or a temporary residency motel. - Unless there is a flood or a toilet issue maintenance will not be issued to your unit in a timely manner. It was not uncommon for work orders to be completely forgotten. The average was about 5 days to a week, with my calling everyday to ensure the work order was still on the agenda. The maintenance team are nice enough people & the fixes are usually quick but you are regarded as such a hassle when the issue really is the cheap, old equipment. At one point our roof leaked & a bucket sat in my living room for two days. The drywall was destroyed in the living room & bathroom & it took them months to come repaint it. It was so embarrassing when guests would come over & we looked like people who didn't bother to maintain their home or couldn't afford for proper upkeep. Issues like this would go unresolved with no regard or sense of urgency from Finisterra. The last few months of our stay we basically stopped trying to get any non-essential issued fix & just lived with it. We were sick of the fight. I understand that my needs cannot always be meet immediately, but to live daily in an environment that is being neglected is a total bummer- & yet I'm still obligated to pay my rent in full every month. - Looking towards the positive, I can say Finisterra is beautifully maintained on the outside- & that's about it. I am happy to no longer be under contract with them. If this review can convince one person to pass on this complex (& hopefully any Milestone Management-run facility) than at least my misfortune may have saved one person from my same sufferings! For real.

author: Former Resident 171469
review_title: Finisterra - Where brain cells go to die
review_text: Overall, Finisterra is pretty nice. The grounds are kept pretty nice, the staff is pretty nice (barring one of the front desk employees, more about that later), and the residents are pretty nice. The single worst we experienced at Finisterra was getting the security deposit back. My god. We moved out in SEPTEMBER. We just received the correct amount THIS LAST WEEK. Do you see the date of this review? Weâ€TMre almost at the end of March. Iâ€TMm not exaggerating when I say we called the office 20+ times. Every time we called we were assured that they would talk to management. Multiple times we were sent the wrong amount. Legally, in AZ, youâ€TMre supposed to receive your deposit within two weeks of moving out. If itâ€TMs not returned to you within that time, you can go to small claims court and submit a claim to get x2 your deposit back. For one of my calls last month, I threatened them with going this route. Surprise, it didnâ€TMt matter to them. I should have just filed the claim due to the sheer amount of our time they wasted and the fact that we left the apartment in better shape that we found it. We even asked, what about the damage that was there when we moved in, did the last person get charged for that as well? Radio silence on their end. 5 months later we got the security deposit back. Ridiculous. The second worst thing weâ€TMve experienced at Finisterra was actually our move-in day. We were first time movers, so looking back we were a bit naive and should have said something. But in our defense, we had a full rental truck and an army of movers waiting soâ€¦ When we arrived at the office on our move-in date, they were simply not ready for us. We had to wait 45 minutes (with our friends and family who were moving us) to get the keys ready. This was in June. Once we got the keys, it was obvious that they also didnâ€TMt get the apartment ready for us either â€“ it wasnâ€TMt clean. There was clear evidence that the renters before us had a black cat. There was black cat hair everywhereâ€“I am allergic to cats. I was still cleaning up cat hair 14 months later. Also, there was human hair (like beard clippings) in the bathroom cabinets. The toilets werenâ€TMt clean. Some of the bathroom and kitchen cabinets smelled like cat food months later. The floors were not clean, it left our feet dirty enough that we made a special trip to Walmart and bought a mop that very first day. The apartment complex is consistently covered with dog poop (not exactly not-the-norm, but the apartment could do more than just encouraging people to pick up dog poop in a friendly email) and rats roam around. The third worst thing was the package delivery system. We paid $15 a month forâ€¦nothing. In fact, they closed the parcel lockers at the mail area so any packages (Amazon, online shopping, etc) got sent directly to the post office down the street. A little inconvenient, but hurts more when youâ€TMre paying for something that you donâ€TMt get the service of. My mail actually got stolen from my mailbox (a Christmas card from my parents for christâ€TMs sakeâ€¦) but the office quickly fixed my mailbox. The mail man was consistently leaving our mailbox open for all to take. So, I would be a little wary of having important things sent. We never had anything stolen from our door, however, and we were facing one of the parking lots. The fourth worst thing we experienced was when they decided to renew our lease for us, which was interesting to say the least. Especially since our type of units were going for $200/month less. We actually went into the office and discussed the possibility of lowering our lease for when we renewed it, since our units were currently going for cheaper at the time. The employee, Angalique, said sheâ€TMd email corporate and let us know what the response was. After calling to ask a month later, still no response. By the time we moved out, our apartment was still going for $200/month less and they were still calling us about renewing at our current lease price. The trash system is fine. That is included in the fees (not a part of rent) and you cannot get out of it. But, this means people just leave trash on their porch when theyâ€TMre not really supposed to. We had our neighbor (who we shared an entrance with) leave her dogâ€TMs pee pads outside of the door in the summer sun all day which became pretty aromatic to come home to. The grounds are kept generally clean. Thereâ€TMs always dog poop everywhere, but Iâ€TMm pretty sure thatâ€TMs with every complex. They did send out an complex-wide email that reminded people that their porches cannot be used as a storage unit and to clean up after the dog poop (at least x3). That was nice to see. Maintenance is pretty responsive, but some of our problems are still not fixed a month after we put the request in (blinds not working). Our neighbors had to have their sewer/plumbing worked on and they used a jackhammer on the sidewalk outside of the door to get under the concrete. 8 months later they have yet to fill it up with something other than dirt. The apartment we were in was renovated and was really nice. I like the hardwood floors (second floor), countertops, and patio. The patio is a huge part of the apartment and was the biggest patio we saw in our search. Every one of our friends and family who saw it were pretty amazed. The admin office is very responsive. There was a resident who left their dogs with separation anxiety on the porch for a trip, who were barking all through the day and night. I messaged the admins and they quickly resolved the situation. They also forgot to add in the month-off deal to our lease so we went into the office to inquire. The employee, a young man (sorry I donâ€TMt remember his name) was very apologetic and super nice. That was a nice interaction. The only problem I had was when we went to discuss renewing with the front office employee, Angalique, who seemed like she didnâ€TMt want to be there and was rude to us when we asked about renewing our lease. Iâ€TMm not one to call employees out much but that left a lasting impression. I didnâ€TMt want to speak with her again. She shouldnâ€TMt work there. The pools are pretty small, so expect them to be filled with kids in the summertime. Not really the apartmentâ€TMs fault, but donâ€TMt expect quiet hours during that time. The area around the apartment is fine, the two highlights are the Walmart 0.1 miles away and the Costco 0.2 miles away. South mountain is right there for hiking, and the I10 is right there for commuters. When we moved out, we left it cleaner than when we found it. We were still charged $150 for cleaning. Upon inquiring about the itemized bill, we magically got half off. Then, when they sent us pictures of what they cleaned and it was actually from the previous resident. So, it seems like they donâ€TMt clean the places, say that they did, and then still charge the next resident for not cleaning it. Weâ€TMre waiting on a reply from management to see whether or not they billed the previous residents as well. Also, it looks like they try to charge for normal wear and tear (paint and baseboard touchups), which they canâ€TMt do. Itâ€TMs against the law. We also returned our keys a month earlier and got a call a month later saying we didnâ€TMt return our keys and that we didnâ€TMt return them and we would be billed. They called us multiple times about that and we explained multiple times that we in fact had turned in the keys and we had photos. That eventually stopped after they were finally able to figure it out. Seems like they canâ€TMt find the keys when you get there and when you leaveâ€¦ Overall, the complex is fine and the apartments are quite nice. I would say the crowd is more families than not, which can be good or bad in peopleâ€TMs eyes. I wouldnâ€TMt say Iâ€TMd be happy next to the grass fields with the playing kids but some might be. Would I live here again? Before the deposit fiasco, I would have said probably. The cons werenâ€TMt enough to keep me from coming back, but Iâ€TMd be selective about what building I was in in regards to some areas and to be wary of the lease price. It fluctuates a lot. But after the whole ordeal with management, seeing how incompetent they are (except Harry, thanks Harry), Iâ€TMm not sure I would go back. Thereâ€TMs not a lot of brain activity going on there when you call the office staff.

author: Livip237
review_text: I moved into Finisterra in 2022 and loved living here when it was managed by Greystar. However, since the Preferred Apartment Communities (PAC) team took over the complex in early 2023, the complex has gone drastically downhill. Here is a list of issues that have happened since PAC took over: -Crime: Three of my neighbor's vehicles were broken into and multiple packages were stolen. The Greystar team used to hire security to walk around the complex at night to prevent break ins. The PAC team cut security out (even though our rent and fees increased), and break ins have significantly increased. -Amenities & Grounds: Since PAC took over, the pool and hot tub were closed for 2.5 months, and the gym was closed for 2 months. The gates have been broken over 50% of the time (which doesn't help with crime either) and the fire pit was closed for over 6 months. The lawn used to be beautiful with healthy grass and plants. It has now been replaced with dirt and dying plants that aren't watered. They didn't even bother to respond to the emails or voicemails I sent asking to give us some money back on our rent due to the amenities being closed. When we went in person to ask, they said that since there wasn't an amenity fee at the time, they could choose to close the amenities at any time and wouldn't be reducing rent in any form. The amenities were the primary reason that I (and several other residents) chose this complex. -'Paint Fee' - Beware that when you move out, you will receive a significant paint fee which will cause you to get less than half of your security deposit back. Even if the condition of your walls is perfect, you will still be charged this fee (I was actually told this by one of the employees). As it is not in the lease under fees you will be charged upon move out, I have been trying to contact someone for over 1.5 months to have this reimbursed. To this date, I have not received a single email or phone call from the manger regarding this (even though I was promised 4 times that the manager would reach out to me next day). After reading other reviews, other residents also seem to have been scammed by this 'paint fee' and ghosted by the PAC team when trying to inquire about the fee. -Move out date: Make sure your lease end date isn't on a date the office is closed. The last day of my lease was on the 14th of January, and I wanted to move out this date. The office was closed the 14th because it was a Sunday, and also closed the 15th for MLK Jr. Day. I was told I either had to move out the 13th (and still pay for the 14th) or pay to extend the lease and move out the 16th since the office doesn't have a drop box for keys. I was also told I had to pay extra fees if I were to stay beyond the 14th. To avoid additional fees, I was forced to move out the 13th and still had to pay for a day of rent that I didn't even get. I'm honestly not sure if this is even legal, but the PAC team did not care. -Communication: If you have a grievance or issue, you will need to go in person to the office to talk to the PAC team as they ignore emails and phone calls. When they do rarely answer the phone, they tell you they will call you back with an answer (& they never call back). I would highly recommend avoiding this apartment complex due to the issues listed above.
response_text: We value feedback to help us improve our policies and living experience, so we truly appreciate you taking the time to share your thoughts. We are sorry for any difficulty in reaching our team as we know reliable communication is essential. We would be happy to explain any of your move-out charges, so we ask you to email us once more at finisterra@pacapts.com so we can assist you directly. We wish you all the best in your new home.

The apartment interiors are currently undergoing renovations to include new appliances, flooring, and upgraded fixtures. review_title: Rent Here if You Don't Have a Car.
review_text: I lived at Galleria Palms for 2 years. Sure, the place is full of potheads, but what do you expect from a place that hosts a bunch of ASU students? (No offense to those who actually go to ASU to get a degree). The main pool is phenomenal; I miss that pool the most! The fitness center is great and none of the machinery snags like at the current place I live. The office people are generally nice but most of the time they're unsure of policies. They have some dumb rules, like giving you a pass which you must present to the security guards should you ever get questioned. And about security--they only ask people to prove they live in the apartment complex at night. All they ask for though is what apartment you live in, so basically you could just make up a random number and they'd accept that. It's kinda crappy security. The reason I stated it is best to live here if you don't have a car is because during my stay at Galleria, two of my roommates got their cars broken into. One of my roommates got her tire stolen with her own tire jack!! The other got her CD player stolen. However, the first roommate had had the car sitting there for 5 months because it died in October and she didn't bother even TRYING to get it fixed until June, when the tire jacking happened. The other roommate was a complete idiot and left her car door unlocked. Both of these girls also didn't have alarms on their car. Another reason it is good to live here if you DON'T have a car is because the parking SUCKS!! You only get one parking spot assigned to you and half of the time that's taken by a stupid visitor (however, they do tow cars at Galleria like nobody's business.) On a Friday night, you have to get home early if you want a parking spot anywhere! The walls at Galleria are also paper thin, but I'm beginning to think that all apartment complex in the Phoenix area are like that. You can hear people coming and going, the air conditioner on the bottom floor vibrates the top floor, and if you live next to party hosts, expect to be kept up late at night (unless you're one of those people who call the police for noise complaints.) So if you can deal with car theft, annoying security, and loud noises, Galleria shouldn't be too bad of a place for you.

review_title: DO NOT RENT HERE - THEY ENJOY TOWING CARS - POOR MANAGEMENT - OVER PRICED - DO NOT RENT HERE
review_text: http://galleriapalmsapartmentsreview.blogspot.com/ My fiance and I own three cars. We have been in the process of trying to sell two of them. I have let registration lapse on one of them. The same car has a flat tire. We typically drive one or two of the cars, and usually not a third. Since the car was there, with a flat, for a bit of time and not moved - the manager decided to tow the vehicle with their partners ACT Towing - which they have a nice agreement with in towing any vehicles out of their parking lot. Now - here is what happened - we were given a warning about the vehicle and not being registered and how it may get towed about two months ago. I promptly explained that we are considering selling the car, and that it it pointless to spend the money to register the vehicle if someone else will be buying it with no penalties incurred because of the lapse in registration. I had already checked with MVD, and they confirmed that as long as it is not being driven, and insured - I can take as long as I need to sell it, with no penalties. I explained this to someone at the management office, who apparently does not work there anymore. Not my problem. Since I have been here for over two years, it is the business of the management complex to keep track of these kinds of warnings, and how their tenants tried to resolve it. We received another notice 4 days ago, then one 2 days ago - absolutely did not have time to stop in the office - I have a full time job and also run a real estate investment company and upon arriving back to the apartment, car was gone. Called the office - was told it was towed. Manager authorized it and cited it was on my lease. I explained situation again - and she said there was nothing she could do about it. Just call ACT Towing and get my car back - and threatened to have the vehicle towed if the vehicle came back unregistered. Since when did the management at Galleria Palms become DOT? Apparently the management company does not care to handle each and every case as a unique one, and they use the blanket policy to cover themselves. Give me a break, my car was not on cinder blocks with plastic on the windows or on a jack for weeks at a time. I have seen all of that in the parking lot within the last two years. I do not want to see broken down and junk cars in my parking lot. The vehicle we own is far from that, and just had a flat tire - and was not moved. Driving out of the apartment complex this morning, we had noted several vehicles that are in desperate need of towing if our vehicle qualified for it. My fiance had rented at Galleria Palms when it first opened, and suggested it when we were in transition because she had an "OK" experience there. NEVER AGAIN. The quality of tenants moving into the complex has dropped, as I can see who lives around me. The college crowd has not changed since we moved in - and that does not bother us. It can be loud and noisy. You will also here bottles being broken and drunkards arriving from the club throughout the week. Yes, it happens everywhere, and these things won't change. Also, crime happens everywhere and you will also find it at Galleria Palms. I see broken glass next to cars all the time. The point I a making here is that it happens frequently at Galleria Palm, and they are not immune to society's delinquents. Tempe is also a college town, full of party people - so consider doing your due diligence and research before signing on the dotted line at this complex. Besides, rents have been steadily increasing, and this place is not worth it. There are bug problems here as well, and I have had to call management on several occasions. We are clean people and do not leave food everywhere. Do not let the pretty little fountains spouting joy and happiness in the front of the complex fool and seduce you. You will quickly come to the realization that it is a sham to get your hard-earned cash. The landscape and maintenance guys are all good people. I see them diligently working around the property taking pride in their work. They need to be a bit more careful with their golf carts whipping them around the lot like tanks, but other than that, I have no complaints. They are good hearted people - and I see that up close, and from a distance. Speaking of from a distance, you can see the phoniness of management from a distance. LET ME REMIND YOU - THEY ARE IN THE BUSINESS OF REDUCING COSTS, INCREASING REVENUE AND FINDING CREATIVE WAYS OF GETTING YOUR MONEY. At the end of the day, when it comes to customer service, and retention, they don't care. It is a hit and run sale, and you will be stuck until your lease is up. I don't have exact estimates with me, but I can say that I have probably spent upwards of 18 THOUSAND DOLLARS IN RENT here. Do they care about that kind of customer? The answer is a BIG FAT NO. When speaking to the Galleria Palms manager Misty and her supervisor Mary Jacobs who represents the company who owns Galleria Palms, Kennedy Wilson, Inc - they both mentioned to me that there is absolutely nothing that Galleria Palms can do to help me. They offered no kind of resolution and didn't even bother to let me offer solutions to get the car back. It is sitting in some impound right now and I have to spend time and money in getting it back, because Misty made a smart, unilateral and executive decision to get the car towed. Real Smart! This will cost them loss in business in the thousands. How smart is that? Let it be known for the record I have spent probably over 18 thousand dollars here and they can't help that kind of customer? Someone who does not write bad checks - and is never late? I will be sure to bring this to the attention of senior management at Kennedy Wilson, the Executive Group, Regional Leaders, and Business Unit Leaders who oversee the region in which Galleria Palms is located in and let them know that this is unacceptable business practices and a terrible way to treat great tenants. I will also vehemently tell everyone I contact including local and regional real estate partners, business contacts, as well as personal contacts, who are in search of a reputable apartment complex and management company to STAY CLEAR AWAY from Kennedy Wilson properties and Galleria Palms in Tempe, Arizona. If you ever consider renting here, contact Mary Jacobs and let her sell you on why you should rent from Kennedy Wilson Properties: Phoenix 10220 N. 31st Avenue Suite 127 Phoenix, AZ 85051 Tel: 602-861-7037 Fax: 602-331-7367 Contact: Mary Jacobs Managing Director If after this review you are still considering renting from Galleria Palms and are starting to fall for the allure of the fountains and the pseudo-beauty of the clubhouse which you can't even use for special events for your family - call me fast and I will help you snap out of the hypnosis. http://galleriapalmsapartmentsreview.blogspot.com/

review_text: I have only been here for 2 weeks and I want to move out. Where to start? On the initial walk thru, before we signed the lease, I noticed the carpet was not tacked down in the 2nd bedroom where my 17month old would be sleeping. Then I noticed how HORRIBLE the bathrooms looked dirty, stained tub, nasty looking tile, grout not cleaned, CHEAP CHEAP work done when being made. Touch up paint in the master bathroom is a different color thatn the original. Needless to say they re-cleaned everything and fixed the carpet. We still moved in because we we pressed for time and this was out 2nd apartment putting a holding fee down for. The model apartment they showed me was awesome inside (FAR from the actual apartment you get). After the lease was signed we got our checklist to put down any stains, damages, etc WELL, the bedroom door wouldn't close, the wood on the kitchen cabinets are peeling off, there is a hole in the vinyl floor of the kitchen, one of the burners on the stove didn't work, there are traffic stains all over the carpet (Even tho management said it was new carpet when the previous renters moved in), closet door didn't close, could hardly turn the dials on the tempurature gage of BOTH bathrooms, weather strip on the front door does not fit completly therefor weather and bugs get in. Which brings me to my BIGGEST complaint. On the first day here I noticed a bad ant problem by the front door. So I called the office and was told that everyone was having an ant problem because of something they're doing to the outside. She said for me to go get cinnamon and water/vinegar. It was only after her hearing that I was upset that she offered to have the apt sprayed on Thursday(this was a Sunday I called). Thursday comes and goes and there is nothing better about the ant problem. It's actually worse! Which is why I decided to do a review, because I never do reviews. Today after working 11 hours and picking up my 17 month old cranky, tired, hungry, teething son I find a FULL line of ants coming in through the weathering strip that isn't working, and going into my son's room. I kill them all, vacuum and walk away for 5 minutes only to come back and see MORE! Looks like they're coming from under the carpet. I vacuum again and the same thing 3x's. Then I go to sit my son at his high chair only to find it COVERED in ants. I HATE bugs especially with a small child that puts evrything in his mouth and crawls around and sits on the floor. I want to move already and have signed a year lease. The ONLY reason I give this place 3 stars is the grounds out side look nice and the amenities are nice. Even tho our neighbor said not to leave bikes on the bike rack outside even if its locked up because people steal it by bending the metal frame of the rack until it comes off. Her bike was even stolen from her upstairs front patio. This place is NOT worth the amount they charge for rent. 11/7/12- Adding onto my original review. I have now been here one month and after all of ^that I now have termites. I was told about it two weeks ago after I found something "growing" out of my bathroom wall, which turned out to be mud tunnels from termites. The woman in the office (before knowing it was termites) had the nerve to ask "how often that area was cleaned?" I was told they couldn't get ANY exterminators out here unitl the 30th of Nov! A month after being told we have termites. They said it's termite season and its common. I told them that's not acceptable now that we've actually started seeing termites everywhere! I was told last week that the supervising manager was seeing 'what she could do', but NO ONE has called me to tell me anything. I asked if I could be released from our lease and was told this wasn't a good enough reason. I'm now thinking of finding a tenant attorney. It's really uncomfortable and disgusting when you work all day and have to come home to worry about termites falling in your dinner because there are 30 of them crawling on the ceiling right above your head.

author: lluke
review_text:
I have mixed feelings about this place. I lived there for 3 years and never once had a problem with crime or vandalism. However, everyone around me seemed to have problems. The lady in the apartment below me had some homeless guy throw a rock through her window and come into her bedroom. Another person had his car stolen 3 (yes three ) times from his parking spot which was 5 spots down from me. Perhaps I was not a victim because I am very cautious and always watch my back. I used "The Club" on my car and did have an alarm as well. I also had a second story apartment that helps deter "smash and grab" punks.

The staff was usually very friendly. My only real complaint was with the maintenance guy. This moron couldn't fix a thing! I eventually decided calling the office to ask for a repair was pointless I started doing repairs myself.

I'm surprised to hear of problems with bugs. The staff offers a free spraying service every other Thursday. I never took advantage of this service while I lived there so no one sprayed my place for 3 years. Yet I don't think I ever saw a single bug.

The walls are very thin and you can hear your fellow residents even if you don't want to. I actually had the cops show up at my apartment and question me about a domestic dispute. Apparently my neighbor heard me yelling. I was actually yelling at the TV my Suns were playing. Ha Ha. The place is definitely not quiet. Cars, students, parties, idiots, but you get used to it at least I did.

At checkout time they hit me up for a dirty shower and carpet patch. It was $20 for the shower and $15 for the carpet patch. I deserved both so I can't complain. However, they ended up waiving both fees as the finance manager told me the maintenance guy did not deliver his report on my apartment and therefore he could not charge me. It looks like the maintenance guy's lack of competence worked in my favor on the way out.

For $700 a month, I think it is a decent value. If you are going to school at ASU it is not a bad place to live. Much cheaper then San Marbaya but not quite as fun. I'd look around, but definitely consider Galleria Palms.

If your looking for a safer area try stuff in 85283 or maybe even 85284 if you want to commute a bit more.

author: Current Resident 43687
review_text:
I've been living here for three years, and the quality has deteriorated dramatically.

First of all, the roof leaks. Several months ago, it rained incredibly hard, and rain started coming in through a two-foot crack in the ceiling! We called the emergency maintenance number, but they were slow to act on it. Apparently, 13 other buildings were also leaking, and 7 other buildings leaked the year before and this place is rather new! Anyway, it took two weeks for them to actually repair the crack, and we had to call several times for them to paint (which they never did). The independent roofing contractor that worked for Galleria Palms actually advised us to SUE the apartment company because they used LEAD flashings for the ventilation ports on the roofs. So, the rain poured off the lead flashings, and into our apartment, and onto our belongings. When we contacted the manager, she just said that it was not a legal issue, and there was no health hazard! They also refused to repair the water damage on one of the walls, which had bubbling paint. I would not be surprised if this soon turns into a mold issue. Incredible!!

Anyway, roofing aside, the place is incredibly energy inefficient. We can feel heat radiate from the downstairs apartment. Expect energy bills in the summer to be about $200/month and $80/month at the cheapest in the winter (this is with restricted use of the A/C and heating since we try to conserve energy by opening the windows).

Even though you are paying to live in a gated community, I've seen months go by at a time without working gates. If something goes wrong, it takes at least two weeks for their company to repair it. So, it's just as safe as a non-gated community, only much more expensive.

Parking is terrible. Even with one assigned spot, guests have to drive around for awhile before finding something far away and they are not comfortable leaving their car in a vandalism-prone area. Bicycle theft is a problem. Every bicycle on the rack closest to our building and near other buildings were stolen. I've resorted to carrying my new bike (my second since living here) up a flight of stairs and locking it to my balcony.

Even though there is a night security service, they only come once every evening, and have to be called in at other times. A nice security guard on duty actually said it would be better to call the Tempe police instead for faster service on even small matters like noise complaints!

These so-called "luxury" apartments are not worth the money. You can find better apartments you are willing to live less than two miles south of Galleria Palms, and for more than hundred dollars less per month! Believe me, I've already made plans to move when my lease is over and that is four months in the future! As you can see, I am very anxious to move out of this over-priced dump.

review_title: Pretty nice, it could be better though.
review_text: As with all apartment complexes, there are going to be some problems. Overall, my boyfriend and I have had a pretty good experience here. We have lived here for 2 1/2 years, and are moving out because we want more of a luxurious place to live in a better location. Galleria Palms has been nice for the stay we had here. I have a few issues for people to be aware of before they move in. Firstly, the front gate rarely works - so do not move here for the safety of a gated community, it might as well not be. My boyfriend's car was broken into as well (and we live right near the front desk), so make sure to at least put a club on your steering wheel at night. Second, main pool is often closed because people bring glass in to the pool area. If maintenance or any staff found any glass, the pool would be closed the next day. This was frustrating because the pool is very fun and beautiful to hang out at, so to arrive there to find it closed is discouraging. They do keep the other pools open when this happens, but it is still frustrating. Third, there can be a lot of little kids running around at times. They were never very annoying, but I personally don't like to hang out with kids when I am drinking with friends at the pool. I'm sure families thought us drinking at the pool was annoying too though, so I guess it goes both ways. Overall, it has been a good experience. We are not moving for any bad reason; just want a change of scenery. The office staff and maintenance are very friendly and reliable. I would say the majority of people living here are college kids, so take that into account if that is not what you are looking for. We lived on the second floor and had no problems with noise. I really think a lot of people post on here because they feel very strongly against or for a place. That being said, I found no serious problems here and I recommend giving it a try. Anywhere you live there will be good and bad.

author: AJG85
review_title: Great for the price and location
review_text: For Tempe this place is really good. I'm actually only moving because ADOT is buying the buildings running along the 10/60 for highway expansion and I don't have a choice about that but I knew this might happen when I signed the lease. I'm having a really hard time finding something as good in the same price range in Tempe and the plethora of nasty reviews for just about every place I look at on here prompted me to look up this place. Puts my concerns into perspective. Tip from a fellow apartment dweller is always screen the unit before signing the lease and again before leaving and get everything in writing and signed as necessary. It seems a lot of people haven't read or don't understand the landlord/tenant act. Google it. Both landlords and tenants have certain rights but by signing the lease you are legally agreeing to follow it's provisions, I'd suggest reading them first. You wouldn't sign to buy/finance a car without looking at the price, interest rate, and terms would you? Pros: Good size apartment floor plans (more space than i need) Full sized washer/dryer in unit (1 load of laundry once a week in my case) Maintenance (my thermostat and heater broke they replaced both within 48 hours even though my unit was scheduled to be torn down, emergency maintenance responded quickly as well see cons for that night of fun) Plenty of extra open parking compared to other places (easy to invite friends or have multiple vehicles) Good amenities overall (small gym, but indoor basketball court makes up for that) Cons: Assigned covered parking spaces are a bit tight for american cars Optional garage is an extra $60 a month and far away from your unit Small microwave (can't fit a normal sized plate, i'd just buy my own if I wasn't moving out soon) Drug use (there are significant amount of pot and meth users in residence but I say do what you want as long as it doesn't affect me) Shoddy poorly installed deadbolts (the pin in mine snapped due to improper install) Neighbor called the cops on me when my lock broke and I was waiting for maintenance late at night, can't blame her given previous observations. Edit: Neighbor calling the cops on me could be a positive if you're a paranoid type. Personally I've never seen any situation improve with police presence to date.

The patio has a large storage unit to hold all of your belongings. We love the double sinks in the Jack-and-Jill bathroom. We have been fortunate to call this place home for over two years. I would recommend this apartment complex for ASU students, families and everyone in between.

author: Santear2
review_text: These apartments are liars, thieves, and scandals. Don't trust them. I have never been so disappointed in any place I have lived as I was with Galleria Palms apartments. When I first moved in I was excited to be getting such a great deal on such nice apartments. Within a week of moving in several residents approached my brother and I telling us they felt bad for us having just moved in since everyone in our building would have to move out soon. Funny how it was never mentioned to us that we might have to move not long after moving in. The only thing ever mentioned to us was on the day we were signing our lease they mentioned ADOT had taken over some of their buildings due to construction that was going on nearby. They said it wasn't anything to worry about though. About 2 months later we were notified that we either had to find another apartment within 30 days or move into the apartment they offered us. Since we had just paid move in costs to move into the apartment we ended up taking the apartment they offered since that option meant we didn't have to pay security costs again. When we went to move into the apartment they offered they insisted we had to sign another year lease instead of just continuing the lease we had previously. They only allowed us one week to move from one apartment to the other even though nobody was moving into the previous apartment any time soon and we would have had more time if we just moved some where else. Fast forward 3 or 4 months later. My brother and I went on vacation thinking the nightmare was done. When we came home a week later our parking area was fenced off and we had no place to park. We went in to find out why we didn't have a parking spot and why we weren't given any notice about this situation either. The lady in the office was rude and kept telling us we still had the same parking number. She said they put a note on our door as soon as they knew about it. Granted I will admit my brother and I were both beyond upset after the first incident and then this. Yet I still believe customer service requires that a person try to disarm the situation instead of making it worse. I have worked customer service my whole life and I would never have approached an upset customer the way she approached us. Now move forward to months later when the construction is over. We received a paper (on our door again)stating our parking number may change, but our space should remain the same. We ended up finding out from a new tenant that our parking space changed. This happened when my brother was about to have the person's car towed, but found out who the person was and talked to them. Again Galleria Palms did not communicate information to us and when confronted flat out lied about having communicated the change to us. Due to all these problems my brother and I decided to speed up our plans on finding a house. Now come to present day. My brother kept checking Galleria Palms website for a bill to see how much we owed if any. Day after day there was no bill that appeared. As is Galleria Palms way we finally got a bill from them. The kicker on this is they are charging us for a spot on the carpet that neither my brother nor I know about (and I went over all spots with my steam cleaner)and they want the full amount of $878.70 within 7 days. The problems with this is: First by tenant laws and all payment laws they have to allow a reasonable amount of time from the time the person being charged receives the bill to pay the bill. Seven days is not a reasonable amount of time by law and in reality. Second they only sent the bill out as of 1/4/2013. So where they get the idea that they legally have the right to set a payment due date of 1/14/2013 is beyond me. Third after all the above issues we have I really feel that they should pay my brother and I for having to deal with them. My advice go live in the roach invested Midtown on Main before moving into Galleria Palms. At least then you will receive communication and honesty on what is going on. I would rather have roaches since I can get roach spray and roach motels to kill them than deal with an apartment complex who lies to me and does dishonest business.

author: Current Resident 735461
review_text: Dear Prospective Residents, I work second shift and as a result I do not get to utilize the "outstanding" trash valet service. As you will soon become aware, trash valet is a mandatory and non-negotiable fee which comes standard in every resident's lease agreement, but if you happen to live in a building without a trash chute and work during the allotted trash times, you are SOL. The Assistant Manager persists that you shall walk an exorbitant distance just to take the trash out every day, and if you decide to leave your trash out before going to work at 4pm like I did, expect the pleasure of paying a $50.90 fee for doing so. I really deserve it though; $50 dollars is most certainly a worthy punishment which fits the despicable crime of *checks notes* putting my trash can out 2 hours early. I mean really, won't someone think of the potential loss of revenue from fresh, gullible, prospective residents? Be aware that it took management the greater part of a year to fix the melted down BBQ pit. Unsurprisingly, they also cannot seem to manage fixing any broken doors or parking lot gates that will arbitrarily and randomly refuse to open, or modifying the parcel system such that packages are not haphazardly thrown about the package room or placed in the wrong lockers-don't forget: you actually pay to have your package lost or given to someone else. Management obviously needs to increase rent across the board as they cannot afford to water the grass, or even attend to the mangled mess of dog park equipment which looks like it will collapse any day. But do not fret, as the property's "dog-friendly" dog park has now become a luxury spa for residents who wish to have a cozier and more refreshing mud bath experience, at the behest of absolutely no one. All in all, I'm satisfied with the unorthodox methods management employs to take special care of us residents, and I definitely do not expect that my very courteous and appreciative donation of fifty dollars and ninety cents to Residences at Fountainhead will go towards fixing any of our issues on the property. After all, why should it? Signed, Resident. P.S. If you are resident management, do not post a response to this review trying to "remedy" the issue. That will not fool anyone into thinking that this is a one-off freak occurrence that would never happen on your beloved property. This façade has been worn down and anyone who lives here longer than a month will see what a sham show you're running here. Go yourselves.

author: Current Resident 1230389
review_text: I have lived in this apartment complex long enough to fully experience its ongoing issues, and unfortunately, I cannot recommend it to anyone looking for a safe or well-maintained place to live. One of the biggest concerns is the lack of security. The complex feels unsafe, and basic features like functioning door knobs are often broken or left unrepaired for long periods of time. Something as simple as being able to securely close and lock your door should never be an issue, yet here it is a recurring problem. The elevators are another constant frustration. They work only part of the time, and when they do, it's unreliable at best. This becomes especially inconvenient for residents with mobility needs, parents with strollers, or anyone carrying groceries or heavy items. Having an elevator that only works sporadically is not acceptable for a residential building. Cleanliness throughout the complex is also a major problem. The hallways frequently smell like trash, and it seems like proper maintenance and sanitation are not priorities for the management. This contributes to an overall feeling of neglect. What makes these issues even worse is the lack of support from the office staff. When residents bring up concerns or requests, the employees often seem uninterested or unwilling to help. Instead of addressing problems, they give the impression that complaints are an inconvenience to them. Overall, this complex needs significant improvements in safety, cleanliness, maintenance, and customer service before it can be considered a decent place to live.

author: Current Resident 65026
review_text: So I have been living at Onnix for about 6 months and I love my apartment and the community. However there are several issues that I have a problem with. Over this past weekend I had no hot water and I did not receive a single notification about what was going on. I put in a maintenance request online and no one ever called me. It wasn't until I called in an emergency maintenance request that I heard anything. I was told it would be fixed the next day and it was in the morning, then I notification was sent out 3 minutes before they turned off the water and I had no hot water again. The pool closest to my apartment has been unusable for months. The water is as green as the leaves on the trees and I have never seen anyone working on it. There's a hot tub that looks like it is perfectly fine to use but the gate has a chain around it so you can't even enter. The grill by my apartment wasn't in great shape when I moved in and has only gotten worse (see pictures). I've never seen any maintenance done to it what so ever. I've been told by some of my neighbors that the dog parks don't have working water fountains for their dogs and one of the dog parks has a gate that doesn't lock. Someone almost lost their dog because they were able to just walk right through the gate (luckily his dog knew his way home). Overall everyone that I have spoken to that works here has been super nice and friendly but there should be no reason why these issues haven't been looked in to. Especially considering the complex has no problem sending out late fees in a time where plenty of people have lost jobs or have had their work hours reduced and may be struggling. Throughout this entire pandemic they have only helped us out once by waving the late fee for 10 days in October. I have no problem with paying a late fee because it is something that I agreed to but if that's the case then the "luxury" amenities that are bragged about on their website should be up and running properly. I've been told that they are under new management but if things don't change within the next 6 months of my lease I will not be renewing.

They've added fresh paint, added new (and better landscaping), fixed all the lights so it's safe to walk around at night and see whats around you, and repaved the parking lot. Second, I've had a really positive experience with their maintenance staff. They're really accommodating and friendly whenever they stop by. Bridge has a strong track record with notifying residents of any water shut offs (the pipes are old and a little faulty) but it's never for long. The apartments are nice, I used to live on the east side but now I live on the West side. I prefer West side over East, but my understanding is that they're working on updating both sides of the complex so that they're a little more in sync with each other. That being said, Bridge has far exceeded any expectations and contributed to a more positive experience overall as a resident. I will certainly continue to resign my lease here, it's been an awesome experience.

author: Current Resident 409624
review_text: I moved to Apt#2081E earlier this month and wanted to write to you about absolutely pathetic experience that I have had till now. Moving sucks, especially if you have a kid. When we moved in, little had we expected that the packing and moving would be nothing compared to the harrowing experience that we about to get. As my wife, who has already spoken to you twice, would have told you, we took a 5 day overlap between moving out of my old apartment in north Phoenix and shifting here. However, we had come here to inspect the apartment and provide you with move in issues, in the first 48 hours. In the email that she had sent you, she had reported a few issues including presence of a few bugs in the apartment and requested for a pest control inspection, which I guess never happened. However the actual problems start the night we move in i.e. 7th Oct. We had just spent 3-4 hours in the apartment and we notice a couple of bugs, which after some googling, turned out were bed bugs. We were shocked on two fronts: one we never had bed bug problem in my earlier apartment and two we expected a new apartment that we were asked to move in to, to be checked for and certified bed bug free. It was clear to us at that very moment that we had moved into an apartment which had bed bug presence. Imagine, all your stuff scattered around the apartment, waiting to be arranged and finding out that there are bed bugs in the apartment. Every belonging of ours was exposed to bed bugs. We notified the leasing office first thing next morning and we were told that pest control inspection would happen on Tuesday, following which next course of action will be identified, which turned out to be bed bug treatment. Let me list down two major complaints that I have with Onnix management: 1. It is completely unprofessional and in fact unethical for Onnix to move me in to an apartment that had bed bug presence in it. I have never experienced bed bug infestation before, so I didn't know the signs to look for it, but after some googling, at hindsight, I can safely assume that this apartment has had a history of bed bugs. It has black spots all over the bottom of walls (where walls meet the carpet). Secondly, it is pretty clear from what I can see that you have had a chemical treatment done previously to this apartment for bed bug infestation. Pics attached. a. So why this house was not double checked for bed bug presence before we moved in? b. How can a property owned by a big and reputable company like Bridge, be so irresponsible / careless of in such a grave matter? 2. Ever since we have reported this problem, no one from leasing office has ever reached out to us proactively to apologize or to let us know next course of action or just to make us comfortable. Whether it was to arrange pest control inspection, bed bug inspection or actual chemical treatment or just calling and letting us know that we are there to help you, how many times did the leasing office proactively contact us? ZERO. Every time, my wife had to call the leasing office or visit there personally. Now let me list down the problems / inconvenience that this has caused my family: 1. As I mentioned above, everything I own has been exposed to bed bugs. Although, the initial inspection categorically proved that nothing that I own had bed bugs in it and they were just present in below the carpet near three walls, I will now always live in fear of something being missed. 2. I have a 3 year old daughter, who was anyways not taking the move well, as both her familiar surroundings, her home and her school changed. The only thing familiar to her, her toys, we had to wash thoroughly with soap water, and stack away in our car as we didn't want them being risked exposed to bugs or the chemical treatment. 3. We were asked to run every cloth / shoe we have in a dryer which as you know is more effort than money. Above all, its time consuming. We have spent last two weekends going to and fro the laundry room washing and drying our clothes / shoes / bags. 4. After the treatment, we were told that we need to thoroughly vacuum the apartment every day for successful / guaranteed results. We had to buy a new bagged vacuum cleaner, as the bag- less one we had would not suffice. And above all, it takes almost an hour every day to vacuum the apartment / crevices/mattress/ suitcases thoroughly. Ideally, Onnix should have offered us to get someone to do this vacuum cleaning, however, ironically, we are doing all this every day and paying you rent to do this. 5. We were also asked to have all our stuff bag in plastic / air tight bags until the next inspection. So right now we are not even living out of our suitcases, but out of plastic Ziploc bags. 6. My wife and I moved here from Phoenix, as she is studying Industrial Engineering at ASU. We left the place where we and more importantly our daughter was settled, just because we wanted to save my wife those two hours of travel time, which would mean spending two more hours of quality time with my daughter or just study. None of which has happened by the way as she has either spent that time washing/ drying clothes or vacuuming or just googling on what precautions to take. 7. We had planned to buy furniture over the same weekend we moved in. Now we are being told that we can't buy any new furniture until the house is re-inspected and certified bed bug free. We have no chair, no sofa / couch, no table. My wife has to go to library every other day to study / complete her assignments, not because she loves studying there, but because she can't study sitting on floor every day. Studying with a kid is anyways difficult, but you guys managed to make it more difficult than it already was. 8. Last and worse of all, my daughter developed an allergic reaction, due to the chemical that was sprayed. Now we have to apply allergic ointment on her twice every day. I have attached a couple of pics, just so that you understand the gravity. 9. And to mention the least, none of the move-in issues have been resolved, i.e. ? adding the missing blinds, changing the light bulbs etc. I received a voice mail from Laura, saying that the kitchen sink issue has been fixed, however, that the issue still exists. Now, the funny part is my wife says she was home all day and no one had come to fix it. So, how did your maintenance team manage to fix the leakage without even visiting the apartment? Needless to say that along with financial impact, we have also gone through significant physical and mental trauma, with no mistake of ours. Our only mistake being choosing this apartment to live in.
response_text: Please accept our sincerest apologies for the inconveniences you've faced during your time with us. Providing our residents with a comfortable experience is our main priority and we're disappointed to hear that we've missed the mark with you early on. We appreciate your patience and will continue working diligently to resolve these issues. If you have any questions, please contact our office. Again, we're very sorry about these turn of events and look forward to making you happier in your home.
