author: harikrishnag
review_text: Well, I lived in this apartments for 10 years and finally I vacated in the month of August. The lease system is not to update and it has lot of flaws. I was supposed to renew my lease in May 2011. They never sent the lease renewal notice and as I was staying there years and years, I didn't check either. In February 2012, they alerted me about the missing renewal and I said I will renew it. They asked me to renew the lease as per the original dates i.e from May 2011 to May 31, 2012. They use the 3rd party web site to sign the lease digitally. The sales representative sent the lease with the dates from Feb 1, 2012 to Jan 31, 2013, thinking that the lease starts from that month. I went back and asked about the dates. They corrected and generated new lease documents. We both (me and my wife) signed the lease. From May 2012, I was going on month-to-month basis and in July 1st week, I gave the 1 month notice to vacate in August. After vacating the apartment, I got the bill for breaking the lease. I went there and talked to account manager and she told that I signed a lease from Feb 2012, Jan 2013 - which I didn't sign. She showed me the lease agreement where it shows that we both signed the lease on Jun 6th. The lease was generated in February and asked them to correct it, but they corrected and generated the new one, but forgot to delete the wrong one. I think that existed in the system, and on June 6th some one checked and would have thought this was supposed to sign in the month of Feb 2012 itself and they would have marked it as signed. But the account manager didn't agree with my theory and asked me to check with the 3rd party software/site if I have questions on who actually signed the lease. I tried my level best to convince her. In that process I repeated some of the questions 2 to 3 times, because I wanted to clarify my doubts. She got irritated with my questions and told that there are lot of customers waiting and I need to leave and pay the balance. I asked for the copies of the lease and went home and started checking the lease documents. It clearly shows, on June 6th, 2012, the lease was signed by 3 different people (me, my wife and apartment sales representative) from the same ip address with the seconds difference. My wife traveled abroad during that time frame and I have the proofs of her itinerary and stamps on the passport about her departure and arrival. So it is impossible for 3 of us to sign the lease from same ip address. So it is clear that we didn't sign the lease. I went back and showed the same ip address on the lease and asked to remove the lease breaking charges and send me the updated bill. I tried to talk to the manager on that day, but she was busy and mentioned that she cannot give the appointment for next 4 days. A week after, they sent to the collection agency. I tried to talk to them again to remove the lease breaking charges, but they said it's with collection agency and cannot talk about it at all. I asked if I pay to collection agency and once you receive the money, can you refund the lease breaking charges, but the account manager told that they cannot do anything about this. They said I don't have an option to talk about it. In short, unacceptable responses from the management even though there is a clear evidence that I didn't sign the lease. I am not sure, this is even considered as forgery. Clearly we didn't sign the lease and they are not even open to talk about it and correct it. I am not recommending this apartment to any one at all and stay away from this.

review_text: I still live here, but I dont plan on renewing my lease for other reasons then Solara. The A.C. does tend to go out at least 3 times during the summer, which really sucks. The staff are always changing, it's kinda odd. The residents are a mixture of college students, families and handy cap people. The handy cap people tend to be super nice, but they take some getting used to. Drug dealers do live here and so do drug users, but it is my understanding that they do background checks. The issue is not everyone has a background. Cops are here every night. The windows suck for keeping out noise and you can hear through the walls. Here is the reality of the situation though, there are tons of people who live here. That means you are going to get the roaches, the ants, the crazies, the druggies, have issues with the AC, have issues with the cops, ect. For the location it is a good price, its right by the 60 an close to the 101. You can walk to the store, there are three bus routes, you can take a taxi home from mill, you can ride your bike to ASU, you dont have to deal with R.A's or roomies you dont chose. They do have security some what, there is a lot of parking, there is a work out center that is nice, the cops will come if needed, the staff while stand offish can be helpful. The people who live here can be nice if you actually get to know them. Maintenance is always super polite and will try to do what they can. As for the increase in rent, I am going to be honest, no clue why it keeps on going up an down, up and down and the book keeping is sometimes way off. There are pro's and con's to every place, but Solara is HUGE so its going to have more then others. Hopefully I can leave once school is over an say hey, I really had no huge issue, fingers cross, but I would tell someone to consider renting here. Im sorry I know everyone else hates it here, but yeah so far I dont think its so bad.

review_text: I had to delete my previous good review that I made when I first moved in, because the first impressions were not lived up to in the slightest degree. I told them about the issue & requested that they have it tested to see if it was toxic BEFORE cleaning it & the person I spoke with assured me that they would not clean it, they were only going to inspect it. Well, I came home the next day & it was cleaned & painted over. They seriously will do anything to avoid any costs to them. I should have paid to get it tested myself so that I could possible get the entire place condemned. I moved out on September 29th, & requested that I be present during the walk-thru inspection and assured me that I would be present and that they would let me know when they were planning on doing the inspection. However, they went ahead & did the inspection anyway without letting me know. Then, I was told I would be receiving an itemized list of deductions with whatever balance I would owe in the mail and via email. After two weeks of not getting anything, I called to find out what was going on. said that she didn't have access to the amount that I owed and that she would have their property manager call me with a break down of what I owe. I received no call, so a week later (yesterday) I gave them another call, to which was able to pull up my account and see what I owe (after she said she didn't have access to a week prior). She told me that I owed them a balance of $500, and that's after them taking my $150 deposit and that it would be sent to collections tomorrow. After fighting it and stating that they were required to send me a bill & itemized list before sending it to collections, they sent it anyway. I have never dealt with a more incompetent staff in my life, nor have I ever heard of any company being able to send a debt to collections before the day the bill is due, and before even receiving a bill! I guess this a lesson learned on my part, but this place seriously needs to get their together, otherwise I could see some lawsuits happening down the road.

author: Current Resident 504028
review_text: I am writing this review to make prospective residents aware of an ongoing issue that seems to never get resolved. These apartments do NOT have a/c. They run off of a centralized chiller system, one chiller services many apartments. The chillers are constantly breaking down, leaving you without cool air. Most of the time it will get fixed within a day but obviously that depends on the nature of the issue. Another issue with this complex is the office staff and a few maintenance staff refuse to admit there is a problem with the chillers, and instead tell you the resident "your apartment is cool" or "I haven't heard of the chillers being down" or even "call of it gets worse", but sometimes you don't even get a response. The chillers went out a few nights ago and it reached 86 degrees in my apartment and was very humid. But when I called they told me that if it were the chillers more residents would have called. So no one came to my apartment to fix or even check on the issue. The next day they found that the chillers were indeed not working and it took until that night before it was "fixed". Well the next morning it was a few degrees cooler but it was still in the high 70s and the humidity in my apartment was over 50%. You can't cook or do laundry when it is this way because the temperature will rise dramatically and take quite a while to cool down (speaking from past experience). So I called the office to put in a repair order and the gentleman I spoke to was very rude. He said if it were the chillers, more people would have called (de ja vu) and told me that he keeps his apartment at 80 and it seems like a reasonable temperature so he didn't think he could get someone to come look at my apartment. I told him, that is fine if you have a/c, but when you have a broken chiller trying to cool your home the humidity gets unbearable, and you have to eat out and let your laundry pile up so not to heat up your house. He still did not want to make a repair order! So I demanded he make a repair order, and in a very sarcastic tone he said ok mam I put in the repair order. I'm not saying he didn't put the order in, he just sounded sarcastic and was just very rude. I spoke to a few of my neighbors, all had called about the chillers and got similar responses. So I spoke directly to a maintenance staff who told me that indeed the chillers were down again, and they were currently working on them. We do now have cool air again, but I can assure you it won't last all summer. I am counting the days for my lease to be up.

author: jblangi
review_title: Great Experience, Value, Staff. Recommended. (read me!)
review_text: Ok, so here are the straight facts on this place. Solara is a BEAUTIFUL remodeled community with meandering walkways and attractive landscaping. Situated in a sought-after location by the airport, Mill Ave District, and major highways- Solara features 3 POOLS. One of which is heated over the winter (does Tempe even have winter?). The office staff is friendly and effective. I consider myself a discerning tenant, especially coming from a real estate background. I physically visited 13 other apartment communities in the 3 days prior to choosing Solara. For starters, the leasing agent I worked with was the best of all the communities I'd visited- not by a little, by FAR. He was personable, competent, knowledgeable, and not at all salesy. I found a great unit next to the pool, at the best VALUE for my money. I signed a lease same day- and this staff member stayed late on New Year's Eve just so I could get keys that night. Since move in, I've been very happy with with my experience here. The units are updated, and were UPDATED SMART and effectively. If you're in construction, you'd know what I mean. They did a great job modernizing the units without any major construction, probably helping keep rents so affordable. Mine has nearly all new appliances, a GAS RANGE, brand new carpets, and fresh paint. Behind the walls and ceiling is cement. I haven't heard a sound from my neighbors since I've lived here (the girl above me even has yappy dogs!). The window glass is likely single pane- but it's an EXTREMELY QUIET complex. Unless you're unlucky enough to have someone engaged in a loud conversation about 2 feet from your window, you really have nothing to worry about. The times that I've placed maintenance requests were only for minor items, to keep the place looking GREAT (I can be a little OCD..). It's worth noting that recently, a blonde staff member in the office took my very minor work order and made me feel TOTALLY APPRECIATED like it was the most important issue of the day! She followed up so well, I would get unexpected calls with little updates and just to let me know she cared and was working on it. I felt spoiled. Maintenance has always been fast, responsive, and friendly. One I met from Flagstaff was really a good guy. If there was a chance they were busy and wouldn't be able to make it over that day to take care of an issue, the office staff would always let me know ahead of time. And sometimes maintenance would even make it over anyway. The one concern that I have with Solara is safety and theft. Once of my neighbors had his apartment broken into and robbed twice and a person above me had her window pried opened but nothing stolen. There are a couple of areas nearby that have had other problems recently. I don't think Solara is especially unique in that and I'm sure other communities throughout Tempe contend with the same issues. However, Solara could do a better job keeping the gates CLOSED, especially at night. They fixed 2 of the front vehicle gates but there are others which remain open, including the gates by the back mailboxes. I think that if Solara made it a priority to take care of this issue it would be the biggest step they could take to creating a truly incredible living environment. I'd give Solara 5 stars overall.

Safety: This is not a gated community. The homeless walk in and out pretty comfortably. I have seen high homeless guys casually taking a stroll in the night where there are children playing alone nearby. And I am not even kidding when I say that I have seen the police cars go around the community at least 20-30 times. This is not normal. I have seen people get arrested. BIGGEST of all- there was a shooting right behind my unit- someone fired two shots and got arrested later. VERY SKETCHY place with SKETCHY neighbors. It is something everyday- some sort of police activity in the area everyday. 4. Smoking: My family doesnâ€TMt smoke. On paper, this is a smoke free community. But irl, several neighbors smoke every single day around where I live. The neighbors above me smoked so much weed that it used to travel through the vents and seep through our clothes and bedsheets. Thereâ€TMs this stench of weed etched into every inch of our house due to the amount of smoke coming through the vents and the air. There is smoking in the common areas, in the walkways and outside houses. Somedays, we couldnâ€TMt sleep due to the amount of smoke we were passively smoking ourselves. 5. AC/Water/Electricity issues: This community was built around the 1970s. Now with such an old construction comes plumbing and electricity issues. During peak summer, our unit went up to 86 degrees due to no AC. The AC stopped working for around 10 days community wide due to some issue. After a few days, they provided us with 1 portable AC per unit. What about AC in the other room or the kitchen or the bathroom or the living room? NO AC. We all had to sleep in one room with no cooling in the other areas. The house was absolutely uninhabitable and itâ€TMs not legal for the communities to have houses beyond 82 degrees in the summer. We had an attorney come over and sign paperwork to complain against the community. The neighbors above me had shower leaking issues. The construction is so bad and old that the water used to seep through the roof and it used to shower on me when using the toilet. Yellow stench water. Absolutely unacceptable. We had to use buckets to collect this water to prevent from flooding the bathroom. It took about one month to get this to managementâ€TMs attention. There is water repair and shut off notice like once a week. There are days when water is shut off for the full day. The plumbing system, AC and electricity wires systems are very old and broken. The electricity and water bills are very high some months. This is because they donâ€TMt ave a direct meter to your home through SRP or something similar. They split between all residentsâ€TM usage. So even if you donâ€TMt use anything because youâ€TMre out on vacation or something for a long time- you still pay for your neighbors usage. 6. Amenities: There is a key to access amenities. However, none of the amenities are ever locked- making it accessible to non-residents. I wanted to go for a swim the other day, but there was this big bachelor group that pulled in, dirtied the pool surrounding by partying, dumped all the trash at the leasing office and sped out. The fitness center was vandalized a while ago, no repair services begun till date. The gym was closed for a very long time. We keep paying amenities fees with no amenities. The pool is not cleaned everyday. There is dog poop everywhere- pet owners are irresponsible and donâ€TMt clean after themselves. The community does not take action against them or arrange cleaners to clean it. It just remains there, stinks and decomposes. 7. Management: They are very friendly when they get you to sign the lease. Once you become a resident, you are ignored. We sent countless emails with absolutely no response from the management- not once. They may answer if you call in- but people canâ€TMt always call in due to work. Even if you call in to report, they will just direct you to the maintenance report portal. Management overall does not care about the residents and is not responsive to a single email. They brought this rule to keep the patios clean without any other items in patio except patio furniture. We had a SINGULAR chain in our patio, mind you- ONE CHAIR. We couldnâ€TMt buy any â€œpatioâ€� furniture so used our chair instead. Management immediately fined us for having ONE CHAIR (later removed after disputing). My question to the management is, according the rules your attorney prepared for you regarding residentsâ€TM maintenance and if you have the right to fine them without second thoughts, what about the rules you overwrite? What about the horrendous laundry rooms? What about the regular AC/water shut off? What about the safety you promised? We all signed the lease trusting you to abide by your rules as well. If you expect discipline from residents, we except the same discipline, respect and commitment towards your residents as well. PROS: The trees/greenery is nice. Location is good, grocery stores, gas stations, schools and other places are close by. Rent is comparatively affordable. Management was helpful when the catastrophe hit. Nothing much to say Overall, as you can see, I had a pretty rough stay for a year. Canâ€TMt wait to get out. So many things at so many times took a toll on my mental health. Never thought my first time in Tempe would be so rough. It is also my fault that I didnâ€TMt do an in-person tour and thorough research before signing this last minute lease. Please do your research before signing the lease, this is just my experience. I hope other people find this review helpful before signing the lease. THIS IS A BIG FAT NO FROM ME.

author: wschromm
review_text: It wouldn't be fair of me to not leave a review for these apartments. I have lived here for a year now and it has been one of the worst rental experiences of my life. One year ago I signed a lease for a ground-floor 2 bedroom 2 bathroom apartment. The night we moved in our sink overflowed with our neighbors runoff from there laundry machine. After putting in multiple complaints with the office, they finally sent a plumber to clean out our sink. All of the maintenance staff for Solara seemed amazed at the fact this was happening so I figured this should be the end of it. Within the week it occurred again. The second maintenance worker figured the problem would be resolved by "running water through the sink to dislodge the clog created by the plumber." Again, I had hopes this would help, but highly doubted the logic of the employee. Since then, this has occurred numerous times and I have been told by management that this is, "something that I will just have to live with." When I confronted the head of maintenance about this, he informed me that this is a problem with one out of every four apartments due to the style of the plumbing. This was definitely not something I was informed of prior to signing my lease. The next issue began two months into the lease and has continued the entirety of my term. We received our bill in the mail and were shocked to see that a mysterious $35 charge was added. Now, I understand that isn't much, but being a college student on a budget, every little bit counts. I went to the management to figure out where this charge came from and was informed that this was an error in their billing system. They assured me this would not occur again. Sadly, this has occurred 10 times now and IS NOT BECAUSE OF LATE RENT. Each month, I had to walk to the office where they assured me that a "billing error" was the reason for the charge. I was even reassured by the district manager of Holland Residential that this issue would be resolved. The staff at Solara is constantly changing. Don't expect the agent that handles the signing of your lease to be employed longer than a month or two. Not only are they constantly hiring new staff members, who never take the time to remember names or faces, but they are some of the rudest and most judgmental people I have met. One employee in particular, who I will name "L" is the worst. Not once have I been greeted by her or seen her greet a resident in the many times I have been to the office the past four months of her employment. She talks down to you as if you don't understand English and when questioned about a policy, treats it as an attack. Near the end of my lease, I was looking for new locations and decided to see what rate I would get on a single bedroom/bathroom at Solara and if continuing my lease would result in any discounts on the rent. When I arrived at the office I was again handled by "L" who informed me that before I could see what rates and rooms were available I would need to sign paperwork guaranteeing my stay for another year, as well as, pay an $80 fee. This was also required before I could even see what the model unit looked like. When my girlfriend, who was with me, asked what the rates would be for a non-continuing resident, L again informed us that the paperwork would need to be signed before any tours or quotes could be given. Finally, they make many promises that they will not keep. Upon signing my lease, I was assured that the fixed utility rate would not increase as the lease contracts all prices including utility rate. However, December 15th, 2011, I received a notice stating that as of January 1st, 2012, utilities would increase, per unit, by $17.80. I was also assured during the lease signing that when the lease was up, a 30 day notice of moving out would be required by the office. It is now 42 days until my lease expires and I was informed by "L" that the notice requires 60 days and that I would have to wait 60 days from submitting the paperwork to leave, which would result in my rent increasing by nearly $300 to the month-by-month rate for the remainder of my lease. I understand that I m only one person and that everyone s experiences at Solara may differ, but I find it very hard to believe that all of this would occur during one lease. Please take this to heart when considering Solara. I don't want anyone to go through the annoyances I had to endure.

author: Current Resident 333025
review_text: The grounds are decent and the apartments are roomy. But most of them are old and have cheap parts. Some of the office staff can be dismissive and downright rude at times (Harlie and Todd are the only ones I feel like actually care about their jobs). Maintenance is awful. Be prepared to fight for any areas you need fixed and stay on them, otherwise it won't get done. Renewals have been pretty high. I pay almost $200 more a month now than when I moved in three years ago. There are flat rate utilities, but those can and have increased mid rent cycle multiple times. And there are frequent issues with plumbing and AC, so on average at least once a week, one of them is not working and needs to be turned off. Biggest issue is the apartments are HOT in the winter. They control the AC and will not turn it on until it's "warm" out. The apartments are poorly ventilated with large glass walls that will cook your rooms with no way to cool them off (literally I have two square foot windows in my bedroom and living room that are in the corner of the room with no way to help airflow). I will say the grounds are clean and the remodel has helped the exterior look nicer and I have never had a bug problem besides a few ants, but that's about all it has going for it. Oh and if you don't like college neighbors, stay away. Shame on me for not thinking that college kids would be loud at all hours of the day and night, but I have had a string of noisy neighbors. I don't even use my living room any more because I can't hear my TV over the noise most nights. Oh and there are safety issues too. The "security gates" have no code or locks, so they are open most of the time. Even when they're closed, you can just pull up close and they will open automatically. I've come home more than once to cops. And there are on again off again drug problems. And a group of transients who will hang out in the complex during the day. I don't feel safe a lot of the time and am very grateful I have a dog. Bottom line, I don't think they care about making this complex actually BE better, they're just making it look better.

author: Current Resident 653286
review_text: With every bad experience, I've tried giving these people the benefit of the doubt by assuming it was just a one-time thing and that their management would get better should there be a "next time." Hope you're prepared to read this because tonight was the last straw for me. With the countless issues I've had here, I'm going to outline a few because they are my favorite examples of why nobody should live here. Last night my sink randomly flooded my entire kitchen. I called the office this morning and talked to the only person in management that actually cares about residents, Erin, and asked for a maintenance request because it was an emergency. I came home from work to my cabinets open and a plunger sitting next to my kitchen sink, but the problem had still not been resolved. Thinking that maybe it could just be clogged or something that was our fault, I went to the store and bought 2 large bottles of Drain-o, came home and filled both sides of the sink. That still not resolving the problem, I called and asked if the maintenance guy could come back and finish fixing it, which they said was no problem and that he "should be there shortly." Three hours passes and he literally doesn't even show up. It's now 9:30 at night and every time the upstairs neighbor uses their water, my sink starts overflowing with disgusting liquid. I called the apartment hotline literally ten times and every time it prompts you to press a number all you hear is "invalid option" with an immediate hang up following it. The emergency maintenance line doesn't work, the message option doesn't work so I can't even leave management a message telling them that because their maintenance guy didn't show up, I now have a lake in my kitchen. I am quite literally wearing boots in my kitchen (because any other shoe would not suffice to keep my feet from getting disgusting) and filling buckets with water because there is so much of it and nobody in this apartment complex can help because the office just so happens to be closed and that is THE ONLY way you can get ahold of anyone (depending on if they actually answer the phone.) Here's another fun example: About a month ago there was a death in my immediate family and my sister had to fly across the country to try to help out with the funeral. She would only be gone for a maximum of 3 days, so i didn't see the issue with watching her animal while she was away in an obviously extreme case. A day later I get an eviction notice on my door saying that if I don't pay a fine of $175 and remove the animal immediately, I will be removed from the property. When calling management, (which, by the way is a Godsend if they ever actually answer.) I was put on the phone with 3 people who are obviously incapable of human emotion. Erin tried to help me work something out but they still didn't drop the fee, which I thought was pretty ridiculous considering it's a death in the family and not a permanent situation. Keep in mind that I'm the only other family member in Arizona, a full time student and have a full time job. I've never been late on rent and never had any issues on my end with Solara. Or here's a nice one if you enjoy cops! They are here every. single. night. Normally I would think "Oh, I'm a young girl, I like having a police officer around in case something bad ever happens." Not in this apartment complex. When you don't have sketchy people following you home when you're working out at night then banging on your door at 3 in the morning and leaving creepy notes (yes, this literally happened), you have cops raiding your next-door neighbor, complete with full body armor and riot shields! It makes you feel REALLY at home. Because who wouldn't want to come home from a long day at work to that, right? THEN when you call the office to ask what the hell is going on, they say "oh, someone couldn't get into their apartment and it was a safety issue." I'm just going to stop right there, because obviously you guys get the point. I can't even go into every time they've managed to piss me off because this would be way longer than it is now. I'm done. I know it seems nice because it's affordable and you can take the orbit to campus, but please just do yourself a favor and spare the hair-tearing out by not moving in. It's not in a nice neighborhood. You will literally be so upset with your decision, and this is coming from someone who literally waited a year before writing a bad review because I wanted to see the good in this complex. I'm sorry if I put a damper in your apartment-seeking process but I wish I had taken the reviews before me more seriously.

After a miserable three days without hot water I took my complaints to the office, where the staff/manager just shrugged me off and said they couldn't do anything. The water problems continue to this day (10 months later) and I can expect no hot water/ water pressure about twice a month. Ants: Horrendous ant problem, be prepared. "Flat rate utilities": This is a joke, Solara's "flat rates" are raised every three months. In the course of a year I was paying about $40 more for utilities on a STUDIO apartment. Neighbors: There are always 2-3 cops stationed at entrances at anytime & lots of screaming and fighting any night of the week. This is no joke: I CAN HEAR MY NEIGHBORS SNEEZE. The walls are paper-thin, you can literally hear everything from people snoring to cupboard's shutting. The complex is crawling with shady people; including a 6' giant who hangs out in the parking lot at night with no shoes. There was even a reported rape here in 2011. And one of my delightful neighbors left a DEAD KITTEN STUFFED IN A BAG in front of my door. Message to Women: I've never been so scared for my safety. At night you can hear girls screaming and people threatening to kill each other. There's definitely a lot of domestic violence and drug activity here. Solara is a magnet for creepy old men, the guy that lived across from me would watch me from his patio everyday. The same guy was inexplicably in front of my apartment when I came home late one night. He tried to start a conversation, but I managed to duck past him into my apartment.

author: Current Resident 58933
review_text: I have lived at Solara at Mill Avenue since 2009. Unfortunately, it has not been the best experience. The worst part of my experience has been the management and office staff. They are very unprofessional and offer incorrect information. Some of the issues I had were every year, regardless of how long I had stayed with them, my rent would go up by $100-200 to where I finally couldn't afford staying there any longer. Utilities were included, which was a plus, however, you could not control the air. I had put on my lease I had cats, and was given the wrong amount for the pet deposit and had to pay additional fees because I was given the wrong information. I also had an issue with my apartment facing the sun when it was hottest in the day, and the entire wall was a window. The windows were great, until summer. I placed thermal curtains in the window and after two years of having them in the windows was told to "take them down" to have a uniform community. I asked management how I can hang my curtains, without a way to keep the thermal curtains in the windows? I had to have the tension rods in the window, in front of the blinds, as there was no wall to hang the curtains. They brought me to the "show" apartment and showed how they hung the curtains, which was not the same window in my apartment. I brought the office staff to my apartment and showed them my issue, and they stated "I don't know, figure it out". After this, I continued to get 10 Day Notices of intent to terminate my lease due to stupid issues that they never had called me about. They just placed a notice on my door without calling me. When I attempted to call about the issues, they would never call back after I left a message. I received notices for having my cats, when they were on my lease, and not having the 300, .00 in liability insurance requested. I had insurance, just not the $300, they requested. When I did have it, they gave me a notice for when it got transferred to my new home owners policy, even though I was moving out. I had received 3-4 10 day notices in two months. When I was moving out, they had confused my date of move out. I gave my notice in January of 2014 and when I paid my rent in February, they called asking "I thought you were moving out?". They require a 60 day notice, which is what I gave. Maintenance came by my apartment 3-4 times because they couldn't remember when I was moving out. When I went to obtain the information to break my lease, they had my file on Wednesday and had given me the amount. I went back Thursday to pay the amount to break my lease, they had lost my file and continued to ask if I had given 60 day notice. They are completely unprofessional and unkind, and do not appear to know what they are doing. On top of that, I had been notifying them since the beginning that I moved in that there was green or gray mold or mildew growing on the vents in my apartment. They never came to fix the said issues, and it got worse over the years. My grandparents say its due to the cooler system they use, but I am almost positive they will charge me for this even though I have told them for the past four years it has been on my grates since I moved in. This apartment complex always states "Contact us, and we will attempt to help", but no one ever does. I call and leave messages and get no calls back. I get 10 day notices to terminate my lease without a single phone call from anyone in management or the office. I received no help for issues in my apartment and whenever I went up to the office was always waiting on the office staff to speak to me (They were either on their cell phones texting, or talking to each other).

review_text: The community is very nice and has a lot of very nice amenities. Instead of being helpful and constructive she continually criticized me for asking her a question she didn't know how I answer and was not speaking with an "inside voice". She was very abrasive and made me feel uncomfortable because I did not understand their online payment program and why it keeps failing to do what they designed it to do. It is now at the point where every time I go in there for help because they never answer their phones at the office, she gives me very dirty looks from across the room in her office. I don't think she is fit to be running that place, her office and desk is always a mess and paperwork for God knows what is always scattered all over her office and floor. Absolutely unorganized, unprofessional and unpleasant to speak with. There are many people with very big dogs at the property who do not pick up their animal waste (dog poop). When I moved in, I was told that there what is a size and weight limit for dogs and yet I see animals well over the threshold. Harley Moyes, the assistant manager is a much better suited candidate for a managerial position at Solara and is actually willing to talk, listen and help people in a friendly and professional manor. Also, Harley's office is very clean and organized and she always finds what she's looking for with ease. review_title: Expensive and you are on your own
review_text: We have been living here for more than 5 months and there are several issues 1) Staff is not friendly or welcoming, after you join. Just interested in arguing but not in discussing or understanding 2) Very poor resolution of service requests - First of all, you need to figure out on your own how and where to raise requests. The issues are endless, but I can give few examples - Raised a request for Patio light as it is not working. Someone came after few days, replaced the bulb and closed the issue as resolved and completed. My issue is still not resolved as there is no light - agree they replaced a new bulb, but there is no electricity supply, so it is of no use. When I went in person, staff just argued with me asking me to leave immediately and raise another request. I've raised 3 requests after that, all of them are closed as resolved, but still there is no light. Microwave oven is optional - they will not tell you this up front but charge the same rent as the unit that has microwave. Laundry (washer/dryer) not working for more than 2 weeks - there is no reply when I send an email. When I raised a request, as usual they closed it is as resolved with a message "We do not own or service the laundry equipment. The is a service number on the machines that we need to call for service. Residents are able to call this number as well". They won't tell you this at the time of joining. Equipment was not the issue, all machines are off for some reason. They don't want to check or reply politely. 3) Trash is very expensive - You must pay for trash pickup from your apartment and trash pickup from the community which is generally more than $80 per month. Received email that Gym is closed for maintenance 5 months back and no update after that. Swimming pool is not useful in winter anyway - there is no indoor pool. Without having amenities, you still need to pay each month 4) Your emails will be simply ignored without any reply as they are not important. There is only one way communication and only the property management emails are important which you cannot ignore 5) For that last 5 months, we never received itemized rent bill, though we requested and complained many times. You just need to pay the total amount posted without asking any questions - staff is not ready to understand or discuss as mentioned above. Only service personnel are good. They don't even offer you a seat to sit when you enter the office - after you join. Not useful, though we brought this to higher management notice. 6) Apartment unit won't be ready with all inspections, fixes and cleaning done. You are responsible to find all the issues after you join, raise the tickets and follow up - even if they were present before you join. We moved twice as we need to vacate the building because of Cloud/Micro burst and faced same issues both times. Overall expensive place with unfriendly staff and hidden issues.

author: Current Resident 111868
review_text: Well my experience started out fine. The community was quite, the office staff wasn't the friendliest, but they were helpful, and the apartment was clean, and seemingly upgraded. The last few months however have been h*ll. When we were having those really bad rain storms my entire wall started to leak. So much water came in so quickly while I was asleep that it soaked my new bed frame causing it to break. The complex would not replace my bed and neither would my renters insurance, because they stated it was a building defect not covered. Then the complex never did anything about the wall. It leaked again the next time it rained and I sent in another request and still nothing was done. I had 3 different maintenance men come to my apartment, with their dirty shoes, walk all throughout it, tell me they were gonna fix anything inside, but they would take a look outside and still nothing was done. There were never any checks for moisture or mold, which I was told there would be, and there is now disgusting staining on the walls, baseboards, and the floor boards are warped from all the water, and the next time it rains the same thing will happen. I DO NOT recommend this place to anyone. The staff has turned into the most rude horrible people to deal with, with the exception of the taller gentleman in the office, and they don't care at all about their residents. My recommendation would be to look for a community where people who work there, also live there. Its a good sign that the complex is way better taken care of, and is actually respectable.

author: Current Resident 930304
review_text: I really like Scottsdale Gateway. I find the size of the apartment to be more than adequate, it's very easy to keep clean, generally, all the services (AC, water, electricity) are very reliable, and the few times I've needed maintenance or had questions for local management, both have always been professional and courteous. I think the grounds are well-maintained and I love the pool areas and the convenience (and cost-savings) of the fitness center. I really like the proximity to Papago Park as it's such a great place to take my pup and let her run around and swim, and the dog-friendly facilities at the complex (the off-leash areas, the numerous clean-up cans that are always stocked w/ clean-up bags, plenty of grassy areas where I can walk her even in the middle of the day without worrying she'll burn her feet (yes, I will carry my Setter/Retriever across the concrete and high noon)). As you may have guessed, the fact Scottsdale Gateway is pet friendly is pretty important to me :). Generous amount of parking areas, timely garbage pickup, timely notification and frequent updates of unplanned problems w/ utilities (and prompt repair or work-around), the investment made in, and the upkeep of, the pool areas and the other grounds, the convenience of the laundry facilities along w/ the large number of washers and dryers, access to reasonably-priced, fast and reliable internet services - really, everything needed to live, comfortably, made Scottsdale Gateway a great and lucky choice. Plus, it turned out that this part of Tempe has great access to work in virtually any location, especially for tech. And, Scottsdale Gateway is affordable - there's a lot more to apartment living than just the apartment, and after thinking of all the services provided for the price, and writing them down, I think I just talked myself into renewing my lease. Thank you, the complex is much appreciated.

review_text: Where do I begin? I have lived here for a few years now. The first couple were not bad, the company left me alone to live in peace relatively most of the time, neighbors were average, the place was okay. Now I fully regret renewing my lease, I knew I should have moved. This place has been under constant construction/renovation/painting for over a year and who knows how many more to come. The new leasing center took a few months longer to build than they said with longer noise, dust and major parking issues. They just ripped down some big shade trees to put in new tiny ones, whenever that happens right before ripping up the pool at the beginning of summer when they could have done it in the winter when no one was using it and they were building the leasing center anyway. They renovated the pool near the Scottsdale Gateway leasing office in the winter, but those suckers at Solaire don't need the same consideration. By the way, it's now called Solaire, so they can sell it when they are done. Then they will probably start on Scottsdale Gateway again. This place has no brain running it, very apparent there is no common sense. Always trying to up the rent, for more dust,dirt and noise. They let you know the afternoon before decide to shut the water off all day or some other inconvenience. If they communicate with you about an issue, its rarely polite or professional. Kids play in the common areas often until 11pm, sometimes later, usually unsupervised, 7 days a week. There is a security patrol according to my lease, and I have seen him, about once a month and usually is just hanging with the kids. Kids pile rocks, dirt and other things on stairs so you almost fall first thing in the morning. Parking is a nightmare for you and your guests. When this lease is done, I'm done and out of here. I must say the maintenance staff are really quick and helpful here. As for anything else, I have nothing to recommend about this place that is really positive anymore.

We are always working hard to make sure we are improving our community and making it better for our residents. author: Current Resident 113832
review_text: I leased a studio for here for 5 months while my house was under renovation. It was essentially a storage unit with a shower. It was cheap and conveniently located just up the street from my work. Over 5 months, my dog and I spent the night 3 times. I never once turned on the stove or dishwater, and only kept water in the refrigerator. I never touched the thermostat. Over the last 3 months, I only went by on the 1st to pay rent and grab a load boxes to bring back to the house. My walk thru was scheduled on Monday, March 2nd although my lease didn't technically end until the 5th. On Sunday, we went to clear out the remaining boxes, sweep, and wipe everything down. When we arrived the door was unlocked and the apartment had been ransacked. All of the boxes were ripped open and disheveled. Sadly, the last of the boxes were full of things from my childhood, and some family things. Nothing of any real value, and to be honest I couldn't really tell if anything was missing. I hadn't gone thru some of them myself in years. So we decided against calling the police. I did however go down to the office to report it. After having me write down what happened, they told me that TWO of my neighbors had actually called to report hearing activity in the apartment over the weekend. Several of the office personnel knew my situation and that I wasn't living in the apartment, including the guy I was reporting to. I asked him why he didn't give me a f-ing courtesy call and he said "he didn't want to bug me". I took him back to the apartment and showed him that there were no signs of forced entry and implied that it was someone with access to a key. He was like "that's weird, because there are only 2 keys: the 1 you have, and the 1 in the office." Did I mention that the office personnel knew of my living situation? The following day, Monday, I return to do my walk-thru and turn in my keys. I sat there with my check book and ASKED if I owed anything for those few days into March. I was told NO, any remaining utilities would be deducted from my security deposit which I would receive by mail within 14 days. Fast forward about 6 weeks later, after being redirected and redirected and several unreturned voicemails, I finally got ahold of someone at their office in Seattle. According to him, BOTH my email and forwarding address were incorrect in their records. Long story short, he ended up emailing me a breakdown of where my $450 security deposit was going and that I in fact owe them $17. Among the deductions were prorated rent thru the 5th (even though they scheduled my walk-thru and took my keys on the 2nd), a $50 LATE FEE for not paying said rent on time, a cleaning fee (IF warranted, one would think should be taken out of the $200 nonrefundable deposit), the last month's utilities (fair), and "final" utilities which were 3X the cost of the monthly. We tried tirelessly to fight every line of it, ended up getting redirected to the voicemail of a supervisor up in Seattle, and now it's May and I still haven't heard back, let alone seen a penny. At this point I'm just checking my mail everyday for that bill for $17 which I imagine I'll indefinitely end up having to pay so this doesn't end up in collections and destroying my credit. Such. A. Nightmare. Stay away. They are crooks and clearly in the business of scamming deposits. I wish I would have checked Yelp beforehand, because I'm clearly not the 1st person they've done this to. Don't be the next.

author: Christie Lee
review_text: Blinded by their cheap rent and personable leasing staff (shout out to Commander - he's the man), I gave Scottsdale Gateway the benefit of the doubt when signing a 12 month contract with the property in February. One month later, my two bedroom apartment has been broken into and robbed with claims surpassing $10, between my roommate and myself. And conveniently enough Scottsdale Gateway failed to mention that their renters insurance does not cover personal items at the time I signed my lease. Anyhow, I asked the new manager about any previous criminal activity on the premises as well as the unit specifically and she assured me it had never happened within the Scottsdale Gateway community before. However, upon visiting raidsonline.com it was quite easy to find multiple police reports within even the past year that have happened on the grounds of Scottsdale Gateway. Some happening as close as a .01 mile radius of my apartment. See below: 4/26/2015: 8:30am: Burglary - Force 4/28/2015: 9:00pm: Burglary - No Force 4/28/2015: 12:00pm: Burglary - No Force 5/14/2015: 7:30am: Burglary - No Force 10/27/2015: 3:04pm: Burglary - No Force Note these are all burglaries close in proximity and comparable to the recent violation of my own "home", and all occurring within the past 12 months. The other reports of crime throughout the past year that took place on the Scottsdale Gateway property are equally worrisome: 6/8/2015: Motor Vehicle Theft 8/4/2015: Motor Vehicle Theft 9/27/2015: Aggravated Assault 11/1/2015: Motor Vehicle Theft 2/8/2016: Motor Vehicle Theft 3/18/2016: Motor Vehicle Theft I understand that such reports are not attractive to present to perspective tenants. However, I would expect the Scottsdale Gateway management to be a) aware and b) honest about the recent activity on their grounds upon request, especially with it being public information. In other words: Do not move here. It is not safe. It is not well managed. And it is infested with cats.
response_text: Hi Christie- We are very sorry to hear about your experience. Please reach out to me at scottsdalegatewaymgr@greystar.com or 480.945.8423 as soon as you can so we can discuss. Thank you.

author: Current Resident 745422
review_title: You get what you pay for in this case, very little.
review_text:
Good:
- Close proximity to restaurants, bars and Mill Street shops.
- Pools and laundry facilities are never crowded.
- Maintenance staff fix problems quickly, without any quibbles.
- Cheap, for Tempe. Our "junior one-bed" was $519 per month - just over $606, with all the utilities etc.

Bad:
- If you don't like cockroaches, don't move here! The complex has a cockroach problem and although we kept our apartment extremely clean, kept all the plugholes stopped up and sprayed Raid around, we still had trouble with them. We were told to expect to see some when we moved to Arizona, but we didn't expect to see quite as many as this. The worst was when one crawled up my pant leg - in broad daylight, as I was sitting at my computer. We also found an egg sac in the closet (unhatched, fortunately - a dozen baby roaches would have come out of there!). I went to see the staff about this and they put our apartment on a list of apts., for a pest control man to come round and spray the place. They said he came every week to do this. I didn't know if this was a good thing or a bad thing! It seemed to me that the roaches were just circulating around the building - when they were sprayed out of one apt., they moved onto other apts., and so on.
- This area suffers from vehicle crime. Police cars were often present in the parking lots during the day and the night. When we moved here we bought bikes but other residents advised us against keeping them outside, in the cycle ranks.
- The apts were small and poky. Our "junior one bed" was a 450 sq ft room with a half wall in the middle.
- When we moved in we were told that the majority of residents were students and young professionals. But it seemed to us that many of the people here were section 8.
- Another resident told us that there was a drug problem here. I didn't experience anything to support that claim. Although there was a lot of door-knocking and brawling late at night.

To those moving to Tempe for the first time: why don't you look at Mesa? You can get much more bang for your buck there, and cities round here all look the same anyway.

review_text: I would NOT recommend this complex. I rented a studio apartment for a good price for the location (and quiet community), but had several problems that caused me to enjoy the experience less and less. First, maintenance never responded when called, other than to inform me that they received my request. Additionally, the water in my particular unit was shut off almost weekly for pipe repairs, though it was not on a consistent schedule and I was only informed the first two times it was shut-off--after that it was a gamble as to whether or not the water would be working when I got up for work/school. Second, the turnover rate for management is ridiculously small: every time I walked in the office (at least once a month) the entire staff was new, which caused problem when it came to reporting to me the CORRECT rent amount due per month and when answering questions. The complex decided to go "paperless" at about month #2 into my lease and yet never sent out a properly functioning, complete e-mail. After about month #4 I receive no e-mail whatsoever and could only ever be told how much I owed for rent if I was able to walk in to the office and talk to someone (heaven forbid someone answers the office phone once in a while). Also, the "great deal" I was offered and pestered about to resign my lease was at least $50 MORE than what I had been paying for rent. Thirdly, though the complex seems nice and is quiet, lights are often broken, the apartments themselves are old and therefore break easily (I was down to a single, half-functioning stovetop coil and a from door that would not close completely by the time I moved), and a few crimes have occurred in and around the complex (possibly because of how dark it is). It is liveable and semi-safe, but I would definitely keep and eye peeled for safety hazards associated with both the shady neighborhood and the old appliances/apartments. Also, do not trust any staff member that tells you that the apartment is "old and worn" and that in general they will be a bit more lenient on the condition of the carpet, walls, and other features--I cleaned my tub/shower to a point that it was cleaner than when I moved in, yet I was charged for a "dirty tub". author: luvit2008
review_text: I've been here less than a year,but in that time the AC has gone out no fewer than 4 times. Twice in the last week. Not really acceptable in the middle of July. Their website claims 24 hour maintenance, however, when the call was made yesterday concerning the AC, we were told that they would leave a message for the office in the morning. Hell, I could do that. As a consequence, cooking was out, forcing us to go out for dinner. Not easy when only one of us is working at $8 an hour. And being it's Sunday, we'll probably have to wait til noon to get any response. By that time it'll be well over 100 degrees. The staff is courteous, but that doesn't necesarily mean they care. Maintenance is short staffed, so I can understand that they don't always get here right away. However, it's obvious that they don't have a full working knowledge of the various skills required. I say this having worked in building maintenance for 10 of the last 20 years. Case in point. They came to clean the coils in our unit (totally clogged, no light passing thru). After spraying what was apparently window cleaner on one side, they called it fixed. After they left I went and purchased a bottle of proper coil cleaner for $10. Came home, removed the coil unit from the blower and spent the next 1 1/2 hours cleaning the fins and flushing out the rust from the pipes. Now it works, at least when the main unit sends cold water out to the buildings. But with the way the windows and front door leak air, it's a losing battle to keep out the heat. Hot water in the shower fluctuates constantly, like someone is flushing repeatedly. Roaches occasionally, but not a serious problem. There does seem to be an issue with the security of your spare keys. Ours have been 'lost' 3 times. I've heard of similar stories from other residents. Electricity is included, at least for some folks. Don't know about everyone. Rents can vary by several hundred for the same floorplan, we're on the low end at 560. Neighbors can be noisy, but no more so than anywhere else. Although the single pane, loose in the frame windows certainly don't stop any noise, least of all the airplanes that fly over from 5 AM to 11 PM. Very dog friendly, I've got 2 big dogs. Pet deposit was low. At move-in we made a list of approximately 15 deficiencies, mostly minor, but items that would cost us upon move-out. That list was lost once by the office, may have been lost again since being replaced. All in all, I would not live here again.

author: Current Resident 93681
review_text: I have lived in Sierra Vista 1 for two years. Pros: I love the location: 10-minute drive to Sky Harbor Airpot, 5 minutes from ASU by car or bus or 15 minutes walking. 4 bus routes go by the nearest intersection: Red Line which can take you to campus or to the airport no need to call a cab, a shuttle or bug someone to drop you off or pick you up), 30, 44, and 62, all of which go by ASU. I haven't had any major issues with maintenance, but occasionally things do come up. They have replaced all the machines in the laundry facility; they are now operated with cards (no need to carry around a load of quarters anymore). Cons The apartments are old and a bit overpriced. I didn't mind so much because the electricity used to be included with the rent so you could save lots of money (You could run your AC all you want, not a small detail in blazing hot Arizona!). However as of this month electricity is no longer included, so you might find a better deal somewhere else. Occasionally you might see a roach and need management to send someone to your place to spray it. With all the parking space available, surprisingly few spots are covered and you have to pay extra for covered parking. Overall, I don't think it's that bad. I think it's good for people who don't need the latest fanciest most fashionable place. I'd totally recommend it if they had the electricity deal going on. Now I think you might find a better deal elsewhere. Not so bad over all though. I'm moving out of state and saying good bye to Sierra Vista for good.

author: Current Resident 830970
review_text: Its location is great, especially if you're a student, and for once, the maintenance team at a location is rather timely, friendly, and willing to assist. I'm so unbelievably thankful that I was able to sign a 6-mo lease only, because I would move out yesterday if I could. We've had PAGES of complaints regarding roach infestation both inside our apartment, and around our building. All we've gained from our complaining and demanding is them saying "pour bleach down your sink" and some half spray jobs. Roaches are terrible pests and as a business offering rent-free living, they are pitiful. They say they've received no other complaints, yet we talk to our neighbors and those in OTHER BUILDINGS and hear the same issue. My hope right now is that I can survive the next few weeks and not take any roaches with me to my new apartment as I will NOT be renewing lease. author: Current Resident 372073
review_text: I have never dealt with management staff so manipulative and incompetent. Maintenance is a constant issue and will not be taken care of in a timely fashion, if ever. You will be towed if your plates are even a day expired. Lighting in the parking lot is terrible and comes on way too late in the winter--I never felt safe. I did actually my apartment--it was cute, decently sized, I personally didn't have major noise issues. I'm actually going to leave some tips if you unfortunately do live here--if you have issues with office staff, download the ARIZONA RESIDENTIAL LANDLORD TENANT ACT. Guess what? Leaving residents without AC is illegal. Failing to fix maintenance issues in a timely fashion can get you out of your lease. So, I suggest submitting any complaints/maintenance requests in writing, and cite the code that says if they don't fix it within X days you are exercising your right to get out of the lease. Have office staff PUT IN WRITING any promises they make. After getting screwed over many times, I started putting things in writing and citing codes, and that made them shape up a little. If you have consistent/major issues, there's an official Arizona landlord/tenant dispute counselor downtown--she's great and incredibly helpful: http://phoenix.gov/nsd/programs/landlord/index.html

author: canonlyhope22
review_title: Air Conditioning Down 28 Days and Counting
review_text: UPDATE ON SITUATION AND PHOTOS 09/20/2010 Office DOES NOT return phone calls, that is if you can get hold of the office staff and not the answering service when calling during business hours. Someone had busted the light and trashed the main laundry room,clothes were thrown all over the place. The laundry money machine was broken into,laundry company was here today handling the matter. In the smaller Animal feces in front yards. Dropped off a list of repairs that are still waiting to be finished, some dating back to our original move in date. Office manager stated that someone from maintenance would have to stop by and look,today being Monday and still waiting. Put in a a couple of calls to the office today, first time the call was answered by answering service(call was put in at approximately 1pm this afternoon), having been put on hold for more than five minutes I hung up and decided to call back later. Placed call to office about an half and hour later, and was told by the office staff member that answered the phone that the office manager was busy, left a message and number for the office manager to call me back. I just got off the phone with the manger(as almost four hours should have been sufficient time to return a phone call) When I spoke with the manager the answer for why I have not received a call as yet was "Oh, I thought someone had already called you." Do you not know? I asked about the other issues listed and was asked "which ones?" I mentioned the list of repairs that was dropped off on Thursday and was told "Yes I have that paper" at least they know what needs to be done. Supposedly a member of maintenance will be by today to take a look at the situations, once they are done with the service call that they are currently working on. Maybe it is just me but, I tend to not trust what I have been told. The main air conditioning unit broke down on 17 July called to the office and was told it was the main portion of the unit and would be in working order that night (Saturday) called the next morning and was told will be up by that evening (Sunday) called the next day and was told that the main unit was fixed but, had caused issues with individual units. On Monday 20 July 2010 we placed a work order maintenance came out two days later and told us all we needed was a filter and that they were on order and would be in a day or two. Three days later when no filter shows I call again and am told they are still waiting for them to come in. I called every other day to see if they were in, they were not. Finally, after calling for almost two weeks I call and I am told the filters were in and one would be brought to my apartment, which it was within one half hour. We replace the filter and think that it will take at least a few hours if not overnight for the apartment to cool down. The next morning our apartment was still eighty five degrees, even while running two box fans, two desk fans and a mini turbo fan. Once again I call the office and was told that maintenance would come by first thing the next morning. Which they did, they proceeded to clean the system and we were told that after they were done and a few hours wait we would start feeling the cool air. still 85 Once again I call up to the office they send down another maintenance guy who says it is the thermostat it is not working properly so he will order the part. He does tell me he is not sure when it will be in but he will order the part. Okay I called the office a few times last week to see if the part was in, of course not yet. I called yesterday( Monday) and was told that the part was in and she would get a hold of maintenance and call me back. Needless to say I did not get a call back. Today Tuesday 17 August three days shy of a month with no remedy in sight. I call the office and get the answering service it is 9:05am the office is supposed to be open. So I wait and call again at 11:12am again the answering service. Okay so maybe there was an issue I would call later.At 3:29pm I called and got the office and asked to speak to a manager was told they were out to lunch and I would get a call when they returned. Having not received a call by 4:40pm, I called again was asked to hold then while on hold for several minutes was asked to hold again, this time a few minutes, when the phone was picked up, I was told that it was going to be a while so I would get a call back. I said I wanted a call back before the office closed for the day. Needless to say I did not receive one back. Now, I can understand there are many things involved when managing a property. It upsets me that now I have the feeling that we are just getting the run around. We pay our rent on time abide by the rules, and respect our neighbors. I had mentioned to both management as well as maintenance that this is not just a comfort issue but, a health risk as well. I know I may be sounding a bit snippy but since this situation has been going on Tempe has been issued several excessive heat WARNINGS. One of the thing they tell you to do is stay indoors where it is cool Well, my indoors are not cool. We are just about at our wits end with this place The turnover of staff both office and maintenance seems to be a deterrent to resolving these issues. I am honestly worried as to what is going to "break down" next. I feel we have been more than patient up to this point but, we are getting tired of things not being done something really has to be done. UPDATE ON SITUATION 05/26/2010 New Property manager has been open to listening to issues with apartment. As of the posting of this review the roach situation is being remedied, seems there was a small hole behind the refrigerator as well as a metal plate that was loose under the sink that was where the roaches were gaining entrance into the apartment. Seems as if the roaches had traveled from another apartment and the property manager has assured me that she will look into the situation. Maintenance filled the holes and the exterminator has been out to spray. Seems to be working so far we are seeing less roaches in the apartment. Several other issues that we had notified the apartment manager of have either already been taken care of or are in the process of resolving. Hopefully things will continue to improve. I still would suggest touring the actual apartment you will be renting before signing a lease. Unfortunately it has been one thing after another. First off got a call the night before our move that our apartment would not be ready for the date agreed upon at the signing of our lease. So okay how is this issue solved? Received a call back later on the night and to remedy the situation we would be given an apartment other than the original one, no problem or so we thought. Due to the fact that we were moving ourselves we did not actually see more of the apartment other than the time we were going in and dropping off our boxes. I know I should have looked over the apartment but, at the time we had a deadline on which we had to meet to get our rental truck back. So we finally settle in and the first thing that greets us are roaches, in our bathroom kitchen and later on the evening even in our bedroom. So we call the office (note it is now after hours so we get the service) and inform them of the situation. The next morning we get a call saying we will be first on the list to have an exterminator spray 4 days from the time we called. We were told when they did arrive that they would have to come every week for a while and possibly bomb. I do not know but, I would imagine all that should have been done prior to anyone moving in. Okay so we figure lets try the weekly spraying and go from there. Needless to say they did not show this week so the problem is NOT getting under control. We also gave the rental office a list of repairs that need doing over a week ago and they have fixed one of the issues listed yesterday We were told that maintenance would be by today as well to take care of the other issues they never showed. We are hoping this is a rare occurrence and that ALL the issues will be remedied in a timely manner.. If you are going to rent here I would strongly suggest that you make sure you see the actual apartment you will be renting before you sign a lease.

author: Current Resident 527544
review_text: Now, first off, let me say that I did not hate living here. I'm a very poor college student who liked the price range and the fact that all utilities were included except water. I think my day-to-day living experience might have been better because I was right next to the office & surrounded by college students or quiet people. My biggest complaints about living there were the crusty carpets and the HUGE roach problem. Even if you could kill them off, there were roach carcasses everywhere. It sucked. Now, that being said, I can't really report this place/area being safe. One night after I got home from work, a stranger followed me into my apartment. I defended myself and he clocked me pretty good and then left. I dont know if he wanted to rob me, or rape me or was just a high individual but I'm glad neither happened. The police were called and i was in shock for a while. I know it's not the staff's fault but it was a really bad thing to have happened. When I went to the office the next day to let them know I was going to need to go. And I think they meant well, but they really questioned me about what happened and it was in front of the whole staff and other residents. It was really embarrassing and I was upset that they did that. They didn't even know (or were informed) at all that a resident had been attacked in an apartment so close to the office when there had been around 10 cops there the night before. Though Yvonne (who I've actually known from when I lived in another complex) I am sure was just very genuinely concerned. She wanted to know what the person looked like so she could keep an eye out. But these were kind of things I was not ready to share with everyone else. Again, not the staff's fault. Yvonne, Matt and Ryan (i think thats his name) were always pretty kind to me. The apartments aren't great by any means but you get what you pay for and it's great for college students. Believe it or not, I would recommend it. Because, despite what happened, I liked living there. It suited my needs. Just know that this area isnt very safe.

author: gradstu22
review_text: I have lived at the Sierra Vista Apartments for two years now, and it is not nearly as bad as most of the reviews on this site make it out to be. I have had issues with loud neighbors, but frankly that sort of thing occurs everywhere, especially in a party-school college town like this one. For the most part, the staff is courteous and helpful, and repairs happen quickly. Given that you don't pay the electrical bill, I'd say it's a pretty good deal. Also, this part of Tempe does have a fair amount of crime-- but you can look online to see how many times the police have been called to each apartment complex, and for what-- and other apartment complexes in the area have much worse records for car break-ins, etc. I did have a problem with roaches at first, but it was nothing that a few roach poison traps couldn't take care of. At any rate, I would live at the Sierra Vista apartments for another year! It's not the finest apartment complex ever, but it costs much less than others in the area. Just exercise common sense, and don't leave your car unlocked on the window rolled down (and don't leave CDs sitting out in plain view in your car!) and buy renter's insurance (as you should do anywhere!) and you will be fine.

When you sign up to move here they just tell you the utilities are included and sugar code everything. But let me tell you 5 months out of the year your AC is not on due to the winter season (haha in AZ). You have to have store bought fans and open your windows to get some air circulating in your house and who cares if you are an allergy sufferer like me. Everything breaks down here. Maybe 6 or 7 times our toilet has overflooded and got all our carpet wet. So there is some type of plumbing/sewage problem. The parking lot is in terribly bad shape. No value in the tenants here, while the front office looks so nice. Our car has been broken and vandalized into twice. Party after party. I have called the police here like 30 times for noise and domestic disputes around here. The laundry room is a mess and junkies walk around here. Don't move here. It is not for you and your family.

author: Current Resident 172879
review_text:
I've been here two years and am anxious to get the hell out. The problem isn't with the apartment or the management, it is with the neighborhood and the tenants. Here is what I've encountered:

- My girlfriend's car was burglarized the third night were were here. My truck was burglarized two days later IN BROAD DAYLIGHT 20 MINUTES AFTER I GOT HOME
- An attempt was made to steal my bike that was locked to the railing.
- Yelling and screaming domestic disputes at all hours of the day and night every day.
- Constant partying throughout the complex every night of the week at all hours of the night.
- A woman was attacked and nearly raped on the stairs leading to my apartment one night. The attacker ran away when my neighbors and I came out in response to the screaming.
- Kids running rampant stomping up and down the stairs that lead to my apartment (they don't live in either of the apartments the stairs go to).
- All kinds of creepy people roaming around.
- Apparently is the preferred place to abandon vehicles and dump stolen cars.
- AC/Heat is on central boiler so you can't make the decision to switch from AC to heat when the temperature drops at night in the fall. You have to wait until the switch the whole system over.
- Hot water mains constantly breaking so there was no hot water.

There was good stuff about the place though.
- The rent was cheap and included most of the utilities.
- The apartment itself was in good condition.
- Maintenance was usually quick to fix problems (provided the office got the work order to them). They also did good job trying to pick up trash every morning.
- Lots of parking spaces on my end of the complex. The rest of the place seemed crowded.

If you like to party or don't mind your neighbors partying, then, live here. It's cheap and close to a lot of stuff. If you're like me and like "quiet time, you need to find something that isn't in Tempe.

author: MrTempe

author: lcr4489
review_text: Moved into my apartment about a week ago(3/13). We worked with several different members of the staff who were all extremely helpful and very professional, going as far as to stay late to finish the paperwork for our lease so that we could move in on time. So far they have been very good about seeing to anything we need right away. The area is well maintained and always looks nice, which is what attracted us to the place to begin with. There have been minimal problems with the apartment so far, just a few issues to work out as can be expected when you first move in. I have not had any trouble with noise, just the normal sounds of neighbors talking and passing by. I can't hear anything through the walls, just the sounds coming from outside. There is open parking with plenty of space, and the option to pay for covered parking if you want it. Overall this has been the best experience I have had with an apartment complex.
