author: mookaoman
review_text: Sierra Vista Apartments are terrible. This was my first experience living on my own, so when they rushed me through the walk through and all that, I didn't think a thing of it. We thought it looked pretty ok when we first saw it. It looked average, nothing special, but definetly not horrible. First of all, there is a huge roach problem. The roaches pretty much rule the place normally roaches are afraid of humans/light, but I have woken up in the middle of the night from roaches crawling on me. They are very used to being here. I have tried everything from roach spray, to traps, to bug bombing the place, and have been keeping it very clean. I still have bug problems, but have managed to keep it semi-tolerable. Also, weird electrical problems, I have a feeling something is screwy as far as that goes. There have been two fires in other units in the last 4 months we have lived here, one was literally two doors down. Not only that, but every time my room mate or I have tried to clean the stove, we get a mini electrical shock up our arm like one that is strong enough to make me pull away and jump across the room. Once a month or so, the water shuts off for no reason at all, no notice which can be really inconvenient if I plan to take a shower before work or school. I will call the leasing office, and they always say "They are doing maintenance , it will be about 3 hours ". Another thing, the dishwasher is crap. It doesn't wash our dishes, it sloshes soap on them and leaves soap residue. We rinse our dishes well before loading the washer. Other gross things that were noted when moving in randomly finding gobs of hair in the dishwasher, and sink, and another unidentifiable cruddy substance. I am starting to notice that all over the walls there is hair that has been painted over, in several places, in several rooms, as well as other weird chunks (painted over of course), that don't look like they are part of the kind of texture on the wall. There are a lot of neighbors who are loud and noisy, a lot of druggies that hang out here too. There are also a lot of people with loud, noisy kids. I found out from my neighbors that crackheads used to live in the unit we're currently in. Our rent is an amazing price, and our utilities (except water) are included, but it isn't worth it to live in a crappy place. The landlords here are ding dongs, this management company doesn't know how to hire people. The first main landlord was a complete jerk to us every time we told him we had an issue, and basically brushed aside all our issues, and then he was fired. This new lady is such a flake, that we had to pay our water bill a month early because she screwed up something with their account with the city of Tempe (according to the Leasing office, which they tried to blame on the post office). Point of this whole drabble is, that these guys run you around in circles and stick you with a crappy deal. They screwed us into signing a 13 month lease, because they were going to charge us $150 more per month if we decided to only sign a 6 month lease. Don't live here if you can help it. If its a must for some reason (like cost, for instance), get a unit on the side close to the leasing office, it is cleaner, better maintained, and it generally looks better. Plus the laundromat on that side costs less.

author: Euthanasia
review_title: As close to hell as you can get.
review_text:

The new management had inexperienced maintenance staff, they moved just about anyone in, cars were being vandalized, there were 9 people living in the apartment next door, and once (the walls are a thick layer of brick) I asked them to turn down their music, so I could study for a test at school, and they slashed my bicycle up.

The laundromat was dirty and in disrepair. Half the time there was no hot water, no parking, no safety from the supposed "security patrol" that no one ever saw. If you had an emergency (I consider a toilet backing up to be an emergency) at night, they told you to wait until morning.

They offered to renew our lease with a rent bonus, and we literally told them to go to hell.

They renovated each apartment to make it more modern, however the new apartments are shoddily renovated and the cabinets are falling off the walls in the kitchens.

author: Current Resident 609946
review_text: Nice place, nice grounds. But many common area things don't work. Gas grills, and gas fire rings have not worked since we moved in. They just look pretty. However, the maintenance people are great at repairing issues in your apartment. Ample parking and wide spaces. Buildings are older, but generally updated (mostly painted). Walking distance to ASU and Mill Ave. The lease amount will be more than you think. They say utilities are included, and indeed, you get electric, water, etc. through the complex, but you are billed a fixed amount for these. My rent was quoted to be $795 monthy, but it is actually $958 with the utilities included. Also, they have valet trash pickup, whereby someone gets your trash if you leave the container outside your door. It, too is "included" for $25 a month. Give me back my $25 and I will run my own trash to the dumpster. I guess when they say "included", they really mean "it's not optional".

review_text: I've only lived here about a week so its hard to really judge but so far I'm very happy here. It's very quiet, clean, everything works well and the people here seem friendly. The surrounding area is very nice and there a lot of food/drink places.

author: Current Resident 720738
review_text: Don't think twice about moving here. They charge you random charges for damages that you didn't make, and overcharge you on rent, and none of these charges can be fought. Very dangerous place to live, and expect to get all your possessions stolen. Worst apartment complex ever.

author: Current Resident 494128
review_text: My husband and I lived there 2010-2011. While we were there the maintenance did not do half of the requests, the pool was green all summer, and our laundry was stolen three times. The police were called out numerous times, and more than once on holidays neighbors would shoot guns into the air. Not the best place to start a family, for sure.

author: limeturtles
review_text: My husband and I moved in here in the beginning of December 2012 the office staff is all very helpful, friendly and welcoming. There are always maintenance issues with older buildings, but they always take care of it as soon as you make it aware. There are a lot of tenants that don't pick up after their dogs but that's pretty typical in any complex. Landscapers come weekly, haven't seen any bugs, even had the unit inspected for mold and such before we moved in, haven't had a single issue. There has been some water maintenance over the past few months, the office staff has always been EXTREMELY helpful, they even let you take a shower in one of the units across the street if need be, which being 6 months pregnant is kind of a necessity. It's a great price, happy we don't have to pay for electric and the 2 bedrooms are spacious, in fact more so than many other places we have looked at.

author: Kemary
review_text: I have been living at Sierra Vista since October of 2012. The grounds were not my personal first choice because of the older build, but there are plenty of other features that made me decide to rent a studio at these apartments. Once I saw the inside layout of my unit I was impressed at how open and comfortable the room felt.The second deciding factor for me was the amenities offered; with several well-kept pools and laundry facilities, a small but very new and updated fitness room, and the really modern styled Internet cafe I was more than impressed. The overall winning factor to the Sierra Vista apartment community is the staff. Kandis, Renee, Kelly, Bobby, Jeff, and Kim all work very well together and have done exceptionally well with making all the tenants feel welcomed and comfortable in the community. Honesty, if it wasn't for the staff here; I would rate this apartment as an average place to live. I feel like the staff (including maintenance) have done a great job of communicating with people and are great at trying to be adaptable to people's needs. If there's a problem, all you have to do is go to the office and have a quick friendly chat and they make sure to get things done in a timely manner. I am very satisfied with how I am treated and how well the staff prioritizes tenants wants and needs. I would definitely recommend Sierra Vista to a friend or two. In fact, I already have! The grounds are respectable nice, the neighborhood is great! There's a nearby park, mill ave is just a few minutes away, and there's several easy accesses to the freeway from the apartments. The only thing that is really lacking here is a close grocery store and a great hot tub!!

author: Current Resident 4996
review_text: Don't stay here. The electricity is bad, The building lights are never on nor fixed, neighbors are loud and abusive with their domestic problems. Called them in twice nothing is done. Nothing gets fixed and there is no notice once you request maintenance so you don't know if it is fixed or not and when. Not worth the cheap price nor location. Apartments next door look more welcoming for the same location. Staff in the front office is nice but nice doesn't fix things.

author: DougN
review_text: Been living in a studio here for two months. The staff is friendly and maintenance is exceptional. The first week my air conditioning unit broke and they had a new one ordered and installed within a few days. If you're looking for cheaper rent, this is the place to be. It is easy to get by here with the amenities they provide. Highly recommend!

author: Current Resident 472282
review_text: This place is gross. First of all, YES this place has ROACHES. Doesn't matter how clean you keep your place, you WILL see them. It's the biggest nuisance about living here despite the loud, obnoxious neighbors. There also doesn't seem to be any rule regulations here because nobody follows them. There are people here who walk their big dogs without leashes and dont pick up after them. People playing loud music at the firepit on weeknights past midnight. Apparently some people think they're exempt from the rules or just dont understand basic courtesy. These studios are overpriced, you will be paying at least $1k for these tiny apartments. Appliances are small, no dishwasher, sink is so small its laughable. You will be paying $20 a month for a valet service that doesn't exist. And no, theres no negotiating this even if you live right by the filthy dumpsters. Front office offers this lame "internet package" for like $40 a month when its just the PASSWORD TO THE WIFI. Internet connection sucks so I had to get my own setup. Homeless people also like to hang out here - 2 occassions where the same homeless guy got into the laundry room, acting erratic and would not leave. They also like to sleep on the hammocks overnight and leave their trash. You'll see a lot of that here since its not a gated community. The only good thing about this place is the 24hr gym and the maintenance crew. It's clear that this place was NOT renovated with the tenant in mind, just for aesthetic purposes. Please save your money and go find a nice 1 bedroom for the same price or cheaper.

Good luck with your search, but please keep looking.

author: DMS3692
review_text: I've lived here for 2 years now while in school. Honestly, I have had a great experience and very minimal issues here. The location is outstanding. I can walk or ride my bike to ASU or Mill Ave, there is plenty of beautiful landscape with a lot of grass and trees, they're very pet friendly, they are extremely fast to respond to emails and maintenance orders, I personally have not seen one cockroach since I've lived here and although the price of rent has been going up, compared to other complexes in the area it still remains one of the best priced complexes. I also like the layout of the studio. It is kinda like a one bedroom but the other room is separated by an open wall instead of a door. David S.

review_title: It used to be better, but seems to be going downhill.
review_text: * Close to Light Rail * Evap coolers need upgrading * Six legged friends don't pay rent * When I first moved here, things seemed to be a lot better - just pay your rent, be respectful of each other, handle your business, and you wouldn't hear a thing. I had a problem with the garbage disposal and it was taken care of. I am in II, and the thing that upsets me the most is the evaporative coolers will not keep up in the 105 's, get used to it being 85-90 degrees in your place, even if you try to close up doors/vents - seal the windows - replace the filter every month - or use CFL bulbs for less heat. Now the new management never has any get-togethers, try to nickel and dime you for everything they can - must have gotten a call from corporate for more profits, and put notices on your door for any reason they possibly can to charge you. I rarely ever hear my neighbors unless I have the windows open through the walls, they are solid to me and unsure of others having this problem. TLDR Pros: Free electricity Thick walls to not hear your neighbors through Close to Light Rail/everything but a grocery store Police are rarely over, not hearing gunshots every night, only the rare dispute Can pay your bill online (Although they charge $20 to do that now) Cons: Evaporative coolers do not keep up in the summertime and often go down New management tries to find ways to nickel and dime you Six legged radioactive resistant friends that don't have to pay rent

author: Current Resident 614861

My toilet has exploded, my dishwasher has broken twice, the A/C has broken too many times to count, there are holes in the wall, mold in my tub, leaky faucets, the oven doesn't work very well, etc. Half the time when I submit a work request, maintenance doesn't even come out. author: Current Resident 545979
review_title: Quiet and convenient at a reasonable price
review_text: I've lived at Sierra Vista 1 for quite a while. It's just a mile from downtown Tempe, Arizona State University and the lightrail. Most importantly to me Skyharbor International airport is just 2.5 miles away. My experience is only with Sierra Vista 1 but these apartments are reasonably priced and apart from occasional airplane noise they're generally very quiet. The grounds, laundry facility and pool are also always well maintained and there is also an internet cafe available to residents. Utilities are included in the rent which is particularly nice in the summer when Arizona makes air-conditioning a virtual necessity. The few requests for maintenance I've had, including a garbage disposal that had to be replaced, were all dealt with promptly and professionally. Despite a clean apartment the only recurring issue I've experienced over several years has been insect pests. Whenever I stop by the office the staff have always been responsive and friendly so Sierra Vista 1 is a quiet, convenient and reasonably priced place that will appeal to a wide variety of people.

author: Current Resident 533238
review_text: I've lived at these apartments on and off since 2009. The first apartment I shared with my ex-boyfriend was in Sierra Vista II, the furthest building from the leasing office. This apartment was horrible. There were consistent issues with the heating and AC units, the walls were PAPER thin (and I mean tissue paper you could hear a mouse fart next door), and there didn't seem to be a whole lot of maintenance. The rent was very reasonable but the housing seemed flimsy and poorly maintained, so this made sense. Additionally, there was something wrong with the pool so it was off limits for quite a while. Luckily I wasn't on the lease at this time and left. I moved back to Sierra Vista in July of 2010 and it's been fantastic ever since. I live on the "I" side now, and although the apartment is much smaller than I would like it is infinitely better than the garbage on the other side of the street. These buildings used to be a motel (so I hear) and the walls are virtually soundproof. I have a young puppy who tends to cry incessantly and I haven't once had a complaint from my neighbors. I have NEVER had a problem about maintenance coming to handle a problem; they even came to replace my AC unit while I was at work when it broke last summer. The lawns are beautifully maintained, the laundry room is always clean, and there's plenty of parking my only serious complaint other than the square footage are the large number of feral cats hanging around. Although the office staff is all new they are very polite and helpful. I must say, however, that since I moved in I've never been late with rent, had a noise complaint, violated rules or regulations, etc it leads me to believe that at SV if you scratch their backs they scratch yours.

author: Current Resident 556677
review_text: I rented a studio from May-November 2013. I waited to post this review until I received my deposit back, which took over a month and many, many calls to the office. This place is one of the worst apartment complexes out there. It had to have been built in the 60's. Overall apartment: Upon move-in, our entire move-in checklist was filled with problems and we had at least 35-40 urgent maintenance requests. This alerted the property manager who came to our apartment to review our requests. The work orders were put in and everything was "completed" in the next few days but nothing was repaired accordingly. The towel racks were hanging out of the wall so they extended the bars and "patched" the holes in the walls with general caulking. Are you serious The caulking was never covered with paint and was an eye sore to look at. EVERYTHING is painted over after each new tenant. This includes all the electrical plate covers, the breaker box, door/cabinet hinges, the sink stopper. Good luck trying to open/close things properly. All the cabinet door don't close right or completely, we asked for this to be fixed and maintenance refused. The cabinet door in the bathroom fell off the hinges and they just moved the hinge further down the door instead of fixing it properly. The paint in the bathroom tub starting peeling off about a month before our move-out. The toilet is so small it should belong in a daycare bathroom, and the door just barely closes past the toilet- no wonder why they couldn't have a regular sized toilet. The tub is what makes me certain this apartment was built in the 60's. It's not long enough for me (a 5'4" women) to completely stretch my legs out in. The shower liner was detaching from the wall and cracked (a moisture hazard). You can tell it was patched over with their famous general caulking but that didn't help anything. Appliances: The same stove has been in the apartment since it was built because it is impossible to even pull completely out from the counter. It was FILTHY underneath and behind, and the cleaning lady said nothing could be done because it can't be moved. E !! The knobs on the range never worked. We had to use pliers to turn off the knobs. The oven constantly burned our food because it was far too old to properly function. The vent above the stove never functioned and the fan was stuck on for about an hour our first night because we couldn't turn it off. There is no microwave and no place to put one on the counter if you buy one. We constantly were moving our small appliances off the counter just to do dishes, in the very small sink. Flooring: Don't let them fool you if they say you will have "wood" flooring in your apartment. It is the cheapest linoleum there is and was coming up by the time we left, but they told us it was new. The carpet is awfully warn out and stained. It is well past needing to be replaced. Our feet were dirty after walking on it every night until we took the money to clean it, I guess it was our responsibility to clean it?? Lighting: There is one light in the living area and it doesn't provide even adequate light. Be prepared to buy some lamps. The fan was practically coming out of the ceiling when we moved in and it was tightened by maintenance. The fan blades have been painted on and never cleaned. The fan in the bathroom sounded like a lawnmower and we ended up just unplugging it after maintenance put in a "new" one that was even worse. Safety/noise: Our neighbor was definitely dealing drugs out of his apartment and he always allowed his visitors to stand outside our apartment and smoke. Which was nice since it came through our A/C unit and made our whole apartment reek. We were asked on multiple occasions for money from his "guests". He also busted his window out and the management has allowed it to remain that way for over a month. I wonder how long they'll let that continue. The parking is not well lit and the lights were completely out for about 2 weeks on our building and the buildings around us. We lived next to the stairs on the first floor and the dishes in the cabinets would rattle when someone walked up or down the stairs. The police and fire sirens are constantly going off at all hours of the day. The windows are single paned and have a very simple latch to close that could have easily been broken into. We asked for a more security and they gave us another small screw device that goes on the track of the window. Because that's going to stop a whole lot.. Office staff: Oh my The office staff had a turnover rate of about two weeks and someone new would be there every time I went into the office. The people working there would speak Spanish to each other when talking about what I was asking them, which I found incredibly rude and inconsiderate. I think some of them just honestly didn't know English. When I would get a package, no one in the office had the intelligence to be able to find it and I would always have to point it out from across the room. I finally was done dealing with them and would just go pick it out of the pile myself. Maintenance requests were never entered into the system correctly or with enough detail for the maintenance staff to handle the request correctly. One of us always had to be at the apartment for the repairs to explain. But it didn't matter, the requests weren't completed properly, just enough to regain minimal function regardless of how it looked in the end. Amenities: What amenities? You'll see on the website beautiful landscaping and pools. The main pool was green, as in it looked like a lake, for almost a month in the middle of the summer. It takes that long to get a pool's water back to normal? How about drain it and start over at that point? They never did.. We were given the key to the pool across the road (how convenient!) which was full of bugs, leaves, dirt and kids that weren't with their parents (that is the 2 bedroom side of the complex). We didn't swim in any pool after that. There is a fitness center smaller than the studio and I didn't want to pay for a key to use it. The onsite laundry facilities were filthy and expensive to use. You had to pay a deposit on a card and then load the card during business hours, which was very inconvenient. There is also an "Internet cafe" with a coffee machine that is always turned off. The printer doesn't work and if you want anything printed off you must email it to the manager who prints it off in the office (nothing like a little privacy, right??). There is no landscaping unless you count dirt where there used to be grass. The bushes are all overgrown and there is trash thrown down next to them. The pros: There are a few.. Our electric was covered under the rent so we could use as much as we wanted, and we sure did take advantage of it! The water is billed based on how many people live in the apartment, not on usage, so again we took advantage of that. We were always able to park right outside our apartment. We never had a big issue with bugs even though they never sprayed the inside of the apartment. I've been waiting a very long time to write this review. I don't want anyone else to get suckered into this apartment like we were. We were way too naive when we moved in here. Please always look at the apartment you are going to be living in before moving in. The models always look better and that's an understatement in this case. I am so happy to be out of here. Please stay away from this place. There are so many better apartments in Tempe for the price.

author: Current Resident 566019
review_title: If you can afford better, then STAY AWAY!
review_text: My boyfriend and I have been living here for a little over a year. We came here initially because the rent was so cheap - we got a two bedroom apartment for $575/mo, with electricity included. It sounded like a fantastic deal until I realized that we are getting what we paid for. Here is a short list of the problems with this complex: 1. First and foremost, the NOISE! I'm not sure if the walls are made out of cardboard or some other equally cheap/noise-conducive material, but we hear EVERYTHING! Planes flying in and out of Sky Harbor at pretty much all hours, trains blasting their whistles in the middle of the night, drunk people hanging out in the greenbelt area shouting, neighbors screaming at each other and their kids . . we've experimented with various combos of bed placement/ear plugs to mitigate the noise and its still terrible. 2. Plumbing issues. There is currently a river of sewage right outside my apartment, and our water has been shut off intermittently at various points over the last couple of weeks. There is nothing more fun than waking up and realizing that you can't even shower or brush your teeth before work. I've tried calling the maintenance phone number, only to get blown off and ignored, so today I finally called the front office to complain, only to be told that I "should be relieved my electricity is still working" because lots of residents have had both their electricity AND water shut off due to maintenance problems. What a reassuring thing to hear from the front office! Let me be clear here - this is NOT a one-time plumbing emergency. We have had our water shut off three times during the day in the last two weeks, and who knows how many other times it was shut off while we weren't at home. There seem to be broken pipes constantly, since that's the excuse the front office and maintenance people give to explain both the water shut-offs and the river of sewage right outside my apartment. 3. Other residents - let's just say the neighbors are colorful. Fortunately, two of the worst (a drug dealer and an abusive mom who screamed at her children at all hours of the night) have moved out or have been evicted recently. Still, it's not at all surprising to see police cars here constantly. If you can afford better, DO NOT LIVE HERE! I cannot wait until our lease is up!

author: Current Resident 412355
review_text: I would just like to finally take the time to say something. The past year living at Sierra Vista has been in one word, miserable. I take pride in being a very calm, thoughtful and understanding individual and I have been nothing but that until now. The water situation as of lately has been hard to handle. We (myself and my family) went over three weeks without hot water. We didn't even have warm water and on top of that there were days where we went extended periods of time without ANY water. One of the days was almost 12 hours! As a parent, it was hard trying to explain to my three year old why she couldn't take a bath before bedtime. Even then, I was still always friendly with the staff. Shortly after, my fridge started leaking. I went in the office to give my 60 days notice to vacate and while I was there I inquired about what could be done about my fridge that was leaking. The woman I spoke with (she was very friendly, I don't blame her) told me someone would be out to my unit right away to repair it. She said the absolute longest I should expect to wait would be 24 hours. A week and a half went by and no one came or tried to contact me. After that, I received an email explaining that maintainence had entered my apartment while I was gone to perform repairs. Under actions completed the email was blank. Which I guess was true, because it looked like nothing had been touched at all! By this time, the whole idea of expecting any sort of professionalism from Sierra Vista management had become a joke. Me and some of the other residents and my friends as well had joked about how with no hot water, management would organize "community bum showers" in one of the few units that had hot water. Shortly after that, they had posted something on their Facebook offering empty units for hot showers. At least I got some comical relief out of that. And no, I did not shower in an empty unit. I am currently living in a three bedroom one bath unit and I pay 745 a month. When I signed that lease I thought I had landed a sweet deal but after living here I have learned the valuable lesson " you get what you pay for." And not even, because I pay for hot water and still don't get it. Not only that, now they are asking me to stay and up my rent by a nice chunk of money. Month to month would have been well over 1200 dollars! What a joke. I am moving out in less than a month and I could not be happier. Me and my family are literally counting down the days. 24 more to go! Lastly but certainly not least, my lease was signed on February 26th for a 12 month lease. I put my notice to vacate in on December 10th, well ahead of the 60 day time frame. They told me I was 4 days late. I showed them my lease and explained to them how the only thing I had been told was that I need to put in 60 days before February 26th. I even had all my documents to back it up and NOWHERE did any paperwork say ANYTHING about February 6th. They said it didn't matter what my lease said, it only matter what the computer said. Now, I am being forced to pay the prorated rent off of some crazy amount of 1200 and something dollars. Oh and by the way, during all of this there has been an ugly gross hole in front of my apartment! They just covered it with dirt a few days ago after it being there for more than a month. This is what it looked like!
response_text: We are disappointed to hear that your stay with us has not been to your satisfaction. If you have any additional comments or suggestions of how we may improve your experience with us, please email our Cares Team at feedback@trinity-pm.com.

author: Yratilos
review_text:
With so many great places in the Tempe, and surrounding area, why would you want to live here!?!

Yes, I know the rent is reasonable, (that is the ONLY reason that I still live here) but the living conditions are horrid. The staff is, ok, as long as you have MONEY for them, they don't complain much.

I moved here from California, (god i miss home) to attend school. Unfortunately, with such a short notice on my start date for my classes, I had to accept the apartment sight-unseen. I was promised by Josh, who was on of the office "personnel" at the time, that I qualified for a $51 dollar move in special, only to arrive at the complex and find out that Josh NEVER ran the qualification process and I was told that I had to fork over an extra $300 dollars to move in.

In all fairness, the management staff is decent, that is if you can keep them around long enough to get to see them, I can't even count how many different managers this place has gone through since we have been residents. They will, however, work with you a little if your going to be a little late for rent, as long as you can get it taken care of by the 9th of the month, (thats when they take people to court) and pay additional fees of:

$20.00 Late notice delivery fee
$25.00 Promise to pay agreement fee
$20.00 "Insert payment reason here" fee
$ 5.00 Late fee per day

So, if you have an extra $50.00 to $100.00 just laying around no big deal right?

I have not had to deal with maintenance much due to my experience as a hotel manager / maintenance chief. I do think that the maintenance crew around here is lacking either the experience, knowledge, or both to be able to do an effective job.

The apartments are beyond small, and almost everything has had to be repaired or replaced. The toilet is constantly overflowing and there is no water pressure in the shower. I really hate the fact that in the air conditioning/heating unit has to be switched every season and you can never have both of them working at the same time. The parking lot seems like a good place for drug busts, there is no telling how many drug related transaction myself or my family have seen take place, and domestic violence appears to be a favored pastime around here.

o yeah, I have had shots fired outside my apartment while the cops were hear dealing with a different domestic violence situation the cops never found the shooter.

And make sure that you never, ever, under any circumstances have a package that is too large for your mailbox to, and has to be delivered to the office. They kept my laptop down in the office for well over 2 weeks without notification

In all honesty and fairness, please just save yourself the time and aggravation. Look somewhere else

author: Current Resident 504
review_title: Terrible living environment, do NOT move here
review_text: I've lived here for 3 months now and it has been the worst experience of my life. Maintenance is not very helpful at all, and not even a flooded apartment is considered an emergency. I called on a Sunday with a terrible leaking pipe that flooded the whole bathroom. "Put a bucket under the leak until tomorrow" was their response. Appliances do not work correctly. 2 police reports have been filed in 3 months. 2 friends and I walked to a gas station and were jumped and beaten in front of the apartment complex. Then 2 months later (on Christmas day) a man broke into and attempted to steal my car. They refuse to hire security. Management does nothing to help this situation unless I want to pay almost $1, to break the lease. They may transfer us to Parkside Apts. but from reading reviews, it doesn't look much safer at all. I shouldn't have to be scared to go outside in the middle of the day and I shouldn't have to cross my fingers that my car will be there in the morning. Ridiculous! Do not move here!
